heading_en: What have universally been the beginnings of any city, and what was that of Rome
thesis: Rome's free origin and the laws imposed by its founders explain how so much virtue was maintained there for centuries and how its empire arose.
thesis_quote: Coloro che leggeranno quale principio fusse quello della città di Roma, e da quali latori di leggi e come ordinato, non si maraviglieranno che tanta virtù si sia per più secoli mantenuta in quella città

propositions.statement: All cities are founded either by men native to the place or by foreigners.
propositions.quote: dico che tutte le cittadi sono edificate o dagli uomini natii del luogo dove le si edificano o dai forestieri

propositions.statement: Men act either from necessity or from choice, and there is greater virtue where choice has less authority.
propositions.quote: perché gli uomini operono o per necessità o per elezione; e perché si vede quivi essere maggior virtù dove la elezione ha meno autorità

propositions.statement: It is the more prudent choice to found a city in a fertile place, provided laws constrain the idleness that fertility would otherwise breed.
propositions.quote: Dico, adunque, essere più prudente elezione porsi in luogo fertile, quando quella fertilità con le leggi infra i debiti termini si ristringa

episodes.description: Athens was founded under the authority of Theseus by dispersed inhabitants gathering for security.
episodes.quote: La prima, sotto l’autorità di Teseo, fu per simili cagioni dagli abitatori dispersi edificata

episodes.description: Venice was founded by peoples who took refuge on Adriatic islets fleeing the barbarian wars after the decline of the Roman empire.
episodes.quote: sendosi molti popoli ridotti in certe isolette che erano nella punta del mare Adriatico, per fuggire quelle guerre

episodes.description: Alexander rejected Dinocrates' plan to build a city on Mount Athos because it could not feed itself, and founded Alexandria instead.
episodes.quote: venne Dinocrate architetto, e gli mostrò come e’ la poteva edificare sopra il monte Atho

episodes.description: Florence was founded under the Roman empire, either by Sulla's soldiers or by inhabitants of the hills of Fiesole, and so lacked a free origin.
episodes.quote: Simile a queste fu l’edificazione di Firenze, perché (o edificata da’ soldati di Silla, o, a caso, dagli abitatori dei monti di Fiesole

episodes.description: Moses occupied cities found in conquered lands, while Aeneas built a new city, exemplifying free founders.
episodes.quote: questi tali, o egli abitano le cittadi che e’ truovono ne’ paesi ch’egli acquistano, come fe’ Moises; o e’ ne edificano di nuovo, come fe’ Enea

episodes.description: The kingdom of Egypt, though in a most pleasant country, produced excellent men because its laws imposed necessity of exertion.
episodes.quote: Intra i quali fu il regno degli Egizi, che, non ostante che il paese sia amenissimo, tanto potette quella necessità, ordinata dalle leggi, che ne nacque uomini eccellentissimi

episodes.description: The Sultan's kingdom and the Mamluk military order, before Selim the Great Turk destroyed it, used strict laws to counter the idleness bred by a rich country.
episodes.quote: E chi avesse considerato il regno del Soldano, e l’ordine de’ Mammalucchi e di quella loro milizia, avanti che da Salì, Gran Turco, fusse stata spenta

episodes.description: Ragusa stands as an example of a city built in a sterile place whose poverty keeps its people united and industrious.
episodes.quote: come interviene in Raugia, e in molte altre cittadi in simili luoghi edificate

episodes.description: Rome, whether traced to Aeneas as foreigner or Romulus as native, had a free beginning and was constrained by the laws of Romulus, Numa, and others.
episodes.quote: Chi esaminerà, adunque, la edificazione di Roma, se si prenderà Enea per suo primo progenitore

notes: Chapter closes by announcing the plan of Book I: discourses on Rome's public internal deliberations as celebrated by Livy.

heading_en: Of how many kinds republics are, and of which kind the Roman republic was
thesis: A mixed constitution combining principality, aristocracy, and popular government is the firmest, and Rome attained it by accident through the disunion of plebs and senate.
thesis_quote: ne elessero uno che participasse di tutti, giudicandolo più fermo e più stabile; perché l’uno guarda l’altro, sendo in una medesima città il Principato, gli Ottimati, e il Governo Popolare

propositions.statement: Each of the three good forms of government slides easily into its corrupt counterpart.
propositions.quote: perché il Principato facilmente diventa tirannico; gli Ottimati con facilità diventano stato di pochi; il Popolare sanza difficultà in licenzioso si converte

propositions.statement: All republics revolve through a cycle of governmental forms, though few survive its repeated turns.
propositions.quote: E questo è il cerchio nel quale girando tutte le republiche si sono governate e si governano

propositions.statement: Many men never agree to a new law establishing a new order unless necessity, which always carries danger, shows them it must be done.
propositions.quote: gli assai uomini non si accordano mai ad una legge nuova che riguardi uno nuovo ordine nella città se non è mostro loro da una necessità che bisogni farlo

propositions.statement: What no single orderer did for Rome was done by chance, through the accidents arising from the disunion of plebs and senate.
propositions.quote: furo tanti gli accidenti che in quella nacquero, per la disunione che era intra la Plebe ed il Senato, che quello che non aveva fatto uno ordinatore, lo fece il caso

episodes.description: Lycurgus gave Sparta laws distributing power among kings, aristocrats, and people, creating a state that lasted more than eight hundred years.
episodes.quote: ordinò in modo le sue leggi in Sparta, che, dando le parti sue ai Re, agli Ottimati e al Popolo, fece uno stato che durò più che ottocento anni

episodes.description: Solon ordered Athens as a purely popular state, which proved so short-lived that he saw Pisistratus' tyranny arise before his death.
episodes.quote: per ordinarvi solo lo stato popolare, lo fece di sì breve vita, che, avanti morisse, vi vide nata la tirannide di Pisistrato

episodes.description: The republic of Florence was reordered by the accident of Arezzo in 1502 and disordered by that of Prato in 1512.
episodes.quote: la republica di Firenze, la quale fu dallo accidente d’Arezzo, nel dua, riordinata; e da quel di Prato, nel dodici, disordinata

episodes.description: Those who expelled the Tarquins immediately created two consuls in the kings' place, expelling the name but not the power of royalty.
episodes.quote: quelli che li cacciarono, ordinandovi subito due Consoli che stessono nel luogo de’ Re, vennero a cacciare di Roma il nome, e non la potestà regia

episodes.description: The people rose against the insolent nobility, forcing the creation of the tribunes of the plebs, which stabilized the republic by giving all three forms their share.
episodes.quote: E così nacque la creazione de’ Tribuni della plebe, dopo la quale creazione venne a essere più stabilito lo stato di quella republica

notes: The six-forms typology and the cycle of constitutions follow Polybius, unnamed as 'alcuni altri... più savi'.

heading_en: What accidents caused the creation of the tribunes of the plebs in Rome, which made that republic more perfect
thesis: Since a lawgiver must presuppose all men wicked, the nobles' insolence once fear of the Tarquins vanished made the creation of the tribunes necessary and perfected the republic.
thesis_quote: è necessario a chi dispone una republica, ed ordina leggi in quella, presupporre tutti gli uomini rei, e che li abbiano sempre a usare la malignità dello animo loro, qualunque volta ne abbiano libera occasione

propositions.statement: Men never do anything good except by necessity; where choice abounds and license is possible, everything fills with confusion and disorder.
propositions.quote: gli uomini non operono mai nulla bene, se non per necessità; ma, dove la elezione abonda, e che vi si può usare licenza, si riempie subito ogni cosa di confusione e di disordine

propositions.statement: Hunger and poverty make men industrious, and laws make them good.
propositions.quote: la fame e la povertà fa gli uomini industriosi, e le leggi gli fanno buoni

propositions.statement: Where a good custom is lacking, law immediately becomes necessary.
propositions.quote: quando quella buona consuetudine manca, è subito la legge necessaria

episodes.description: Once the Tarquins were dead and the nobles' fear gone, the nobility spat out against the plebs the venom it had held in its breast.
episodes.quote: come prima ei furono morti i Tarquinii, e che ai Nobili fu la paura fuggita, cominciarono a sputare contro alla Plebe quel veleno che si avevano tenuto nel petto

episodes.description: After confusions, uproars, and dangers of scandal between plebs and nobility, the tribunes were created for the security of the plebs.
episodes.quote: si venne, per sicurtà della Plebe, alla creazione de’ Tribuni; e quelli ordinarono con tante preminenzie e tanta riputazione

heading_en: That the disunion of the plebs and the Roman senate made that republic free and powerful
thesis: The tumults between nobles and plebs, far from being harmful, were the first cause of Rome's liberty, since they produced laws and orders favorable to public freedom.
thesis_quote: coloro che dannono i tumulti intra i Nobili e la Plebe, mi pare che biasimino quelle cose che furono prima causa del tenere libera Roma

propositions.statement: Every republic contains two diverse humors, that of the people and that of the great, and all laws made in favor of liberty arise from their disunion.
propositions.quote: e’ sono in ogni republica due umori diversi, quello del popolo, e quello de’ grandi; e come tutte le leggi che si fanno in favore della libertà, nascano dalla disunione loro

propositions.statement: Good examples arise from good education, good education from good laws, and good laws from the very tumults many inconsiderately condemn.
propositions.quote: li buoni esempli nascano dalla buona educazione, la buona educazione, dalle buone leggi; e le buone leggi, da quelli tumulti che molti inconsideratamente dannano

propositions.statement: The desires of free peoples are rarely pernicious to liberty, because they arise from being oppressed or from fear of oppression.
propositions.quote: E i desiderii de’ popoli liberi rade volte sono perniziosi alla libertà, perché e’ nascono, o da essere oppressi, o da suspizione di avere ad essere oppressi

propositions.statement: Every city should have ordered ways through which the people can vent its ambition.
propositions.quote: ogni città debbe avere i suoi modi con i quali il popolo possa sfogare l’ambizione sua

episodes.description: From the Tarquins to the Gracchi, more than three hundred years, Rome's tumults rarely produced exile and most rarely blood.
episodes.quote: da’ Tarquinii ai Gracchi, che furano più di trecento anni, i tumulti di Roma rade volte partorivano esilio e radissime sangue

notes: Cites Cicero ('come dice Tullio') on the people's capacity for truth when told it by a trustworthy man.

heading_en: Where the guard of liberty may be more safely placed, in the people or in the great; and which has greater cause for tumult, he who wishes to acquire or he who wishes to maintain
thesis: The guard of liberty is best placed with those who have less appetite to usurp it; for a republic that would expand like Rome, that means the people.
thesis_quote: e’ si debbe mettere in guardia coloro d’una cosa, che hanno meno appetito di usurparla

propositions.statement: The nobles have a great desire to dominate while the people desire only not to be dominated.
propositions.quote: si vedrà in quelli desiderio grande di dominare, ed in questi solo desiderio di non essere dominati

propositions.statement: A republic that would build an empire must do everything as Rome did; one content to maintain itself may imitate Venice and Sparta.
propositions.quote: o tu ragioni d’una republica che voglia fare uno imperio, come Roma; o d’una che le basti mantenersi. Nel primo caso, gli è necessario fare ogni cosa come Roma

propositions.statement: Tumults are most often caused by those who possess, since the fear of losing breeds the same desires as the wish to acquire.
propositions.quote: il più delle volte sono causati da chi possiede, perché la paura del perdere genera in loro le medesime voglie che sono in quelli che desiderano acquistare

episodes.description: Sparta placed the guard of liberty in the hands of its nobles, and its liberty, like Venice's, lasted longer than Rome's.
episodes.quote: se si esaminasse il fine loro, si piglierebbe la parte de’ Nobili, per avere avuta la libertà di Sparta e di Vinegia più lunga vita che quella di Roma

episodes.description: In Machiavelli's own times Venice likewise entrusted the guard of liberty to its nobles.
episodes.quote: ne’ nostri tempi, appresso de’ Viniziani, la è stata messa nelle mani de’ Nobili

episodes.description: The Roman plebs, through the tribunes, demanded both consulships, then the censorship, praetorship, and all offices, finally idolizing men able to beat the nobility, whence came Marius' power and Rome's ruin.
episodes.quote: non bastò loro avere un Consolo plebeio, che gli vollono avere ambedue. Da questo, ei vollono la Censura, il Pretore, e tutti gli altri gradi dell’imperio della città

episodes.description: The plebeians Marcus Menenius, made dictator, and Marcus Fulvius, master of horse, investigated conspiracies hatched at Capua against Rome and ambition in Rome itself, whereupon the nobles accused the dictator, who resigned and was acquitted by the people.
episodes.quote: sendo creato Marco Menenio Dittatore, e Marco Fulvio Maestro de’ cavagli, tutti a due plebei, per ricercare certe congiure che si erano fatte in Capova contro a Roma

notes: Livy 9.26 names the dictator C. Maenius; Machiavelli calls him Marco Menenio.

heading_en: Whether in Rome a government could have been ordered that would have removed the enmities between the people and the senate
thesis: Rome could not have removed the causes of its tumults without also removing the causes of its expansion, so the enmities must be tolerated as a necessary inconvenience of Roman greatness.
thesis_quote: volendo Roma levare le cagioni de’ tumulti, levava ancora le cagioni dello ampliare

propositions.statement: In all human affairs one inconvenience can never be removed without another arising.
propositions.quote: che non si può mai cancellare uno inconveniente, che non ne surga un altro

propositions.statement: In every deliberation one should consider where the fewest inconveniences lie and take that as the better course.
propositions.quote: in ogni nostra diliberazione si debbe considerare dove sono meno inconvenienti, e pigliare quello per migliore partito

propositions.statement: All human things are in motion and must rise or fall, and necessity leads where reason does not.
propositions.quote: sendo tutte le cose degli uomini in moto, e non potendo stare salde, conviene che le salghino o che le scendino; e a molte cose che la ragione non t’induce, t’induce la necessità

propositions.statement: Without a great number of well-armed men a republic can never grow, or if it grows, maintain itself.
propositions.quote: sanza gran numero di uomini, e bene armati, mai una republica potrà crescere, o, se la crescerà, mantenersi

episodes.description: Venice closed admission to its governing councils to later arrivals, dividing Gentiluomini from Popolani without tumult.
episodes.quote: chiusero la via a tutti quelli altri che vi venissono ad abitare di nuovo, di potere convenire ne’ loro governi

episodes.description: Lycurgus' laws gave Sparta more equality of property and less equality of rank, and its kings kept the plebs defended from injury, so the city lived long united.
episodes.quote: Perché Licurgo con le sue leggi fece in Sparta più equalità di sustanze, e meno equalità di grado

episodes.description: After subjecting nearly all Greece, Sparta's weak foundation was exposed when Thebes rebelled under Pelopidas and the other cities followed, ruining the republic.
episodes.quote: seguita la ribellione di Tebe, causata da Pelopida, ribellandosi l’altre cittadi, rovinò al tutto quella republica

episodes.description: Venice, having occupied much of Italy mostly by money and cunning rather than war, lost everything in a single day when its forces were put to the test.
episodes.quote: Similmente Vinegia, avendo occupato gran parte d’Italia, e la maggiore parte non con guerra ma con danari e con astuzia

notes: Venice's one-day loss alludes to the battle of Agnadello (1509).

heading_en: How necessary accusations are in a republic to maintain its liberty
thesis: The power of publicly accusing citizens gives the humors that agitate a city a lawful outlet, without which men resort to extraordinary means that ruin the republic.
thesis_quote: non è cosa che faccia tanto stabile e ferma una republica, quanto ordinare quella in modo che l’alterazione di quegli omori che l’agitano, abbia una via da sfogarsi ordinata dalle leggi

propositions.statement: Fear of being accused deters citizens from attempting anything against the state, and if they attempt it they are promptly crushed.
propositions.quote: Il primo è che i cittadini, per paura di non essere accusati, non tentano cose contro allo stato; e tentandole, sono, incontinente e sanza rispetto, oppressi

propositions.statement: When ordinary modes of venting humors are absent, men turn to extraordinary ones, which produce far worse effects.
propositions.quote: quando questi modi ordinari non vi siano, si ricorre agli straordinari; e sanza dubbio questi fanno molto peggiori effetti che non fanno quelli

propositions.statement: Private offense generates fear, fear seeks defense, defense procures partisans, partisans create factions, and factions ruin cities.
propositions.quote: ne nasceva offesa da privati a privati, la quale offesa genera paura; la paura cerca difesa; per la difesa si procacciano partigiani; da’ partigiani nascono le parti nelle cittadi, dalle parti la rovina di quelle

propositions.statement: Whenever foreign forces are called in by a party of citizens, it may be believed to arise from the city's bad orders.
propositions.quote: qualunque volta si vede che le forze estranee siano chiamate da una parte di uomini che vivono in una città, si può credere nasca da’ cattivi ordini di quella

episodes.description: Coriolanus, enemy of the popular faction, advised starving the plebs to strip the tribunes' authority, and only the tribunes' formal citation saved him from being killed by the mob.
episodes.quote: Coriolano, inimico alla fazione popolare, consigliò come egli era venuto il tempo da potere gastigare la Plebe

episodes.description: In Florence, with no ordinary way to resist Francesco Valori's quasi-princely power, his opponents resorted to extraordinary means and the affair ended in arms and the ruin of many citizens.
episodes.quote: come accadde ne’ tempi che Francesco Valori era come principe della città

episodes.description: The fall of Piero Soderini followed from Florence's lack of any mode of accusation against the ambition of powerful citizens, which brought in the Spanish army.
episodes.quote: l’accidente seguito pur in Firenze sopra Piero Soderini, il quale al tutto seguì per non essere in quella republica alcuno modo di accuse contro alla ambizione de’ potenti cittadini

episodes.description: Arruns of Clusium, unable to avenge his sister's violation by a Lucumo through civic means, brought the Gauls into Italy against his own city.
episodes.quote: sendo stato in Chiusi, città in quelli tempi nobilissima in Toscana, da uno Lucumone violata una sorella di Arunte

heading_en: As much as accusations are useful to republics, so much are calumnies pernicious
thesis: Calumnies, which need no proof, corrupt republics; the remedy is to open ample channels for formal accusations and punish calumniators severely.
thesis_quote: quanto le accuse giovano alle republiche, tanto le calunnie nuocono

propositions.statement: Calumnies need neither witness nor corroboration, so anyone can be calumniated by anyone, whereas accusations require true proofs.
propositions.quote: le calunnie non hanno bisogno né di testimone né di alcuno altro particulare riscontro a provarle, in modo che ciascuno e da ciascuno può essere calunniato

propositions.statement: An orderer of a republic should make every citizen accusable without fear, and then punish calumniators harshly.
propositions.quote: un ordinatore d’una republica debbe ordinare che si possa in quella accusare ogni cittadino, sanza alcuna paura o sanza alcuno rispetto; e fatto questo, e bene osservato, debbe punire acremente i calunniatori

propositions.statement: Calumnies irritate rather than punish citizens, and the irritated, hating rather than fearing what is said against them, seek to avenge themselves.
propositions.quote: le calunnie irritano, e non castigano i cittadini; e gli irritati pensano di valersi, odiando più presto, che temendo, le cose che si dicano contro a loro

episodes.description: After Camillus freed Rome from the oppression of the Gauls, all citizens deferred to him without feeling loss of rank.
episodes.quote: la virtù di Furio Cammillo, poi ch’egli ebbe libera Roma dalla oppressione de’ Franciosi

episodes.description: Manlius Capitolinus, envious of Camillus' glory, calumniated the nobles over the Gallic treasure before the plebs, and the dictator, when Manlius could produce no particulars, had him imprisoned.
episodes.quote: Manlio Capitolino non poteva sopportare che gli fusse attribuito tanto onore e tanta gloria

episodes.description: Giovanni Guicciardini, Florentine commissary at the siege of Lucca, was calumniated as corrupted by the Lucchese and could never clear himself, breeding resentments that contributed to the republic's ruin.
episodes.quote: Era lo esercito fiorentino a campo a Lucca, comandato da messer Giovanni Guicciardini, commessario di quello

heading_en: That it is necessary to be alone if one wishes to order a republic anew or to reform it entirely outside its ancient orders
thesis: A republic or kingdom is well ordered only by one man alone, so Romulus deserves excuse rather than blame for the deaths of Remus and Titus Tatius, since his end was the common good.
thesis_quote: mai o rado occorre che alcuna republica o regno sia, da principio, ordinato bene, o al tutto di nuovo, fuora degli ordini vecchi, riformato, se non è ordinato da uno

propositions.statement: When the deed accuses a founder, the effect excuses him; when the effect is good, as Romulus' was, it will always excuse him.
propositions.quote: Conviene bene, che, accusandolo il fatto, lo effetto lo scusi; e quando sia buono, come quello di Romolo, sempre lo scuserà

propositions.statement: The prudent founder must not leave his seized authority as an inheritance, since men are more prone to evil than to good.
propositions.quote: Debbi bene in tanto essere prudente e virtuoso, che quella autorità che si ha presa non la lasci ereditaria a un altro

propositions.statement: Ordering is the work of one man, but an order endures only when its maintenance rests with many.
propositions.quote: se uno è atto a ordinare, non è la cosa ordinata per durare molto, quando la rimanga sopra le spalle d’uno; ma sì bene, quando la rimane alla cura di molti

episodes.description: Romulus killed his brother Remus and consented to the death of Titus Tatius, yet immediately ordered a Senate, showing he acted for the common good.
episodes.quote: uno fondatore d’un vivere civile, quale fu Romolo, abbia prima morto un suo fratello, dipoi consentito alla morte di Tito Tazio Sabino

episodes.description: When Rome became free after the expulsion of the Tarquins, no ancient order was changed except two annual consuls in place of a perpetual king.
episodes.quote: quando Roma divenne libera per la cacciata de’ Tarquini, dove da’ Romani non fu innovato alcun ordine dello antico

episodes.description: Moses, Lycurgus, Solon, and other founders of kingdoms and republics could form laws for the common good only because they took sole authority.
episodes.quote: come Moises, Licurgo, Solone, ed altri fondatori di regni e di republiche

episodes.description: Agis of Sparta was killed by the ephors for trying to restore Lycurgus' laws; Cleomenes, learning from his writings, killed the ephors, renewed the laws alone, but was overcome by Macedonian power.
episodes.quote: desiderando Agide re di Sparta ridurre gli Spartani intra quelli termini che le leggi di Licurgo gli avevano rinchiusi

heading_en: As much as the founders of a republic or kingdom are praiseworthy, so much are the founders of a tyranny vituperable
thesis: Founders of religions and well-ordered states win the highest praise and security, while founders of tyranny like Caesar earn infamy, as the contrast between Rome's adoptive and hereditary emperors demonstrates.
thesis_quote: Intra tutti gli uomini laudati sono i laudatissimi quelli che sono stati capi e ordinatori delle religioni. Appresso, dipoi, quelli che hanno fondato o republiche o regni

propositions.statement: Though all men praise virtue and blame tyranny in the abstract, almost all, deceived by a false good and a false glory, slide into the ranks of those deserving blame.
propositions.quote: quasi tutti, ingannati da uno falso bene e da una falsa gloria, si lasciono andare, o voluntariamente o ignorantemente, nei gradi di coloro che meritano più biasimo che laude

propositions.statement: All emperors who succeeded by heredity except Titus were bad, and all who succeeded by adoption were good, as the five from Nerva to Marcus show.
propositions.quote: tutti gl’imperadori che succederono all’imperio per eredità, eccetto Tito, furono cattivi, quelli che per adozione, furono tutti buoni come furono quei cinque da Nerva a Marco

propositions.statement: A prince seeking worldly glory should wish to possess a corrupt city, not to ruin it wholly like Caesar but to reorder it like Romulus.
propositions.quote: doverrebbe desiderare di possedere una città corrotta, non per guastarla in tutto come Cesare, ma per riordinarla come Romolo

episodes.description: Caesar, founder of Rome's tyranny, is celebrated only because writers were corrupted by his fortune; free writers blame him through Catiline and praise his enemy Brutus.
episodes.quote: Né sia alcuno che s’inganni, per la gloria di Cesare, sentendolo, massime, celebrare dagli scrittori

episodes.description: Of the twenty-six emperors from Caesar to Maximinus sixteen were killed; the good adoptive emperors from Nerva to Marcus lived secure while Caligula, Nero, and Vitellius could not be saved by their armies.
episodes.quote: di ventisei imperadori che furono da Cesare a Massimino, sedici ne furono ammazzati, dieci morirono ordinariamente

episodes.description: Greek exempla contrast good princes such as Agesilaus, Timoleon, and Dion with tyrants such as Nabis, Phalaris, and Dionysius.
episodes.quote: più tosto Agesilai, Timoleoni, Dioni, che Nabidi, Falari e Dionisii

heading_en: Of the religion of the Romans
thesis: The religion introduced by Numa was among the first causes of Rome's felicity, for it produced good orders, good fortune, and success in every enterprise.
thesis_quote: conchiudo che la religione introdotta da Numa fu intra le prime cagioni della felicità di quella città: perché quella causò buoni ordini; i buoni ordini fanno buona fortuna; e dalla buona fortuna nacquero i felici successi delle imprese

propositions.statement: Where there is religion arms are easily introduced, but where there are arms without religion, religion is introduced only with difficulty.
propositions.quote: dove è religione, facilmente si possono introdurre l’armi e dove sono l’armi e non religione, con difficultà si può introdurre quella

propositions.statement: No lawgiver of extraordinary laws ever failed to have recourse to God, for otherwise the laws would not be accepted.
propositions.quote: mai fu alcuno ordinatore di leggi straordinarie in uno popolo che non ricorresse a Dio; perché altrimente non sarebbero accettate

propositions.statement: The health of a republic lies not in having a prince who governs prudently while he lives, but one who orders it so that it maintains itself after his death.
propositions.quote: Non è, adunque, la salute di una republica o d’uno regno avere uno principe che prudentemente governi mentre vive; ma uno che l’ordini in modo, che, morendo ancora, la si mantenga

propositions.statement: Observance of divine worship causes the greatness of republics, and its contempt causes their ruin.
propositions.quote: come la osservanza del culto divino è cagione della grandezza delle republiche, così il dispregio di quello è cagione della rovina d’esse

episodes.description: The Senate elected Numa Pompilius as Romulus' successor, and he turned to religion to reduce a ferocious people to civil obedience.
episodes.quote: inspirarono nel petto del Senato romano di eleggere Numa Pompilio per successore a Romolo

episodes.description: After Cannae, Scipio with drawn sword forced the citizens who planned to abandon Italy to swear not to desert their fatherland.
episodes.quote: il che sentendo Scipione, gli andò a trovare, e col ferro ignudo in mano li costrinse a giurare di non abbandonare la patria

episodes.description: Titus Manlius, later Torquatus, threatened to kill the tribune Marcus Pomponius unless he swore to withdraw the accusation against his father Lucius, and the tribune kept the extorted oath.
episodes.quote: Tito andò a trovare Marco, e, minacciando di ammazzarlo se non giurava di levare l’accusa al padre, lo costrinse al giuramento

episodes.description: Numa, needing divine authority for new and unusual orders, pretended familiarity with a nymph who counseled him on what to counsel the people.
episodes.quote: fu bene necessario a Numa, il quale simulò di avere domestichezza con una Ninfa, la quale lo consigliava di quello ch’egli avesse a consigliare il popolo

episodes.description: Lycurgus, Solon, and many other lawgivers likewise had recourse to God to make their laws accepted.
episodes.quote: Così fece Licurgo, così Solone, così molti altri che hanno avuto il medesimo fine di loro

episodes.description: The supposedly civilized people of Florence were persuaded by Friar Girolamo Savonarola that he spoke with God.
episodes.quote: da frate Girolamo Savonarola fu persuaso che parlava con Dio

notes: Corpus heading reads 'Citazioni di questo testo'; the chapter's actual title is 'Della religione de' Romani'. Also quotes Dante on probity rarely descending by the branches.

heading_en: Of how much importance it is to take account of religion, and how Italy, lacking it thanks to the Roman Church, has been ruined
thesis: Princes must keep the foundations of their religion uncorrupted, and the Roman Church, having destroyed religion in Italy and kept the province divided, is the cause of Italy's ruin.
thesis_quote: nessuno maggiore indizio si puote avere della rovina d’una provincia, che vedere dispregiato il culto divino

propositions.statement: Princes of a republic or kingdom must maintain the foundations of the religion they hold, favoring even things they judge false.
propositions.quote: Debbono, adunque, i principi d’una republica o d’uno regno, i fondamenti della religione che loro tengono, mantenergli

propositions.statement: No province was ever united or happy unless it came wholly under the obedience of one republic or one prince, as happened to France and Spain.
propositions.quote: alcuna provincia non fu mai unita o felice, se la non viene tutta alla ubbidienza d’una republica o d’uno principe, come è avvenuto alla Francia ed alla Spagna

propositions.statement: The sole cause that Italy has neither a republic nor a prince governing the whole is the Church, too weak to seize Italy yet strong enough to prevent anyone else from doing so.
propositions.quote: la cagione che la Italia non sia in quel medesimo termine, né abbia anch’ella o una republica o uno principe che la governi, è solamente la Chiesa

propositions.statement: If the Roman court with its authority were transplanted to the lands of the Swiss, its wicked customs would quickly create more disorder there than any other accident could.
propositions.quote: bisognerebbe che fusse di tanta potenza che mandasse ad abitare la corte romana, con l’autorità che l’ha in Italia, in le terre de’ Svizzeri

episodes.description: The pagan oracles such as Delos and the temple of Jupiter Ammon filled the world with devotion until they began answering to please the powerful and were exposed, making men incredulous.
episodes.quote: l’oracolo di Delo, il tempio di Giove Ammone, ed altri celebri oracoli, i quali riempivano il mondo di ammirazione e divozione

episodes.description: Roman soldiers sacking Veii asked the image of Juno 'Vis venire Romam?' and believed she nodded or assented, a credulity Camillus and the city's leaders fostered.
episodes.quote: alcuni di loro entrarono nel tempio di Giunone, ed accostandosi alla imagine di quella, e dicendole: «Vis venire Romam?»

episodes.description: The Church, by means of Charlemagne, drove out the Lombards who were already almost kings of all Italy.
episodes.quote: quando, mediante Carlo Magno, la ne cacciò i Longobardi, ch’erano già quasi re di tutta Italia

episodes.description: In Machiavelli's times the Church took power from the Venetians with the help of France, then drove out the French with the help of the Swiss.
episodes.quote: ella tolse la potenza a’ Viniziani con l’aiuto di Francia; di poi ne cacciò i Franciosi con l’aiuto de’ Svizzeri

heading_en: How the Romans made use of religion to reorder the city, to pursue their enterprises, and to stop tumults
thesis: The Romans used religion to reorder the city, sustain their enterprises, and quell tumults, enabling the Senate to overcome difficulties it could never otherwise have overcome.
thesis_quote: E così la religione fece al Senato vincere quelle difficultà, che, sanza essa, mai averebbe vinte

propositions.statement: Religion well used served both for the conquest of Veii and for restoring the tribunate to the nobility, ends hardly attainable without it.
propositions.quote: E così la religione, usata bene, giovò e per la espugnazione di quella città, e per la restituzione del Tribunato nella Nobilità

propositions.statement: Among the first remedies the nobility employed against popular agitation was religion itself.
propositions.quote: e tra i primi rimedi che vi usò la Nobilità, fu la religione, della quale si servirono in due modi

episodes.description: After plague, famine, and prodigies, the nobles claimed the gods were angry at the plebeian tribunes with consular power, and the frightened plebs elected tribunes who were all nobles.
episodes.quote: la plebe, sbigottita da questa religione, creò i Tribuni tutti nobili

episodes.description: During the long siege of Veii, oracles tied victory to draining the swollen Alban lake, which kept the weary soldiers at the siege until Camillus as dictator took the city.
episodes.quote: essendo il lago Albano, quello anno, cresciuto mirabilmente, ed essendo i soldati romani infastiditi per la lunga ossidione

episodes.description: Against the Terentillan law the nobility had the Sibylline books consulted, which warned that civil sedition threatened the city's liberty that year, cooling the plebs.
episodes.quote: fecero vedere i libri Sibillini, e rispondere come alla città, mediante la civile sedizione, soprastavano quello anno pericoli di non perdere la libertà

episodes.description: Appius Herdonius with four thousand exiles and slaves seized the Capitol by night, and Publius Ruberius induced the plebs to swear obedience to the consul and retake it.
episodes.quote: avendo un Appio Erdonio, con una moltitudine di sbanditi e di servi, in numero di quattromila uomini, occupato di notte il Campidoglio

episodes.description: The new consul Titus Quinctius held the plebs to its oath to the dead consul, and out of fear of religion the plebs obeyed the consul rather than believe the tribunes.
episodes.quote: Tito Livio mostra come la Plebe, per paura della religione, volle più tosto ubbidire al consolo, che credere a’ tribuni

notes: Quotes Livy verbatim: 'Nondum haec, quae nunc tenet saeculum, negligentia Deum venerat...' (Livy 3.20).

heading_en: The Romans interpreted the auspices according to necessity, and with prudence appeared to observe religion even when forced not to; and punished whoever rashly disparaged it
thesis: The Romans accommodated the auspices to necessity, prudently preserving the appearance of religious observance, and punished those who despised religion rashly.
thesis_quote: quando la ragione mostrava loro una cosa doversi fare, non ostante che gli auspicii fossero avversi, la facevano in ogni modo; ma rivoltavanla con termini e modi tanto attamente, che non paresse che la facessino con dispregio della religione

propositions.statement: The auguries were in large part the foundation of the ancient pagan religion and the cause of the Roman republic's wellbeing.
propositions.quote: Non solamente gli augurii, come di sopra si è discorso, erano il fondamento, in buona parte, dell’antica religione de’ Gentili, ma ancora erano quelli che erano cagione del bene essere della Republica romana

propositions.statement: The whole aim of divination was to send soldiers into battle with confidence, from which confidence victory almost always follows.
propositions.quote: Né ad altro fine tendeva questo modo dello aruspicare, che di fare i soldati confidentemente ire alla zuffa; dalla quale confidenza quasi sempre nasce la vittoria

episodes.description: Papirius, facing the Samnites, accepted the chief pullarius' false report of favorable auspices, placed the lying keepers in the front line where the chief was killed, and won the battle while appearing to honor religion.
episodes.quote: comandò ai pullarii che facessono i loro auspicii; ma non beccando i polli, e veggendo il principe de’ pullarii la gran disposizione dello esercito di combattere

episodes.description: Appius Pulcher in Sicily during the First Punic War threw the sacred chickens into the sea when they would not feed, lost the battle against the Carthaginians, and was condemned at Rome.
episodes.quote: Al contrario fece Appio Pulcro in Sicilia, nella prima guerra punica: che, volendo azzuffarsi con l’esercito cartaginese, fece fare gli auspicii a’ pullarii

notes: The Appius Pulcher episode (249 BC) falls outside Livy's surviving Books I-X.

heading_en: The Samnites, as an extreme remedy for their afflicted affairs, had recourse to religion
thesis: The Samnites in their desperation turned to an ancient religious sacrifice and oath as the last means of restoring their soldiers' resolve, testifying how much confidence religion well used can give.
thesis_quote: Il che testifica appieno, quanta confidenza si possa avere mediante la religione bene usata

propositions.statement: To win it is necessary to make soldiers obstinate, and there is no better means of inducing obstinacy than religion.
propositions.quote: ei sapevano che, a volere vincere, era necessario indurre ostinazione negli animi de’ soldati, e che a indurvela non era migliore mezzo che la religione

propositions.statement: Roman virtue and the fear born of past defeats overcame any obstinacy the Samnites had taken from religion and their oath.
propositions.quote: perché la virtù romana, e il timore conceputo per le passate rotte, superò qualunque ostinazione ei potessero avere presa per virtù della religione e per il giuramento preso

episodes.description: The Samnites, repeatedly routed by the Romans and finally destroyed in Tuscany with their allies beaten, could stand neither by their own nor by external forces, yet would not abstain from war.
episodes.quote: Avendo i Sanniti avute più rotte da’ Romani, ed essendo stati per ultimo distrutti in Toscana, e morti i loro eserciti e gli loro capitani

episodes.description: Through their priest Ovius Paccius the Samnites revived an ancient sacrifice, binding their soldiers one by one, amid slain victims and drawn swords, by terrible oaths never to flee battle.
episodes.quote: pensarono di ripetere uno antico loro sacrificio, mediante Ovio Paccio, loro sacerdote

episodes.description: Papirius, encouraging his soldiers against the Samnite linen legion drawn up near Aquilonia, said crests make no wounds and the Roman pilum passes through painted and gilded shields, and the Samnites were defeated.
episodes.quote: Contro a costoro venne Papirio; il quale, nel confortare i suoi soldati, disse: «non enim cristas vulnera facere, et picta atque aurata scuta transire romanum pilum»

notes: Contains two verbatim Latin quotations from Livy (10.31 and 10.39) without naming him.

heading_en: A people accustomed to living under a prince, if by some accident it becomes free, maintains its freedom with difficulty
thesis: A people habituated to life under a prince can scarcely preserve liberty acquired by accident, because servitude leaves it incapable of self-government and the new free state gains partisan enemies but no partisan friends.
thesis_quote: Quanta difficultà sia a uno popolo, uso a vivere sotto uno principe, perservare dipoi la libertà, se per alcuno accidente l’acquista

propositions.statement: A people long kept in servitude is like a wild animal raised in captivity: released, it cannot feed itself and becomes prey to the first who would rechain it.
propositions.quote: quel popolo è non altrimenti che un animale bruto, il quale, ancora che di natura feroce e silvestre, sia stato nutrito sempre in carcere ed in servitù

propositions.statement: A state that becomes free makes partisan enemies (those who fed on the tyranny) but not partisan friends, since free life rewards only through honest, defined channels that create no personal obligation.
propositions.quote: lo stato che diventa libero si fa partigiani inimici, e non partigiani amici

propositions.statement: There is no more potent, secure, or necessary remedy for a new free order than to kill the sons of Brutus, i.e., to eliminate the enemies of the new order.
propositions.quote: non ci è più potente rimedio, né più valido né più sicuro né più necessario, che ammazzare i figliuoli di Bruto

propositions.statement: Whoever has the general populace as his enemy is never secure, and the more cruelty he uses the weaker his principality becomes; the greatest remedy is to make the people friendly.
propositions.quote: chi ha per nimico l’universale non si assicura mai, e quanta più crudeltà usa tanto più debole diventa il suo principato

episodes.description: Rome acquired its liberty after the expulsion of the Tarquins and, being uncorrupted, was able to maintain it.
episodes.quote: come l’acquistò Roma dopo la cacciata de’ Tarquinii

episodes.description: The sons of Brutus, with other Roman youths, conspired against the fatherland because under the consuls they could no longer profit extraordinarily as under the kings, and were executed.
episodes.quote: non furono indotti, insieme con altri giovani romani, a congiurare contro alla patria per altro, se non perché non si potevono valere straordinariamente sotto i consoli come sotto i re

episodes.description: Clearchus, tyrant of Heraclea, restored by the optimates against the people, cut all the optimates to pieces to the extreme satisfaction of the populace, thereby satisfying the popular desire for revenge.
episodes.quote: tagliò a pezzi tutti gli ottimati, con una estrema sodisfazione de’ popolari

episodes.description: The kingdom of France lives secure because its kings are bound by infinite laws that comprehend the security of all their peoples, disposing freely only of arms and money.
episodes.quote: In esemplo ci è il regno di Francia, il quale non vive sicuro per altro che per essersi quelli re obligati a infinite leggi

notes: Clearchus episode is non-Roman antiquity (Heraclea Pontica, 4th c. BC). France classified contemporary-italy per period rule (1400s-1500s present-day reference, though non-Italian).

heading_en: A corrupt people that comes into freedom can maintain itself free only with the greatest difficulty
thesis: Whether a city can take and keep its liberty depends on whether its matter is corrupt: uncorrupted Rome kept freedom after the Tarquins, while the corrupted Rome of Caesar's time could never recover it.
thesis_quote: una città corrotta che viva sotto uno principe, come che quel principe con tutta la sua stirpe si spenga, mai non si può ridurre libera

propositions.statement: Where the matter is not corrupt, tumults and scandals do no harm; where it is corrupt, even well-ordered laws avail nothing unless enforced by extreme force until the matter becomes good.
propositions.quote: dove la materia non è corrotta, i tumulti ed altri scandoli non nuocono: dove la è corrotta, le leggi bene ordinate non giovano

propositions.statement: A city in decline through corruption of matter is raised, if at all, by the virtue of one living man, not by the virtue of the collectivity sustaining good orders.
propositions.quote: se mai occorre che la si rilievi, occorre per la virtù d’uno uomo che è vivo allora, non per la virtù dello universale

propositions.statement: No one man lives long enough to re-accustom to good habits a city long accustomed to bad ones.
propositions.quote: non può essere uno uomo di tanta vita, che ’l tempo basti ad avvezzare bene una città lungo tempo male avvezza

propositions.statement: Corruption and unfitness for free life arise from an inequality present in the city, which can only be removed by extraordinary means few know or wish to use.
propositions.quote: tale corruzione e poca attitudine alla vita libera, nasce da una inequalità che è in quella città

episodes.description: Rome, having expelled the Tarquins while still uncorrupted, could immediately take and maintain its liberty, an oath against kings sufficing to keep the people firm.
episodes.quote: la quale, cacciati i Tarquinii, poté subito prendere e mantenere quella libertà

episodes.description: After the deaths of Caesar, Caligula, and Nero and the extinction of the whole Caesarean line, corrupted Rome could not even begin to recover liberty.
episodes.quote: morto Cesare, morto Caio Caligola, morto Nerone, spenta tutta la stirpe cesarea, non poté mai, non solamente mantenere, ma pure dar principio alla libertà

episodes.description: The corruption that the Marian factions, headed by Caesar, had introduced into the Roman people so blinded the multitude that it did not see the yoke it was placing on its own neck.
episodes.quote: quella corruzione che le parti mariane avevano messa nel popolo; delle quali sendo capo Cesare, potette accecare quella moltitudine

episodes.description: Syracuse remained free only during the lifetimes of Dion and Timoleon, whose virtue held the city free; at their deaths it returned to its former tyranny.
episodes.quote: come intervenne, a Siracusa, di Dione e di Timoleone

episodes.description: After the death of Filippo Visconti, Milan tried to return to liberty but could not and did not know how to maintain it, its members being wholly corrupt.
episodes.quote: Il che si vide dopo la morte di Filippo Visconti; che, volendosi ridurre Milano alla libertà, non potette e non seppe mantenerla

episodes.description: Thebes, through the virtue of Epaminondas, could hold the form of a republic and of empire while he lived, but returned to its former disorders at his death.
episodes.quote: come intervenne a Tebe, la quale, per la virtù di Epaminonda, mentre lui visse, potette tenere forma di republica e di imperio

notes: Milan after Filippo Maria Visconti's death (1447, Ambrosian Republic) is strictly mid-15th century.

heading_en: In what way a free state could be maintained in corrupt cities, if one exists; or, if it does not exist, how to establish one
thesis: In a thoroughly corrupt city it is almost impossible either to maintain or to create a free state, because no laws or orders suffice to restrain universal corruption unless orders themselves are renewed by extraordinary, quasi-regal power.
thesis_quote: non si truovano né leggi né ordini che bastino a frenare una universale corruzione

propositions.statement: Just as good customs need laws to be maintained, so laws need good customs to be observed.
propositions.quote: così come gli buoni costumi, per mantenersi, hanno bisogno delle leggi; così le leggi, per osservarsi, hanno bisogno de’ buoni costumi

propositions.statement: Laws change with circumstances but orders rarely or never do, so new laws do not suffice because the fixed orders corrupt them.
propositions.quote: le nuove leggi non bastano, perché gli ordini, che stanno saldi, le corrompono

propositions.statement: It very rarely happens that a good man is willing to become prince by evil ways even for a good end, or that a wicked man, having become prince, is willing to do good.
propositions.quote: radissime volte accaggia che uno buono, per vie cattive, ancora che il fine suo fusse buono, voglia diventare principe; e che uno reo, divenuto principe, voglia operare bene

propositions.statement: If a republic is to be created or maintained in a corrupt city, it must be drawn toward the kingly state so that insolent men whom laws cannot correct are checked by a quasi-regal power.
propositions.quote: sarebbe necessario ridurla più verso lo stato regio, che verso lo stato popolare

episodes.description: Once the Romans had subdued Africa and Asia and reduced nearly all Greece, they felt secure in their liberty, and the consulship came to be given first by favor and then by power rather than by virtue.
episodes.quote: avendo i Romani domata l’Africa e l’Asia, e ridotta quasi tutta la Grecia a sua ubbidienza, erano divenuti sicuri della libertà loro

episodes.description: Cleomenes killed the ephors so as to rule alone in Sparta and then used his authority well.
episodes.quote: che fece Cleomene: il quale se, per essere solo, ammazzò gli Efori

episodes.description: Romulus killed his brother and Titus Tatius the Sabine for the same reasons and afterwards used his authority well, his material not being stained by corruption.
episodes.quote: Romolo, per le medesime cagioni, ammazzò il fratello e Tito Tazio Sabino, e dipoi usarono bene quella loro autorità

institutions: laws on adultery, sumptuary matters, and ambition
notes: The description of Rome's orders (People, Senate, tribunes, consuls, mode of electing magistrates and making laws) is treated as institutional analysis rather than an episode. Death of Titus Tatius is Livy 1:14; quote ref keyed to Remus (1:7).

heading_en: After an excellent prince a weak prince can maintain himself; but after a weak one, no kingdom can be maintained by another weak one
thesis: A weak successor can live off the virtue of an excellent predecessor, but two weak princes in succession doom a kingdom, as the sequence of Rome's first kings shows.
thesis_quote: dopo uno eccellente principe, si può mantenere uno principe debole; ma, dopo un debole, non si può, con un altro debole, mantenere alcun regno

propositions.statement: A successor of less virtue than the first can maintain a state through the virtue of the man who ruled before him and enjoy his labors.
propositions.quote: uno successore, non di tanta virtù quanto il primo, può mantenere uno stato per la virtù di colui che lo ha retto innanzi

propositions.statement: If two rulers of great virtue follow one another, they often do very great things and their fame reaches the heavens.
propositions.quote: se dua, l’uno dopo l’altro, sono di gran virtù, si vede spesso che fanno cose grandissime

propositions.statement: A prince who resembles Romulus, armed with prudence and arms, will hold his state in any case unless an obstinate and excessive force takes it from him; one who resembles Numa holds it only as times and fortune allow.
propositions.quote: chi somiglierà Romolo, e fia come esso armato di prudenza e d’armi, lo terrà in ogni modo, se da una ostinata ed eccessiva forza non gli è tolto

propositions.statement: If Rome had drawn as its third king a man who did not know how to restore its reputation by arms, it could never, or only with the greatest difficulty, have taken root and achieved what it did.
propositions.quote: se Roma sortiva per terzo suo re un uomo che non sapesse con le armi renderle la sua riputazione non arebbe mai poi, o con grandissima difficultà, potuto pigliare piede

episodes.description: Rome had the great fortune that its first three kings were, in order, most fierce and warlike (Romulus), quiet and religious (Numa), and again fierce and war-loving (Tullus).
episodes.quote: avendo il primo re ferocissimo e bellicoso, l’altro quieto e religioso, il terzo simile di ferocità a Romolo

episodes.description: David, excellent in arms, learning, and judgment, left Solomon a peaceful kingdom which Solomon preserved by the arts of peace, but Rehoboam, resembling neither, barely kept a sixth of the kingdom.
episodes.quote: Davit, sanza dubbio, fu un uomo, per arme, per dottrina, per giudizio, eccellentissimo

episodes.description: Bajazet, sultan of the Turks, a lover of peace, could enjoy the labors of his father Mehmed, and his son Selim now seems set to surpass the grandfather's glory.
episodes.quote: Baisit, sultan de’ Turchi, come che fussi più amatore della pace che della guerra, potette godersi le fatiche di Maumetto suo padre

episodes.description: Ancus, gifted by nature to use peace and endure war, first sought peace, but seeing his neighbors judged him effeminate and esteemed him little, turned to war and resembled Romulus rather than Numa.
episodes.quote: venne Anco, in modo dalla natura dotato, che poteva usare la pace e sopportare la guerra

notes: Ottoman succession (Mehmed II, Bajazet II, Selim I) classified contemporary-italy per period rule (1400s-1500s), though non-Italian.

heading_en: Two continuous successions of virtuous princes do great things; and as well-ordered republics necessarily have virtuous successions, their acquisitions and growth are great
thesis: Two consecutive successions of virtuous princes suffice to acquire the world, and a well-ordered republic, electing its rulers, necessarily enjoys infinite virtuous successions and thus great expansion.
thesis_quote: due continove successioni di principi virtuosi sono sufficienti ad acquistare il mondo

propositions.statement: A republic, by its mode of electing, has not merely two but infinite most virtuous princes succeeding one another, and such virtuous succession exists in every well-ordered republic.
propositions.quote: avendo per il modo dello eleggere non solamente due successioni ma infiniti principi virtuosissimi che sono l’uno dell’altro successori

propositions.statement: Because the consuls came to power not by heredity, deceit, or violent ambition but by free suffrage, they were always most excellent men, and Rome reached its final greatness in as many years as it had spent under kings.
propositions.quote: non per eredità o per inganni o per ambizione violenta, ma per suffragi liberi venivano a quello imperio, ed erono sempre uomini eccellentissimi

episodes.description: Philip of Macedon and Alexander the Great exemplify two consecutive virtuous princes sufficient to acquire the world.
episodes.quote: come furano Filippo di Macedonia ed Alessandro Magno

episodes.description: Once Rome expelled its kings, it escaped the dangers of a weak or wicked royal successor, since supreme command was vested in freely elected consuls.
episodes.quote: Poiché Roma ebbe cacciati i re, mancò di quelli pericoli

heading_en: How much blame that prince and that republic deserve which lack arms of their own
thesis: Where there are men but no soldiers, the fault lies with the prince, not with site or nature, for a capable ruler can make excellent soldiers out of any people.
thesis_quote: se dove è uomini non è soldati, nasce per difetto del principe, e non per altro difetto o di sito o di natura

propositions.statement: Present princes and modern republics that lack their own soldiers for defense and offense should be ashamed of themselves.
propositions.quote: Debbono i presenti principi e le moderne republiche, le quali circa le difese ed offese mancano di soldati propri, vergognarsi di loro medesime

propositions.statement: Men fit for war are born not only in Lacedaemon but everywhere men are born, provided someone knows how to direct them to military service.
propositions.quote: non solamente in Lacedemonia nascevano gli uomini da guerra, ma in ogni altra parte dove nascessi uomini, pure che si trovasse chi li sapesse indirizzare alla milizia

episodes.description: Tullus, succeeding to the kingdom after forty years of Roman peace in which no man had seen war, chose to use his own men rather than Samnites or Tuscans and by his virtue made them excellent soldiers at once.
episodes.quote: Tullo, sendo stata Roma in pace quarant’anni, non trovò, succedendo egli nel regno, uomo che fusse stato mai in guerra

episodes.description: The king of England recently assaulted the kingdom of France using only his own people, though England had been thirty years without war, because that well-ordered kingdom does not neglect the orders of war in peacetime.
episodes.quote: il re d’Inghilterra assaltò il regno di Francia, né prese altri soldati che popoli suoi

episodes.description: Pelopidas and Epaminondas, having freed Thebes from Spartan servitude, armed its effeminate citizens and defeated the Spartan armies in the field.
episodes.quote: Pelopida ed Epaminonda tebani, poiché gli ebbero libera Tebe, e trattala della servitù dello imperio spartano

notes: Chapter closes quoting Virgil (Aeneid 6): 'Desidesque movebit / Tullus in arma viros'. English episode refers to Henry VIII's 1513 invasion of France.

heading_en: What is to be noted in the case of the three Roman Horatii and the three Alban Curiatii
thesis: The combat of the Horatii and Curiatii teaches that one should never stake one's whole fortune on part of one's forces, that well-ordered cities never offset faults with merits, and that agreements whose observance may be doubted are never wise.
thesis_quote: Dove sono da notare tre cose: l’una, che mai non si debbe con parte delle sue forze arrischiare tutta la sua fortuna

propositions.statement: One should never risk one's entire fortune with only part of one's forces.
propositions.quote: mai non si debbe con parte delle sue forze arrischiare tutta la sua fortuna

propositions.statement: In a well-ordered city faults are never compensated by merits.
propositions.quote: non mai in una città bene ordinata le colpe con gli meriti si ricompensano

propositions.statement: Decisions are never wise where one must or can doubt their observance by the other party.
propositions.quote: non mai sono i partiti savi, dove si debba o possa dubitare della inosservanza

episodes.description: Tullus of Rome and Mettius of Alba agreed that the people whose three champions won would rule the other; all the Alban Curiatii died, one Roman Horatius survived, and Alba became subject to Rome.
episodes.quote: Furono morti tutti i Curiazii albani, restò vivo uno degli Orazii romani

episodes.description: The victorious Horatius killed his sister, who wept for her betrothed Curiatius, was put on trial for the crime, and was freed more by his father's prayers than by his own merits.
episodes.quote: scontrando una sua sorella, che era a uno de’ tre Curiazii morti maritata, che piangeva la morte del marito, l’ammazzò

episodes.description: Mettius, though he confessed defeat and promised obedience to Tullus, sought to deceive him in the first expedition they undertook together against the Veientes, having realized too late the rashness of his bargain.
episodes.quote: nella prima espedizione che gli ebbero a convenire contro a’ Veienti, si vide come ei cercò d’ingannarlo

heading_en: That one should not put at risk one's whole fortune without one's whole forces; and that, for this reason, guarding passes is often harmful
thesis: It was never a wise course to put one's whole fortune at risk without all one's forces, which is why attempting to hold mountain passes with necessarily small detachments is usually ruinous.
thesis_quote: Non fu mai giudicato partito savio mettere a pericolo tutta la fortuna tua e non tutte le forze

propositions.statement: The decision to hold difficult places and guard passes is almost always harmful unless all one's forces can be conveniently kept there.
propositions.quote: quasi sempre questa diliberazione sarà dannosa, se già in quello luogo difficile commodamente tu non potesse tenere tutte le forze tue

propositions.statement: Many men cannot be brought to guard alpine places, since they cannot live there long and the places are narrow and hold few, so a massed enemy intent on passing cannot be withstood.
propositions.quote: non si potendo condurre alla guardia de’ luoghi alpestri molti uomini, sì per non vi potere vivere lungo tempo, sì per essere i luoghi stretti e capaci di pochi

propositions.statement: When the pass you counted on is lost, such terror enters your peoples and remaining troops that you lose without even testing their virtue, forfeiting your whole fortune with part of your forces.
propositions.quote: entra il più delle volte ne’ popoli e nel residuo delle genti tua tanto terrore, che, sanza potere esperimentare la virtù d’esse, rimani perdente

episodes.description: Tullus and Mettius committed the entire fortune of their countries and the virtue of all the men in their armies to just three citizens each, a minimal part of their forces.
episodes.quote: faccendo come Tullo e Mezio, quando e’ commissono la fortuna tutta della patria loro

episodes.description: Despite the difficulty of Hannibal's Alpine and Apennine crossings, the Romans chose to await him first at the Ticinus and then on the plain of Arezzo rather than destroy their army in harsh mountain positions.
episodes.quote: i Romani l’aspettarono prima in sul Tesino, e dipoi nel piano d’Arezzo

episodes.description: In 1515 Francis I of France, expected to be held at the mountain passes by the Swiss, entered Italy by an unknown route and reached Lombardy before they realized it, dismaying them into retreating to Milan.
episodes.quote: Quando Francesco re di Francia disegnava passare in Italia per la recuperazione dello stato di Lombardia

notes: Hannibal episode (Ticinus, Trasimene campaign) belongs to Livy's third decade, outside Livy I-X, hence no candidate ref.

heading_en: Well-ordered republics establish rewards and punishments for their citizens, and never compensate one with the other
thesis: No well-ordered republic ever cancels its citizens' demerits with their merits: it rewards good deeds and punishes bad ones in the same man without regard to his past services.
thesis_quote: nessuna republica bene ordinata non mai cancellò i demeriti con gli meriti de’ suoi cittadini

propositions.statement: When rewards and punishments are well observed without offsetting, a city lives free a long time; otherwise it soon comes to ruin.
propositions.quote: quando questi ordini sono bene osservati, una città vive libera molto tempo: altrimenti sempre rovinerà tosto

propositions.statement: If a citizen's famous deed earns him both reputation and the audacity to do wrong without fear of punishment, he quickly becomes so insolent that all civil life dissolves.
propositions.quote: si aggiugne, oltre alla riputazione che quella cosa gli arreca, una audacia e confidenza di poter, senza temere pena, fare qualche opera non buona

propositions.statement: Even a poor republic should not abstain from giving what little it can, for any small gift given in recompense of a good deed is esteemed honorable and very great by its receiver.
propositions.quote: E benché una republica sia povera, e possa dare poco, debbe da quel poco non astenersi

episodes.description: Although Horatius had just conquered the Curiatii, the Romans were so displeased by his killing of his sister that they brought him to trial for his life despite his great and fresh merits.
episodes.quote: dispiacque tanto tale omicidio a’ Romani, che lo condussono a disputare della vita, non ostante che gli meriti suoi fossero tanto grandi e sì freschi

episodes.description: Horatius Cocles held the enemy on the bridge until it was cut, and was rewarded publicly with two staiora of land.
episodes.quote: l’uno sostenne i nimici sopra un ponte, tanto che si tagliasse

episodes.description: Mucius Scaevola burned the hand that had erred in trying to kill Porsenna, king of the Tuscans, and received the same public reward of land.
episodes.quote: l’altro si arse la mano, che aveva errato, volendo ammazzare Porsenna, re degli Toscani

episodes.description: Manlius Capitolinus, rewarded with a small measure of flour for saving the Capitol from the besieging Gauls, was later thrown headlong from that same Capitol when he stirred sedition in Rome, without regard for his merits.
episodes.quote: per avere salvato il Campidoglio da’ Franciosi che vi erano a campo

notes: Manlius's later sedition and execution is Livy 6:20; the quoted clause (saving the Capitol) corresponds to Livy 5:47.

heading_en: Whoever wishes to reform a long-established state in a free city should retain at least the shadow of the ancient modes
thesis: A reformer of a city's state must retain at least the shadow of the ancient modes so that the people, who feed on appearances as much as realities, do not perceive the change of orders.
thesis_quote: è necessitato a ritenere l’ombra almanco de’ modi antichi, acciò che a’ popoli non paia avere mutato ordine

propositions.statement: The generality of men feed on what seems as much as on what is, and are often moved more by things that seem than by things that are.
propositions.quote: lo universale degli uomini si pascono così di quel che pare come di quello che è

propositions.statement: If new magistrates differ from the ancient ones in number, authority, and term, they should at least retain the ancient name.
propositions.quote: se i magistrati variano, e di numero e d’autorità e di tempo, degli antichi, che almeno ritenghino il nome

propositions.statement: He who wishes to establish an absolute power, which authors call tyranny, must renew everything.
propositions.quote: quello che vuole fare una potestà assoluta, la quale dagli autori è chiamata tirannide, debbe rinnovare ogni cosa

episodes.description: At the start of their free life the Romans, creating two consuls in place of a king, allowed them no more than twelve lictors so as not to exceed the number that had served the kings.
episodes.quote: avendo in cambio d’uno re creati duoi consoli, non vollono ch’egli avessono più che dodici littori

episodes.description: Because an annual sacrifice could only be performed by the person of the king, the Romans created a head of that sacrifice called the Rex Sacrificulus, subordinated to the high priest, so the people would not miss the kings.
episodes.quote: crearono uno capo di detto sacrificio, il quale loro chiamarono Re Sacrificulo, e sottomessonlo al sommo Sacerdote

heading_en: A new prince, in a city or province taken by him, should make everything new
thesis: A new prince with weak foundations who will not turn to civil life has no better remedy for holding his principality than to make everything in that state new, though such modes are most cruel.
thesis_quote: il megliore rimedio che egli abbia, a tenere quel principato, è, sendo egli nuovo principe, fare ogni cosa, in quello stato, di nuovo

propositions.statement: The new prince should make new governments with new names, authorities, and men, make the rich poor and the poor rich, build and destroy cities, and move inhabitants, leaving nothing in the province untouched by him.
propositions.quote: fare nuovi governi con nuovi nomi, con nuove autorità, con nuovi uomini; fare i ricchi poveri, i poveri ricchi

propositions.statement: Since these modes are most cruel and enemies of every Christian and human way of living, every man should flee them and prefer to live as a private person rather than as a king with such ruin of men.
propositions.quote: debbegli qualunque uomo fuggire, e volere piuttosto vivere privato, che re con tanta rovina degli uomini

propositions.statement: Men take certain middle ways that are most harmful, because they do not know how to be either wholly bad or wholly good.
propositions.quote: gli uomini pigliono certe vie del mezzo, che sono dannosissime; perché non sanno essere né tutti cattivi né tutti buoni

episodes.description: David, when he became king, made the rich poor and the poor rich, filling the hungry with good things and sending the rich away empty.
episodes.quote: come fece Davit quando ei diventò re: «qui esurientes implevit bonis, et divites dimisit inanes»

episodes.description: Philip of Macedon, father of Alexander, moved men from province to province as herdsmen move their herds, and by these modes grew from a petty king into prince of Greece.
episodes.quote: tramutava gli uomini di provincia in provincia, come e’ mandriani tramutano le mandrie loro

notes: The Latin quotation 'qui esurientes implevit bonis, et divites dimisit inanes' is from the Magnificat (Luke 1:53), applied by Machiavelli to David.

heading_en: Men very rarely know how to be altogether bad or altogether good
thesis: Men do not know how to be honorably bad or perfectly good, and when a malicious deed has greatness or generosity in it they cannot bring themselves to attempt it, as Giovampagolo Baglioni's failure to strike Pope Julius II shows.
thesis_quote: gli uomini non sanno essere onorevolmente cattivi, o perfettamente buoni, e, come una malizia ha in sé grandezza, o è in alcuna parte generosa, e’ non vi sanno entrare

propositions.statement: The prudent men concluded that men do not know how to be honorably wicked or perfectly good.
propositions.quote: si conchiuse, nascesse che gli uomini non sanno essere onorevolmente cattivi, o perfettamente buoni

episodes.description: In 1505-06 Pope Julius II, marching to expel the Bentivogli from Bologna and remove Giovampagolo Baglioni from Perugia, entered Perugia unarmed with only his simple guard, placing himself in his enemy's hands.
episodes.quote: non aspettò di entrare in quella città con lo esercito suo, che lo guardasse, ma vi entrò disarmato

episodes.description: Giovampagolo Baglioni, an incestuous and parricidal tyrant with troops at hand, did not dare crush the pope and all his cardinals when he had the just occasion, a deed whose greatness would have outweighed every infamy.
episodes.quote: non seppe, o, a dir meglio, non ardì, avendone giusta occasione, fare una impresa, dove ciascuno avesse ammirato l’animo suo

notes: Machiavelli dates the expedition 1505 (Florentine style); modern dating is 1506. Purely contemporary chapter, no Roman material.

heading_en: For what reason the Romans were less ungrateful to their citizens than the Athenians
thesis: Rome showed less ingratitude to its citizens than Athens because, never having lost its liberty to a citizen before Sulla and Marius, it had less cause for suspicion, whereas Athens, once enslaved by Pisistratus, avenged even the shadow of offenses.
thesis_quote: i Romani avevano meno cagione di sospettare de’ suoi cittadini, che gli Ateniesi

propositions.statement: Whoever reads the deeds of republics will find in all of them some species of ingratitude toward their citizens.
propositions.quote: Qualunque legge le cose fatte dalle republiche, troverrà in tutte qualche spezie d’ingratitudine contro a’ suoi cittadini

propositions.statement: Peoples bite more fiercely after they have recovered their liberty than after they have merely preserved it.
propositions.quote: i popoli mordono più fieramente poi ch’egli hanno recuperata la libertà, che poi che l’hanno conservata

propositions.statement: If Rome's liberty had been taken from it as Athens' was, Rome would have been no more merciful toward its citizens than Athens.
propositions.quote: se a Roma fusse stata tolta la libertà come a Atene, non sarebbe stata Roma più pia verso i suoi cittadini

episodes.description: Athens had its liberty taken by Pisistratus in its most flourishing time under a deception of goodness, and on regaining freedom became the promptest avenger of even the shadow of its citizens' errors, whence exiles, deaths, and ostracism.
episodes.quote: sendogli tolta la libertà da Pisistrato nel suo più florido tempo, e sotto uno inganno di bontà

episodes.description: Collatinus, though he had helped liberate Rome, was sent into exile for no other reason than bearing the name of the Tarquins.
episodes.quote: fu mandato in esilio non per altra cagione che per tenere il nome de’ Tarquinii

episodes.description: Publius Valerius, having merely aroused suspicion by building a house on a hill, was nearly made an exile.
episodes.quote: avendo solo dato di sé sospetto per edificare una casa in sul monte Celio, fu ancora per esser fatto esule

notes: Machiavelli places Valerius's house on the 'monte Celio'; Livy 2:7 has it on the Velia.

heading_en: Which is more ungrateful, a people or a prince
thesis: Ingratitude springs from avarice or from suspicion; peoples never used it through avarice and far less through suspicion than princes, having less cause to suspect their victorious captains.
thesis_quote: si vedrà come i popoli non mai per avarizia la usarono, e per sospetto assai manco che i principi, avendo meno cagione di sospettare

propositions.statement: The vice of ingratitude is born either of avarice or of suspicion.
propositions.quote: questo vizio della ingratitudine nasce o dall’avarizia o da il sospetto

propositions.statement: A captain who virtuously wins an empire for his lord necessarily acquires such reputation with soldiers, enemies, and subjects that the victory cannot taste good to the lord who sent him.
propositions.quote: acquista tanta riputazione, che quella vittoria non può sapere di buono a quel signore che lo ha mandato

propositions.statement: When a prince or people fails to reward, or rather offends, a captain out of suspicion rather than avarice, it deserves some excuse.
propositions.quote: quando ei non lo premia, o, a dir meglio, l’offende, non mosso da avarizia ma da sospetto, allora merita, e il popolo e il principe, qualche scusa

propositions.statement: In an uncorrupted republic these suspicious modes are causes of great goods and keep it living free, men remaining better and less ambitious through fear of punishment.
propositions.quote: in una republica non corrotta sono cagione di gran beni, e fanno che la ne vive libera; più mantenendosi, per paura di punizione, gli uomini migliori e meno ambiziosi

episodes.description: Antonius Primus took Vespasian's side, defeated two Vitellian armies and occupied Rome, but Mucianus stripped him of his army's obedience and his authority, and he died almost desperate, reduced to no rank.
episodes.quote: Antonio Primo, che si trovava con un altro esercito in Illiria, prese le parti sue, e vennene in Italia contro a Vitellio

episodes.description: Gonsalvo Ferrante conquered the kingdom of Naples from the French for Ferdinand of Aragon, who as reward stripped him of his men-at-arms and fortresses and led him to Spain, where he died in dishonor.
episodes.quote: Consalvo Ferrante, militando nel regno di Napoli contro a’ Franciosi, per Ferrando re di Ragona, conquistassi e vincessi quel regno

episodes.description: Rome's ingratitude toward Scipio arose from a suspicion born of the greatness of his victory over Carthage and his extraordinary reputation, with Cato Priscus the first to move against him.
episodes.quote: la ingratitudine usata a Scipione nacque da uno sospetto che i cittadini cominciarono avere di lui

episodes.description: Coriolanus and Camillus were exiled for injuries each had done to the plebs; Coriolanus was never pardoned, while Camillus was recalled and adored like a prince for the rest of his life.
episodes.quote: Coriolano e Cammillo furono fatti esuli per ingiuria che l’uno e l’altro avea fatto alla plebe

notes: Chapter quotes Cornelius Tacitus: 'Proclivius est iniuriae, quam beneficio vicem exsolvere...'. Scipio's trials fall outside Livy I-X; Camillus's exile is Livy 5:32 (ref keyed to Coriolanus, 2:35).

heading_en: What modes a prince or a republic should use to escape the vice of ingratitude, and what modes a captain or a citizen should use so as not to be crushed by it
thesis: A prince escapes the necessity of being suspicious or ungrateful by leading his expeditions in person, while a republic must imitate Rome's modes of government and a captain must either promptly surrender his command or boldly make the conquest his own.
thesis_quote: Uno principe, per fuggire questa necessità di avere a vivere con sospetto, o essere ingrato, debbe personalmente andare nelle espedizioni

propositions.statement: A republic that would avoid ingratitude should govern itself as Rome did, and a citizen who would escape its bites should observe the limits observed by Roman citizens.
propositions.quote: una republica che non voglia avere cagione d’essere ingrata, si debba governare come Roma, e uno cittadino che voglia fuggire quelli suoi morsi, debbe osservare i termini osservati da’ cittadini romani

propositions.statement: A victorious captain should either immediately leave the army and place himself in his prince's hands, avoiding every insolent or ambitious act, or else boldly take the contrary course and make the acquisition his own.
propositions.quote: o subito dopo la vittoria lasci lo esercito, e rimettasi nelle mani del suo principe, guardandosi da ogni atto insolente o ambizioso

propositions.statement: Men know how to be neither wholly wicked nor wholly good, so victorious captains stay ambiguous between submission and boldness and in that ambiguity are crushed.
propositions.quote: gli uomini non sanno essere né al tutto tristi, né al tutto buoni; e sempre interviene che, subito dopo la vittoria, lasciare lo esercito non vogliono

propositions.statement: Because the whole city, nobles and commoners alike, served in Rome's wars, so many virtuous and victorious men arose in every age that the people had no cause to fear any one of them, each watching the other.
propositions.quote: adoperandosi tutta la città, e gli nobili e gli ignobili, nella guerra, surgeva sempre in Roma in ogni età tanti uomini virtuosi

episodes.description: The early Roman emperors went personally on their expeditions, keeping the glory and the acquisition for themselves.
episodes.quote: come facevono nel principio quegli imperadori romani

episodes.description: In Machiavelli's own times the Turk (the Ottoman sultan) campaigns in person, as virtuous rulers have done and do.
episodes.quote: come fa ne’ tempi nostri il Turco

episodes.description: Roman citizens raised to the dictatorship gained the greater glory the sooner they laid it down, so such modes generated no suspicion and hence no ingratitude.
