episodes.quote: venendo alla dittatura quello maggiore gloria ne riportava che più tosto la diponeva

notes: The Ottoman sultan reference classified contemporary-italy per period rule (1400s-1500s), though non-Italian.

heading_en: Roman commanders were never extraordinarily punished for errors
thesis: Rome never punished its generals extraordinarily for errors or ignorance, because commanders must deliberate with a free mind, unburdened by fear of punishment, for warfare is already difficult and dangerous enough.
thesis_quote: lo avere l’animo libero ed espedito, e sanza altri estrinseci rispetti nel pigliare i partiti

propositions.statement: If harsh punishments for defeat were added to the inherent burdens of command, no captain could deliberate vigorously amid so many fears.
propositions.quote: egli era inpossibile che quello capitano intra tanti sospetti potessi deliberare strenuamente

propositions.statement: The Romans chastised errors of malice mildly, and errors of ignorance they did not punish at all but rewarded and honored.
propositions.quote: se il loro errore fusse stato per malizia, e’ lo gastigavano umanamente; se gli era per ignoranza, non che lo punissono, e’ lo premiavano ed onoravano

propositions.statement: The ignominy of defeat is itself sufficient punishment for a commander, so no greater penalty should be added to terrify him.
propositions.quote: giudicando essi che a questi tali fusse assai pena la ignominia dello avere perduto, non li vollono con altra maggiore pena sbigottire

episodes.description: Sergius and Verginius, each commanding part of the army besieging Veii, refused out of rivalry to aid one another and were punished only with fines rather than death.
episodes.quote: Erano Sergio e Virginio a campo a Veio, ciascuno preposto a una parte dello esercito

episodes.description: After Varro's temerity caused the Roman defeat at Cannae, the whole senatorial order went to meet him and thanked him for not despairing of Rome instead of punishing him.
episodes.quote: per la temerità del quale sendo rotti i Romani a Canne da Annibale

episodes.description: When the dictator Papirius Cursor wanted to execute Fabius for fighting the Samnites against his orders, Fabius' father argued that the Roman people had never so treated even defeated commanders.
episodes.quote: Quando Papirio Cursore voleva fare morire Fabio, per avere, contro al suo comandamento, combattuto co’ Sanniti

notes: The Cannae/Varro episode falls outside Livy's first decade (Livy 22.61); candidate given on name-match.

heading_en: A republic or prince should not defer benefits until times of necessity
thesis: Benefits granted to the people only when danger compels them earn no gratitude, so a state must win over its people before adversity arrives rather than relying on the exceptional Roman success with Porsenna.
thesis_quote: non sia alcuno che, confidatosi in questo esemplo, differisca ne’ tempi de’ pericoli a guadagnarsi il popolo

propositions.statement: The people will judge benefits conceded under duress as owed to your adversaries, not to you, and will feel no obligation.
propositions.quote: l’universale giudicherà non avere quel bene da te, ma dagli avversari tuoi

propositions.statement: Whoever holds a state must consider in advance what adverse times may come and which men he will then need, and live with them accordingly.
propositions.quote: debbe qualunque tiene stato, così republica come principe, considerare innanzi, quali tempi gli possono venire addosso contrari, e di quali uomini ne’ tempi avversi si può avere di bisogno

propositions.statement: Whoever waits until danger arrives to regain men with benefits not only fails to secure himself but accelerates his own ruin.
propositions.quote: non solamente non se ne assicura, ma accelera la sua rovina

episodes.description: When Porsenna attacked Rome to restore the Tarquins, the Senate, fearing the plebs might prefer kings to war, relieved them of the salt tax and every burden, and the people endured siege, famine, and war.
episodes.quote: quando Porsenna venne a assaltare Roma per rimettere i Tarquinii

notes: Machiavelli explains the Roman success as exceptional: the state was new and the memory of royal abuses fresh.

heading_en: When an evil has grown within or against a state, it is better to temporize than to strike at it
thesis: Once a danger inside or against a republic has grown great enough to frighten everyone, it is safer to temporize with it than to try to extinguish it, since direct opposition usually increases its force.
thesis_quote: è molto più sicuro partito temporeggiarsi con quello, che tentare di estinguerlo

propositions.statement: Those who try to quench a grown evil almost always make its forces greater and accelerate the harm they feared.
propositions.quote: coloro che tentano di ammorzarlo fanno le sue forze maggiori, e fanno accelerare quel male che da quello si sospettava

propositions.statement: Such evils are hard to recognize at birth because men naturally favor the beginnings of things, especially virtuous-seeming works of young men.
propositions.quote: E tanto è più difficile il conoscere questi inconvenienti quando e’ nascono, quanto e’ pare più naturale agli uomini favorire sempre i principii delle cose

propositions.statement: One should weigh the forces of the malady: attack it without reserve only if sufficient to cure it, otherwise leave it alone entirely.
propositions.quote: Ma si debbano considerare bene le forze del malore, e quando ti vedi sufficiente a sanare quello, metterviti sanza rispetto; altrimenti lasciarlo stare, né in alcun modo tentarlo

episodes.description: Some forty neighboring peoples conspired against the rising Roman republic, which responded by creating the Dictator, an office that overcame the danger and benefited Rome thereafter.
episodes.quote: congiurarono bene quaranta popoli contro a Roma

episodes.description: Florentine citizens, ignoring Niccolò da Uzzano's counsel, moved openly against Cosimo de' Medici and expelled him, whereupon his party recalled him and made him prince of the republic.
episodes.quote: si feciono forti contro a Cosimo, e lo cacciorono da Firenze

episodes.description: Caesar's virtue, first favored by Pompey and others, turned into a source of fear too late, and the remedies attempted against him accelerated the ruin of the Roman republic.
episodes.quote: Pompeio aveva tardi cominciato a temere Cesare

heading_en: Dictatorial authority did good, not harm, to the Roman republic
thesis: The dictatorship, being given by public orders for a limited time and purpose, always benefited Rome; it was authority seized by citizens through prolonged commands, not freely granted magistracies, that enslaved the city.
thesis_quote: e’ non fu il nome né il grado del Dittatore che facesse serva Roma, ma fu l’autorità presa dai cittadini per la lunghezza dello imperio

propositions.statement: Magistracies and authorities created by extraordinary ways harm republics, not those that come by ordinary ways.
propositions.quote: e’ nuocono alle republiche i magistrati che si fanno e l’autoritadi che si dànno per vie istraordinarie, non quelle che vengono per vie ordinarie

propositions.statement: It is forces that easily acquire names, not names that acquire forces.
propositions.quote: e’ sono le forze che facilmente si acquistano i nomi, non i nomi le forze

propositions.statement: The dictator's short term, limited powers, and the uncorrupted Roman people made it impossible for him to exceed his bounds and harm the city.
propositions.quote: raccozzato il breve tempo della sua dittatura, e le autorità limitate che egli aveva, ed il popolo romano non corrotto; era impossibile ch’egli uscisse de’ termini suoi

propositions.statement: Republics that lack recourse to a dictator or similar emergency authority will always be ruined in grave emergencies, since ordinary institutions move too slowly.
propositions.quote: quelle republiche, le quali negli urgenti pericoli non hanno rifugio o al Dittatore o a simili autoritadi, sempre ne’ gravi accidenti rovineranno

episodes.description: Caesar, the first tyrant of Rome, commanded the city under the dictatorial title, which led some writers to blame the institution itself for Rome's tyranny.
episodes.quote: il primo tiranno che fosse in quella città la comandò sotto questo titolo dittatorio

episodes.description: The Venetian republic reserves authority to a few citizens who, in urgent needs, may decide in common accord without wider consultation.
episodes.quote: la Republica viniziana, la quale intra le moderne republiche è eccellente, ha riservato autorità a pochi cittadini

episodes.description: In later times the Romans, instead of naming a dictator, gave emergency authority to the consul with the formula 'Videat Consul, ne Respublica quid detrimenti capiat'.
episodes.quote: i Romani usassono, in cambio del Dittatore, di dare tale autorità al Console

notes: Includes the Latin formula of the senatus consultum ultimum, which postdates Livy's first decade narrative context.

heading_en: Why the creation of the Decemvirate harmed Roman liberty although freely elected
thesis: Even authority given by free public suffrage becomes dangerous when it is absolute, long in duration, and unguarded by other institutions, as the Decemvirate proved in contrast with the dictatorship.
thesis_quote: quando e’ si dia autorità libera, col tempo lungo, chiamando il tempo lungo uno anno o più, sempre fia pericolosa

propositions.statement: The dictator was kept good because the Senate, consuls, and tribunes retained their authority and stood as his guard, preventing him from leaving the straight path.
propositions.quote: il Senato, i Consoli, i Tribuni, restando con l’autorità loro, venivano a essere come sua guardia, a farlo non uscire della via diritta

propositions.statement: The Ten, left alone without consuls, tribunes, or appeal to the people, had no one to observe them and so could become insolent.
propositions.quote: trovandosi soli, sanza Consoli, sanza Tribuni, sanza appellagione al Popolo; e per questo non venendo ad avere chi gli osservasse

propositions.statement: An uncorrupted citizenry is no safeguard, because absolute authority corrupts the matter in a very short time and makes itself friends and partisans.
propositions.quote: una autorità assoluta in brevissimo tempo corrompe la materia e si fa amici e partigiani

episodes.description: The ten citizens elected by the Roman people to make laws became tyrants over time and seized the city's liberty without restraint, moved by the ambition of Appius in their second year.
episodes.quote: la elezione dei dieci cittadini creati dal Popolo romano per fare le leggi in Roma

notes: Sparta's kings and Venice's doges are cited as long-term authorities kept good by institutional guards; treated as institutional comparisons, not episodes.

heading_en: Citizens who have held higher honors should not disdain lesser ones
thesis: Roman greatness rested partly on citizens willingly obeying men they had once commanded and serving in armies they had led, a custom contrary to modern opinion, as in Venice, and vital to free government.
thesis_quote: non stimavano così disonorevole ubbidire ora a chi altra volta essi avevano comandato, e trovarsi a servire in quello esercito del quale erano stati principi

propositions.statement: A republic should place more hope in a citizen who descends from a great office to govern a lesser one than in one who rises from a lesser to a greater.
propositions.quote: più speranza debbe avere una republica, e più confidare in uno cittadino che da uno grado grande scenda a governare uno minore che in quello che da uno minore salga a governare uno maggiore

propositions.statement: Had Rome followed the Venetian custom that an ex-consul never serve except as consul, infinite harms to free life would have resulted from inexperienced and unchecked new men.
propositions.quote: che chi era stato una volta Consolo non volesse mai più andare negli eserciti se non Consolo, ne sarebbero nate infinite cose in disfavore del vivere libero

episodes.description: The consuls Marcus Fabius and Gnaeus Manilius won a most glorious battle against the Veientes and Etruscans, in which Quintus Fabius, consul the previous year, was killed serving under his brother.
episodes.quote: Avevano i Romani fatto Marco Fabio e G. Manilio consoli, e vinta una gloriosissima giornata contro a’ Veienti

heading_en: The scandals born in Rome from the agrarian law
thesis: The agrarian law, born of plebeian ambition once necessity was satisfied, convulsed Rome whenever raised and ultimately destroyed the republic, showing that retrospective laws against ancient customs are most scandalous.
thesis_quote: Da questo nacque il morbo che partorì la contenzione della legge agraria, che infine fu causa della distruzione della Republica

propositions.statement: Whenever men no longer fight from necessity, they fight from ambition, which never abandons them at any rank they reach.
propositions.quote: qualunque volta è tolto agli uomini il combattere per necessità, combattono per ambizione

propositions.statement: Because desire always exceeds the power of acquiring, men remain discontented with what they possess, which drives enmity and war and the variation of fortunes.
propositions.quote: essendo sempre maggiore il desiderio che la potenza dello acquistare, ne risulta la mala contentezza di quello che si possiede

propositions.statement: Well-ordered republics must keep the public treasury rich and their citizens poor.
propositions.quote: le republiche bene ordinate hanno a tenere ricco il publico e gli loro cittadini, poveri

propositions.statement: Making a law that reaches far back to remove a disorder already grown in a republic is ill-considered and only accelerates the evil, whereas temporizing delays or extinguishes it.
propositions.quote: a volere levar via uno disordine cresciuto in una republica, e per questo fare una legge che riguardi assai indietro, è partito male considerato

episodes.description: To defuse a dispute over the agrarian law, a colony was sent from Rome to the territory of Antium, and Livy notes that hardly anyone could be found to give his name to go.
episodes.quote: con difficultà si trovò in Roma chi desse il nome per ire in detta colonia

episodes.description: The agrarian law lay dormant until the Gracchi reawakened it, finding its opponents' power doubled, kindling such hatred between plebs and Senate that it came to arms and blood.
episodes.quote: questa legge stette come addormentata infino ai Gracchi; da’ quali essendo poi svegliata, rovinò al tutto la libertà romana

episodes.description: The plebs made Marius consul four times and the nobility, lacking other remedy, raised up Sulla as head of its party, leading to civil wars won by the nobility.
episodes.quote: e volse la sua riputazione a Mario tanto che la lo fece quattro volte consule

episodes.description: The same humors revived with Caesar heading Marius' party and Pompey Sulla's; Caesar prevailed and became Rome's first tyrant, so the city was never free again.
episodes.quote: fattosi Cesare capo della parte di Mario, e Pompeio di quella di Silla, venendo alle mani, rimase superiore Cesare

notes: Machiavelli explicitly names Tito Livio for the Antium colony remark; the specific chapter (Livy 3.1) is inferred, as he cites no book or chapter number.

heading_en: Weak republics are irresolute and decide only from necessity
thesis: Weak republics cannot resolve on doubtful courses and take good decisions only when forced, unlike the Roman Senate, which knew how to make a virtue of necessity and keep authority over its own deliberations.
thesis_quote: le republiche inresolute non pigliono mai partiti buoni, se non per forza, perché la debolezza loro non le lascia mai deliberare dove è alcuno dubbio

propositions.statement: By licensing what its allies would do anyway, the Senate ensured that having disobeyed from necessity they would not grow accustomed to disobeying from choice.
propositions.quote: acciocché, avendo disubbidito per necessità, non si avvezzassero a disubbidire per elezione

propositions.statement: A prudent government always judges things as they should be judged and takes the least bad course as the best.
propositions.quote: sempre giudicò le cose come si debbano giudicare, e sempre prese il meno reo partito per migliore

propositions.statement: Had Beaumont acted like Imbalt and accepted the surrender on his own terms, Florence would have had Pisa as it had Arezzo.
propositions.quote: se Beumonte fosse stato simile a Imbalt, si sarebbe avuto Pisa come Arezzo

episodes.description: During a grave pestilence in Rome, the Volsci and Aequi attacked the Latins and Hernici, and the Senate, unable to defend them, authorized them to arm and defend themselves.
episodes.quote: risposero che pigliassero partito di difendersi da loro medesimi e con le loro armi

episodes.description: Duke Valentino, after taking Faenza and bending Bologna to his terms, sent to Florence to demand passage for himself and his army, and the irresolute Florentines handled it dishonorably.
episodes.quote: mandò in Firenze uno suo uomo a domandare il passo per sé e per lo esercito suo

episodes.description: In 1500 Pisan envoys offered Beaumont the city for the French army under promise of a four-month delay before handover to Florence; the Florentines refused out of distrust and the siege ended in shame.
episodes.quote: vennono oratori Pisani a Beumonte, e gli offerirono di dare la città allo esercito francese

episodes.description: In 1502, after Florence refused a similar accord with rebellious Arezzo, monsignor Imbalt concluded it himself without the Florentine commissioners and entered Arezzo with his troops.
episodes.quote: cominciò a tenere le pratiche dello accordo da sé, sanza partecipazione de’ Commessari

notes: Livy candidate for the pestilence episode (3.6) based on the pestilence and the Hernici/Latini appeal; medium certainty on exact chapter.

heading_en: The same accidents are often seen among different peoples
thesis: Since all cities and peoples have the same desires and humors in every age, whoever diligently examines past events can foresee the future in any republic and apply the remedies the ancients used.
thesis_quote: in tutte le città ed in tutti i popoli sono quegli medesimi desiderii e quelli medesimi omori, e come vi furono sempre

propositions.statement: Whoever diligently examines past things can foresee future ones in every republic and apply the remedies used by the ancients or devise new ones from the similarity of events.
propositions.quote: gli è facil cosa, a chi esamina con diligenza le cose passate, prevedere in ogni republica le future, e farvi quegli rimedi che dagli antichi sono stati usati

propositions.statement: Because these considerations are neglected by readers and unknown to rulers, the same scandals recur in every age.
propositions.quote: queste considerazioni sono neglette, o non intese da chi legge, o, se le sono intese, non sono conosciute da chi governa

episodes.description: After 1494 Florence, blaming the Dieci della guerra for its costly war to recover Pisa, let the magistracy lapse, lost Arezzo and other places, and then recognized the fever, not the physician, was the cause and restored the Ten.
episodes.quote: ravvedutosi il popolo dello errore suo, e come la cagione del male era la febbre e non il medico, rifece il magistrato de’ Dieci

episodes.description: The tribune Terentillus first proposed a law to create five men to examine and limit the consuls' power, greatly alarming the nobility.
episodes.quote: Il primo che tentò questa legge, fu uno Terentillo tribuno

episodes.description: The tribunes' obstinacy extinguished the consular name and Rome created tribunes with consular power instead, hating the name more than the authority, until the error was recognized and consuls were restored.
episodes.quote: più tosto creare Tribuni con potestà consolare, che Consoli: tanto avevano più in odio il nome che l’autorità loro

heading_en: The creation of the Decemvirate in Rome and what is notable in it
thesis: The Decemvirate shows how republics are lost: when people and nobles, instead of agreeing on a law for liberty, each favor one man to crush the other side, tyranny immediately arises.
thesis_quote: E quando e’ non convengano a fare una legge in favore della libertà, ma gettasi qualcuna delle parti a favorire uno, allora è che subito la tirannide surge

propositions.statement: Most tyrannies in cities are born from the people's excessive desire to be free and the nobles' excessive desire to command.
propositions.quote: questo è da troppo desiderio del popolo, d’essere libero, e da troppo desiderio de’ nobili, di comandare

propositions.statement: When a people gives reputation to a shrewd man so that he may beat those it hates, he will always become tyrant of that city.
propositions.quote: quando uno popolo si conduce a fare questo errore, di dare riputazione a uno, perché batta quelli che egli ha in odio, e che quello uno sia savio, sempre interverrà ch’e’ diventerà tiranno di quella città

propositions.statement: Tyrants who have the populace as friend and the great as enemies are more secure, their violence being sustained by greater forces.
propositions.quote: quegli tiranni che hanno amico l’universale ed inimici i grandi, sono più sicuri, per essere la loro violenza sostenuta da maggiori forze

propositions.statement: To hold anything by violence, the one who forces must be more powerful than the one who is forced.
propositions.quote: a volere con violenza tenere una cosa, bisogna che sia più potente chi sforza che chi è sforzato

episodes.description: Rome sent Spurius Postumius with two other citizens to Athens for copies of the laws Solon gave that city, as a foundation for the Roman laws.
episodes.quote: mandarono, d’accordo, Spurio Pestumio, con duoi altri Cittadini, a Atene

episodes.description: Ten citizens, among them the shrewd and restless Appius Claudius, were created for a year to make the laws, with all other magistracies removed and appeal to the people abolished.
episodes.quote: crearono dieci cittadini per uno anno, intra i quali fu creato Appio Claudio, uomo sagace ed inquieto

episodes.description: Entrusted with proposing the next Ten, Appius seized the impediment as an opportunity and named himself among the first, to the amazement and displeasure of the nobles.
episodes.quote: nominò sé intra i primi, con maraviglia e dispiacere di tutti i nobili

episodes.description: The second Decemvirate showed its pride, beating plebs and Senate alike, and to terrify them increased the lictors from twelve to one hundred twenty.
episodes.quote: in cambio di dodici littori, ne feciono cento venti

episodes.description: War moved by the Sabines and Volsci forced the Ten to convene the Senate, where Valerius and Horatius spoke against their pride.
episodes.quote: i Sabini ed i Volsci mossero guerra a’ Romani

episodes.description: Appius fell in love with Virginia and tried to take her by force; her father Virginius killed her to free her, provoking tumults in Rome and the armies, secession to the Monte Sacro, and the fall of the Ten.
episodes.quote: si innamorò di Virginia, e che, volendola tôrre per forza, il padre Virginio, per liberarla, l’ammazzò

episodes.description: Nabis, tyrant of Sparta, having secured himself against a few nobles and holding the people as friend, defended himself when all Greece and the Roman people assaulted him.
episodes.quote: come bastarono a Nabide, tiranno di Sparta, quando tutta Grecia e il Popolo romano lo assaltò

notes: Contains several unattributed verbatim Latin quotations from Livy (e.g. 'haud gratuitam in tanta superbia comitatem fore', Livy 3.35; 'et inde libertatis captare auram', Livy 3.37) without naming him. Also cites a saying of King Ferrando comparing men to lesser birds of prey.

heading_en: To leap from humility to pride, from mercy to cruelty, without due degrees is imprudent and useless
thesis: Appius' sudden change from friend of the plebs to its proud enemy, made without due intermediate steps, stripped him of old supporters before gaining new ones and ruined his tyranny.
thesis_quote: chi è paruto buono un tempo, e vuole a suo proposito diventar cattivo, lo debbe fare per i debiti mezzi

propositions.statement: One who changes nature must manage occasions so that new favors are gained before the changed nature strips away the old ones, lest authority diminish.
propositions.quote: innanzi che la diversa natura ti tolga de’ favori vecchi, la te ne abbia dati tanti de’ nuovi, che tu non venga a diminuire la tua autorità

propositions.statement: Changing so fast that everyone must recognize the falsity of your mind leaves you discovered and friendless, and you are ruined.
propositions.quote: e farlo tanto presto, che, sanza scusa niuna, ogni uomo avesse a conoscere la fallacia dello animo suo

episodes.description: Appius, having skillfully simulated popularity to win the plebs and secure his reappointment, suddenly changed nature, showing himself the plebs' enemy, proud instead of humane, so that everyone saw his deceit.
episodes.quote: mutare, in uno subito, natura; e, di amico, mostrarsi inimico alla plebe; di umano, superbo

heading_en: How easily men may be corrupted
thesis: The Decemvirate shows how easily even good and well-educated men are corrupted and made of contrary nature by a little ambition or utility, which lawgivers must anticipate.
thesis_quote: quanto facilmente gli uomini si corrompono, e fannosi diventare di contraria natura, quantunque buoni e bene ammaestrati

propositions.statement: However good and well-trained, men are easily corrupted and made to assume a contrary nature.
propositions.quote: quanto facilmente gli uomini si corrompono, e fannosi diventare di contraria natura, quantunque buoni e bene ammaestrati

propositions.statement: Lawgivers of republics and kingdoms should therefore be readier to bridle human appetites and remove all hope of erring with impunity.
propositions.quote: farà tanto più pronti i latori di leggi delle republiche o de’ regni a frenare gli appetiti umani, e tôrre loro ogni speranza di potere impune errare

episodes.description: The young nobles Appius gathered around himself became friends of the tyranny for a little profit that came to them from it.
episodes.quote: quella gioventù che Appio si aveva eletta intorno, cominciò a essere amica della tirannide per uno poco di utilità

episodes.description: Quintus Fabius, one of the second Ten and an excellent man, blinded by a little ambition and persuaded by Appius' malignity, changed his good habits into the worst and became like him.
episodes.quote: Quinto Fabio, uno del numero de’ secondi Dieci, sendo uomo ottimo, accecato da uno poco d’ambizione

heading_en: Those who fight for their own glory are good and faithful soldiers
thesis: Armies content and fighting for their own glory conquer, while those fighting for another's ambition fail, which explains the uselessness of mercenary soldiers and the need to arm one's own subjects.
thesis_quote: quanta differenzia è da uno esercito contento e che combatte per la gloria sua, a quello che è male disposto e che combatte per l’ambizione d’altrui

propositions.statement: Mercenary soldiers, held only by a little stipend, can never be faithful enough or friendly enough to die for their employer.
propositions.quote: i quali non hanno altra cagione che gli tenga fermi, che un poco di stipendio che tu dai loro

propositions.statement: To hold a state, whether republic or kingdom, it is necessary to arm oneself with one's own subjects.
propositions.quote: è necessario, a volere tenere uno stato, a volere mantenere una republica o uno regno, armarsi de’ sudditi suoi

episodes.description: The Roman armies, always victorious under the consuls, always lost under the Decemvirs, and regained their old spirit and success as soon as the Ten were removed and they fought as free men.
episodes.quote: dove gli eserciti romani solevano sempre essere vittoriosi sotto i Consoli, sotto i Decemviri sempre perderono

heading_en: A multitude without a head is useless, and one should not threaten before having the power
thesis: The plebs on the Monte Sacro shows that a multitude without a head is useless, and that it is folly to announce the harm you intend before obtaining the authority or means to do it.
thesis_quote: La qual cosa dimostra appunto la inutilità d’una moltitudine sanza capo

propositions.statement: It is foolishness and imprudence to demand a thing while first declaring the evil one intends to do with it.
propositions.quote: quanta stultizia e poca prudenza è domandare una cosa, e dire prima: io voglio fare il tale male con essa

propositions.statement: One should not show one's mind but seek to obtain one's desire by any means, for having the arms in hand one can then satisfy the appetite.
propositions.quote: non si debbe mostrare l’animo suo, ma vuolsi cercare di ottenere quel suo desiderio in ogni modo

episodes.description: The armed plebs on the Monte Sacro, having no heads, dared not answer the Senate's ambassadors until Virginius had twenty military tribunes created as their chiefs to negotiate.
episodes.quote: per suo ordine si creò venti Tribuni militari, che fossero loro capi, a rispondere e convenire col Senato

episodes.description: The plebs demanded of Valerius and Horatius the restoration of tribunes and appeal, but also that the Ten be handed over to be burned alive, which the envoys condemned as impious.
episodes.quote: che si dessono loro tutti i Dieci che gli volevono ardere vivi

notes: Machiavelli explicitly cites Tito Livio ('E Tito Livio dice') for the observation that the plebs lacked not matter but a spokesman; includes the Latin 'Crudelitatem damnatis, in crudelitatem ruitis'.

heading_en: It is a bad example not to observe a law, above all by its author; and daily renewed injuries are most harmful to a ruler
thesis: Nothing sets a worse example in a republic than making a law and not observing it, especially by its author; and keeping subjects fearful with continually renewed injuries is most damaging to whoever governs.
thesis_quote: io non credo che sia cosa di più cattivo esemplo in una republica, che fare una legge e non la osservare; e tanto più, quanto la non è osservata da chi l’ha fatta

propositions.statement: It is most harmful for a republic or prince to keep subjects' minds suspended and fearful with continual penalties and offenses.
propositions.quote: quanto sia dannoso a una republica o a un principe, tenere con le continove pene ed offese sospesi e paurosi gli animi de’ sudditi

propositions.statement: Men who begin to fear coming to harm secure themselves in dangers in any way they can, becoming bolder and less restrained in attempting new things.
propositions.quote: gli uomini che cominciono a dubitare di avere a capitare male, in ogni modo si assicurano ne’ pericoli, e diventono più audaci, e meno respettivi a tentare cose nuove

propositions.statement: One must either never injure anyone or do the injuries all at one stroke, and then reassure men and give them cause to quiet and settle their minds.
propositions.quote: è necessario o non offendere mai alcuno, o fare le offese a un tratto: e dipoi rassicurare gli uomini

episodes.description: Virginius cited Appius before the people; denied the appeal he himself had destroyed, Appius was imprisoned and killed himself before the day of judgment, though violating the new law of appeal was itself uncivil.
episodes.quote: egli fu incarcerato, ed avanti al dì del giudizio ammazzò se stesso

episodes.description: In post-1494 Florence, Savonarola's hard-won law of appeal to the people was broken when the Signoria condemned five citizens to death for state reasons and denied their appeal, costing the friar his reputation.
episodes.quote: furono condannati a morte dalla Signoria, per conto di stato, cinque cittadini; e volendo quegli appellare, non furono lasciati

episodes.description: After the Decemvirate, continual accusations terrified the whole nobility until the tribune Marcus Duellius decreed that for one year no Roman citizen could be cited or accused, reassuring them.
episodes.quote: fece uno editto, che per uno anno non fusse lecito a alcuno citare o accusare alcuno cittadino romano

heading_en: Men rise from one ambition to another
thesis: Men climb from one ambition to the next: first they seek only security from offense, then they offend others; in defending themselves from fear they make themselves feared, so republics dissolve as each side oppresses the other.
thesis_quote: mentre che gli uomini cercono di non temere, cominciono a fare temere altrui; e quella ingiuria che gli scacciano da loro, la pongono sopra un altro

propositions.statement: Ambitious citizens first secure themselves against offense by acquiring friends through apparently honest means—money and protection—which deceives everyone and prevents any remedy.
propositions.quote: cercono, per poter fare questo, amicizie; e quelle acquistano per vie in apparenza oneste, o con sovvenire di danari, o con difenderli da’ potenti

propositions.statement: Once such a citizen has grown great unopposed, the city must either crush him at risk of sudden ruin or slide into open servitude.
propositions.quote: bisogna, o cercare di spegnerlo con pericolo d’una subita rovina, o, lasciandolo fare, entrare in una servitù manifesta

propositions.statement: A republic should order itself so as to watch that citizens cannot do evil under the shadow of good, and that their reputation helps rather than harms liberty.
propositions.quote: una republica intra gli ordini suoi debbe avere questo, di vegghiare che i suoi cittadini, sotto ombra di bene non possino fare male

episodes.description: After the plebs recovered its liberty from the decemvirs, new tumults arose: young nobles began injuring the quiet plebs and the tribunes could offer few remedies, each side oppressing the other in defending its liberty.
episodes.quote: stando la plebe quieta intra i termini suoi, cominciarono i giovani nobili a ingiuriarla; ed i Tribuni vi potevon fare pochi rimedi

notes: Machiavelli explicitly paraphrases Livy's words (Livy 3.65: 'cavendo ne metuant, homines metuendos ultro se efficiunt') and quotes Sallust's sentence placed in Caesar's mouth ('quod omnia mala exempla bonis initiis orta sunt').

heading_en: Men deceive themselves in generalities, not in particulars
thesis: Though men deceive themselves in general matters, they do not deceive themselves in particulars: the people, judging specific men and cases, corrects errors it makes when judging in the abstract.
thesis_quote: gli uomini nelle cose generali s’ingannono assai, nelle particulari non tanto

propositions.statement: Peoples deceive themselves generally in judging things and events, but once they come to know them in particular the deception vanishes.
propositions.quote: Ingannonsi, oltra di questo, i popoli generalmente nel giudicare le cose e gli accidenti di esse; le quali, dipoi si conoscono particularmente, mancano di tale inganno

propositions.statement: A prudent man should never flee popular judgment in particular matters such as the distribution of offices and dignities, for there the people is rarely deceived.
propositions.quote: mai un uomo prudente non debba fuggire il giudicio populare nelle cose particulari, circa le distribuzioni de’ gradi e delle dignità

propositions.statement: When a generality deceives the people, their eyes can quickly be opened by finding a way to make them descend to particulars.
propositions.quote: si può fare tosto aprire gli occhi a’ popoli, trovando modo, veggendo che uno generale gl’inganna, ch’egli abbino a discendere a’ particulari

episodes.description: When tribunes with consular power open to plebeians were first elected, the Roman people, though able to choose all plebeians, elected all nobles.
episodes.quote: venendosi alla creazione di questi Tribuni, e potendosi creare tutti plebei, furono dal Popolo romano creati tutti nobili

episodes.description: After Cannae, Pacuvius Calavius in Capua reconciled the plebs with the Senate by locking up the senators and inviting the people to replace each one, whereupon the people found every proposed substitute unworthy.
episodes.quote: trovandosi in quel tempo nel supremo magistrato Pacuvio Calano, e conoscendo il pericolo che portava quella città di tumultuare

episodes.description: After 1494 Florentine populars blamed ambitious magnates for the city's disorders, but whenever one of them reached the supreme magistracy and saw things closely, he changed his mind—whence the proverb that they had one mind in the piazza and another in the palazzo.
episodes.quote: Dopo il 1494, sendo stati i principi della città cacciati da Firenze, e non vi essendo alcuno governo ordinato

notes: Two verbatim Latin quotations from Livy 4.6 appear in the chapter. The Capua episode corresponds to Livy 23.2-4, outside the books in the local Livy corpus (1-10), so no candidate is given.

heading_en: Keeping magistracies from vile men
thesis: He who does not want a magistracy given to a vile or wicked man should have it requested either by someone exceedingly vile and wicked or by someone exceedingly noble and good, so that the people is shamed into choosing well.
thesis_quote: Chi vuole che uno magistrato non sia dato a uno vile o a uno cattivo, lo facci domandare o a uno troppo vile e troppo cattivo o a uno troppo nobile e troppo buono

propositions.statement: Having a base candidate stand shames the plebs into not giving the office; having a most reputed man stand shames it into not taking the office for itself.
propositions.quote: Questo ultimo modo faceva che la plebe si vergognava a darlo; quel primo faceva che la si vergognava a torlo

propositions.statement: The people, though it deceives itself in generalities, does not deceive itself in particulars.
propositions.quote: il popolo, se s’inganna de’ generali, de’ particulari non s’inganna

episodes.description: When the Senate feared that tribunes with consular power would go to plebeians, it either had the most reputed Romans stand for the office or corrupted some ignoble plebeian to stand alongside the better plebeian candidates.
episodes.quote: Quando il Senato dubitava che i Tribuni con potestà consolare non fussero fatti d’uomini plebei, teneva uno de’ due modi

notes: Very short chapter; a corollary of chapter 47 on electoral practice.

heading_en: Servile-born cities can hardly order themselves free
thesis: If cities born free like Rome struggle to find laws that keep them free, cities born in servitude, like Florence, find it nearly impossible ever to order themselves so as to live civilly and quietly.
thesis_quote: se quelle città che hanno avuto il principio loro libero, e che per sé medesimo si è retto, come Roma, hanno difficultà grande a trovare leggi buone per mantenerle libere

propositions.statement: Cities whose beginnings were immediately servile face not merely difficulty but impossibility in ever ordering themselves to live civilly and quietly.
propositions.quote: quelle città che hanno avuto il principio loro immediate servo, abbino, non che difficultà, ma impossibilità a ordinarsi mai in modo che le possino vivere civilmente e quietamente

propositions.statement: An orderer of a republic must examine into whose hands he places the authority over the blood of its citizens.
propositions.quote: intra le altre cose che si hanno a considerare da uno ordinatore d’una republica è esaminare nelle mani di quali uomini ei ponga l’autorità del sangue contro de’ suoi cittadini

propositions.statement: When capital authority is placed in the hands of a few citizens, the few are always ministers of the few and of the most powerful.
propositions.quote: i pochi furono sempre ministri de’ pochi, e de’ più potenti

episodes.description: Rome created the censors to guard its morals, first for five-year terms; the dictator Mamercus by a new law reduced the office to eighteen months, and the offended censors expelled him from the Senate without remedy.
episodes.quote: fu corretto dalla prudenza di Mamerco dittatore, il quale per nuova legge ridusse detto magistrato a diciotto mesi

episodes.description: Florence, born subject to the Roman Empire and long governed by others, has managed itself for the two hundred years of true memory without ever attaining a state that could truly be called a republic.
episodes.quote: è ita maneggiandosi, per dugento anni che si ha di vera memoria, sanza avere mai avuto stato, per il quale la possa veramente essere chiamata republica

episodes.description: Venice guards against corrupt capital justice with the Ten who punish any citizen without appeal, reinforced by the Quarantia and the Council of the Pregadi to curb the powerful.
episodes.quote: ha dieci cittadini, che, sanza appello, possono punire ogni cittadino

notes: Mentions the lawgiving of Romulus, Numa, Tullus Hostilius, Servius and the decemvirs as background. 'La istoria' is invoked but Livy is not named.

heading_en: No council or magistrate should be able to halt the city's business
thesis: No single council or magistrate should be able to halt the public actions of a city: whoever holds a necessary deliberation must be compelled to perform it, or another must be empowered to perform it in his place.
thesis_quote: mai si debbe ordinare in una città, che i pochi possino tenere alcuna diliberazione di quelle che ordinariamente sono necessarie a mantenere la republica

propositions.statement: If a council or magistrate is given a necessary public function, one must either impose a necessity that it be done in any case or order that, if he will not do it, another can and must.
propositions.quote: conviene o imporgli una necessità perché ci l’abbia a fare in ogni modo, o ordinare, quando non la voglia fare egli, che la possa e debba fare uno altro

propositions.statement: The tribunate was useful not only to check the ambition the powerful used against the plebs, but also that which they used among themselves.
propositions.quote: il quale non era solo utile a frenare l’ambizione che i potenti usavano contro alla Plebe, ma quella ancora ch’egli usavano infra loro

episodes.description: The disunited consuls Titus Quinctius Cincinnatus and Gnaeus Julius Mento halted all actions of the republic and refused to name a dictator, until the Senate resorted to the tribunes, who forced the consuls to obey.
episodes.quote: il Senato, non avendo altro rimedio, ricorse allo aiuto de’ Tribuni; i quali, con l’autorità del Senato, sforzarono i Consoli a ubbidire

episodes.description: The Venetian Great Council sometimes refused out of disdain to elect successors to magistrates at home and abroad, until prudent citizens passed a law that no magistracy should ever fall vacant until successors were chosen.
episodes.quote: fecero una legge, che tutti i magistrati che sono o fusseno dentro e fuori della città, mai vacassero, se non quando fussono fatti gli scambi e i successori loro

heading_en: Appear liberal in what necessity compels
thesis: A republic or prince should make a show of doing out of liberality what necessity in any case compels, thereby earning gratitude for the unavoidable.
thesis_quote: Una republica o uno principe debbe mostrare di fare per liberalità quello a che la necessità lo constringe

propositions.statement: Prudent men always make a merit of their actions, even those that necessity would have compelled them to do in any case.
propositions.quote: Gli uomini prudenti si fanno grado delle cose sempre e in ogni loro azione, ancora che la necessità gli constringesse a farle in ogni modo

episodes.description: The Roman Senate, needing longer campaigns and sieges, decreed public pay for soldiers who had served at their own expense, presenting necessity as a gift; the plebs rejoiced, the tribunes failed to discredit it, and the Senate taxed the nobility first and most heavily.
episodes.quote: diliberò, che si desse il soldo del publico agli uomini che militavano, essendo consueti militare del loro proprio

heading_en: Preempt the roads by which a rising man gains power
thesis: The safest and least scandalous way to repress the insolence of one rising to power in a republic is to preoccupy in advance the ways by which he climbs to that power.
thesis_quote: non si può in una republica, e massime in quelle che sono corrotte, con miglior modo, meno scandoloso e più facile, opporsi all’ambizione di alcuno cittadino, che preoccupandogli quelle vie

propositions.statement: Had Cosimo's rivals adopted his own style of favoring the people, they would have disarmed him without tumult or violence.
propositions.quote: se quegli cittadini che gareggiavano seco avessero preso lo stile suo, di favorire il popolo, gli venivano, sanza tumulto e sanza violenza, a trarre di mano quelle armi di che egli si valeva più

propositions.statement: In every course of action men should weigh its defects and dangers, and not adopt it when it holds more danger than utility.
propositions.quote: Debbono, pertanto, gli uomini in ogni partito considerare i difetti ed i pericoli di quello, e non gli prendere, quando vi sia più del pericoloso che dell’utile

episodes.description: Cosimo de' Medici's adversaries expelled him from Florence instead of preempting the popular favor on which his power rested, a worse course that led to their ruin.
episodes.quote: Il quale modo se fusse stato usato contro a Cosimo de’ Medici, sarebbe stato miglior partito assai per gli suoi avversari, che cacciarlo da Firenze

episodes.description: Piero Soderini built his reputation in Florence solely by favoring the generality of citizens; his envious rivals could more safely have taken over his methods than opposed him at the republic's peril.
episodes.quote: Piero Soderini si aveva fatto riputazione nella città di Firenze con questo solo, di favorire l’universale

episodes.description: Cicero, seeking to strip Mark Antony of his soldiers, urged the Senate to raise up Octavian against him; instead Octavian allied with Antony, destroying the party of the optimates.
episodes.quote: Tullio, per torgli questi soldati, confortò il Senato a dare riputazione ad Ottaviano, e mandarlo con Irzio e Pansa consoli contro a Marc’Antonio

notes: The Cicero-Octavian episode belongs to the lost later books of Livy/other sources; no candidate possible from the Livy 1-10 corpus.

heading_en: The people, deceived by a false good, desires its own ruin
thesis: The people, deceived by a false appearance of good, often desires its own ruin, and is easily moved by great hopes and brave promises, while courses that look timid or losing cannot be sold to it even when salvation lies hidden in them.
thesis_quote: il popolo molte volte, ingannato da una falsa immagine di bene, disidera la rovina sua

propositions.statement: Proposals that show gain on their face, or that seem spirited, are always easy to persuade a multitude of, even when loss or the republic's ruin lies hidden beneath.
propositions.quote: quando nelle cose che si mettono innanzi al popolo, si vede guadagno, ancora che vi sia nascosto sotto perdita; e quando e’ pare animoso, ancora che vi sia nascosto sotto la rovina della republica, sempre sarà facile persuaderlo alla moltitudine

propositions.statement: There is no easier way to ruin a republic where the people has authority than to set it upon bold enterprises.
propositions.quote: non è la più facile via a fare rovinare una republica dove il popolo abbia autorità, che metterla in imprese gagliarde

propositions.statement: Having presupposed victory, the people blames defeat not on fortune or the commander's weakness but on his malice and ignorance, and kills, imprisons, or banishes him.
propositions.quote: avendosi il popolo presupposto la vittoria, come ei viene la perdita, non ne accusa né la fortuna né la impotenzia di chi ha governato, ma la malvagità e ignoranza sua

episodes.description: After the capture of Veii the Roman plebs embraced the opinion that half of Rome should migrate there, and nearly came to arms against the Senate until the reverence of grave citizens restrained it.
episodes.quote: entrò nel popolo romano un’opinione, che fosse cosa utile per la città di Roma, che la metà de’ Romani andasse ad abitare a Veio

episodes.description: Fabius Maximus could not persuade the Roman people that proceeding slowly against Hannibal was useful, since the people judged that course cowardly, and his master of horse was given authority to fight.
episodes.quote: non poteva persuadere al Popolo romano, che fusse utile a quella Republica procedere lentamente in quella guerra, e sostenere sanza azzuffarsi l’impeto d’Annibale

episodes.description: Varro was made consul only for having promised in all the public places of Rome to crush Hannibal, from which followed the battle and rout of Cannae and almost the ruin of Rome.
episodes.quote: fece di poi consule Varrone, non per altri suoi meriti che per avere, per tutte le piazze e tutti i luoghi publici di Roma, promesso di rompere Annibale

episodes.description: Marcus Centenius Penula, a most vile man, obtained from the wary Senate authority to raise volunteers against Hannibal and was routed and killed with all his followers.
episodes.quote: venne in Senato Marco Centenio Penula, uomo vilissimo (nondimanco aveva avuto qualche grado nella milizia)

episodes.description: In Athens the grave and prudent Nicias could not dissuade the people from assaulting Sicily, a decision taken against the wise that brought Athens' total ruin.
episodes.quote: non potette mai Nicia, uomo gravissimo e prudentissimo, persuadere a quel Popolo che non fusse bene andare a assaltare Sicilia

episodes.description: Scipio, made consul and desiring the province of Africa while promising Carthage's ruin, threatened to take the proposal to the people when the Senate balked on Fabius Maximus' advice.
episodes.quote: Scipione, quando fu fatto consolo, e che desiderava la provincia di Africa, promettendo al tutto la rovina di Cartagine

episodes.description: Venice, assaulted by many enemies, could not bring itself to buy off any of them by restoring what it had taken, before its ruin came.
episodes.quote: assaltati da tanti inimici, non poterono prendere partito di guadagnarsene alcuno con la restituzione delle cose tolte ad altri

episodes.description: On Ercole Bentivoglio's brave promises the Florentine people decreed the camp against Pisa despite wise citizens' blame; after the failure Antonio Giacomini fell into such popular disgrace that he survived only by the humanity of those in power.
episodes.quote: andarono a campo a Pisa la quale impresa fu diliberata dal popolo in su le promesse gagliarde di messere Ercole

notes: Cites Dante's De Monarchia ('Viva la sua morte! e Muoia la sua vita!'). Fabius/Varro/Cannae (Livy 22), Centenius (Livy 25) and Scipio (Livy 28) fall outside the Livy 1-10 corpus, so no candidates are given.

heading_en: A grave man can restrain an excited multitude
thesis: Nothing is so apt to restrain an excited multitude as the reverence inspired by some grave man of authority who comes before it.
thesis_quote: veruna cosa è tanto atta a frenare una moltitudine concitata, quanto è la riverenzia di qualche uomo grave e di autorità, che se le faccia incontro

propositions.statement: Whoever commands an army or finds himself in a city where tumult arises should present himself with the greatest grace and honor, wearing the insignia of his rank to make himself more revered.
propositions.quote: quello che è preposto a uno esercito, o quello che si trova in una città, dove nascesse tumulto debba rappresentarsi in su quello con maggiore grazia e più onorevolmente che può

propositions.statement: There is no firmer or more necessary remedy to restrain an excited multitude than the presence of a man who by his bearing appears and is worthy of reverence.
propositions.quote: e’ non è il più fermo né il più necessario rimedio a frenare una moltitudine concitata, che la presenzia d’uno uomo che per presenzia paia e sia riverendo

episodes.description: When the armed Florentine mob of the Arrabbiati came to sack Pagolantonio Soderini's house, his brother Francesco, bishop of Volterra, put on his most honorable robes and episcopal rochet and halted them with his presence and words.
episodes.quote: messosi i più onorevoli panni indosso, e di sopra il roccetto episcopale, si fece incontro a quegli armati, e con la presenzia e con le parole gli fermò

episodes.description: The Roman plebs obstinately embraced the plan of migrating to Veii, judging it useful and not seeing the harm beneath, until the Senate restrained its fury with grave and revered men.
episodes.quote: con quanta ostinazione la plebe romana accettava quel partito d’andare a Veio, perché lo giudicava utile, né vi conosceva, sotto, il danno vi era

notes: Quotes Virgil, Aeneid 1.151-152 ('Tum pietate gravem ac meritis...'). Continues the Veii-migration text discussed in chapter 53.

heading_en: Where equality, no principality; where inequality, no republic
thesis: Public affairs are easily managed where the multitude is not corrupt; where equality reigns no principality can be made, and where great inequality reigns no republic can be made.
thesis_quote: dove è equalità, non si può fare principato; e dove la non è, non si può fare republica

propositions.statement: Gentlemen are those who live idly and abundantly off the revenues of their possessions without any care for cultivation or other necessary labor; they are pernicious in every republic.
propositions.quote: gentiluomini sono chiamati quelli che oziosi vivono delle rendite delle loro possessioni abbondantemente, sanza avere cura alcuna o di coltivazione o di altra necessaria fatica a vivere

propositions.statement: Whoever wants to make a republic where there are many gentlemen cannot do so unless he first extinguishes them all.
propositions.quote: colui che vuole fare dove sono assai gentiluomini una republica, non la può fare se prima non gli spegne tutti

propositions.statement: Where the matter is so corrupt that laws do not suffice to restrain it, a greater force must be ordered along with them: a kingly hand with absolute and excessive power to bridle the excessive ambition and corruption of the powerful.
propositions.quote: dove è tanto la materia corrotta che le leggi non bastano a frenarla, vi bisogna ordinare insieme con quelle maggior forza; la quale è una mano regia

episodes.description: To satisfy Camillus' vow of a tenth of the Veientine spoils to Apollo, the Senate issued an edict that each man present publicly a tenth of his plunder, trusting wholly in the plebs' goodness.
episodes.quote: fece il Senato uno editto, che ciascuno dovessi rappresentare in publico la decima parte di quello ch’egli aveva predato

episodes.description: In the German republics citizens assess their own taxes, swearing an oath and throwing into a chest what conscience tells them they owe, with no witness but the payer—proof of surviving ancient goodness.
episodes.quote: preso prima il giuramento di pagare la conveniente somma, getta in una cassa a ciò diputata quello che secondo la conscienza sua gli pare dovere pagare

episodes.description: In Tuscany three republics—Florence, Siena and Lucca—have long existed in a small space because the province has no lords of castles and few or no gentlemen, but great equality.
episodes.quote: si vede in poco spazio di terreno state lungamente tre republiche, Firenze, Siena e Lucca

episodes.description: Venice does not contradict the rule, for its gentlemen are such more in name than in fact, their wealth resting on trade and movables, with no castles or jurisdiction over men.
episodes.quote: i gentiluomini in quella Republica sono più in nome che in fatto; perché loro non hanno grandi entrate di possessioni

notes: The German-cities episode concerns contemporary Germany (1500s); the period label 'contemporary-italy' is used here for Machiavelli's own era. The tithe edict appears in Livy 5.23 (also treated in 5.25).

heading_en: Great events are preceded by signs and prophecies
thesis: Before great events befall a city or province, signs come that prognosticate them, or men who predict them—whether by diviners, revelations, prodigies, or other celestial signs.
thesis_quote: mai non venne alcuno grave accidente in una città o in una provincia, che non sia stato, o da indovini o da rivelazioni o da prodigi o da altri segni celesti, predetto

propositions.statement: After such signs, extraordinary and new things always befall the provinces.
propositions.quote: sempre dopo tali accidenti sopravvengono cose istraordinarie e nuove alle provincie

propositions.statement: Perhaps, as some philosophers hold, the air is full of intelligences which foresee future things by natural powers and, out of compassion, warn men with such signs so they may prepare their defenses.
propositions.quote: potrebbe essere che, sendo questo aere, come vuole alcuno filosofo, pieno di intelligenze, le quali per naturali virtù preveggendo le cose future, ed avendo compassione agli uomini, acciò si possino preparare alle difese, gli avvertiscono con simili segni

episodes.description: Friar Girolamo Savonarola predicted the coming of King Charles VIII of France into Italy before it happened.
episodes.quote: sa ciascuno quanto da frate Girolamo Savonerola fosse predetta innanzi la venuta del re Carlo VIII di Francia in Italia

episodes.description: Throughout Tuscany it was said that men-at-arms were heard and seen in the air above Arezzo, fighting one another.
episodes.quote: per tutta Toscana si disse essere sentite in aria e vedute genti d’armi, sopra Arezzo, che si azzuffavano insieme

episodes.description: Before the death of Lorenzo de' Medici the elder, the cathedral of Florence was struck at its highest point by a celestial bolt with very great ruin to the building.
episodes.quote: avanti alla morte di Lorenzo de’ Medici vecchio, fu percosso il duomo nella sua più alta parte con una saetta celeste

episodes.description: Shortly before Piero Soderini, made gonfalonier for life by the Florentine people, was driven out and stripped of his rank, the palazzo was likewise struck by lightning.
episodes.quote: poco innanzi che Piero Soderini, quale era stato fatto gonfalonieri a vita dal popolo fiorentino, fosse cacciato e privo del suo grado, fu il palazzo medesimamente da uno fulgure percosso

episodes.description: Before the Gauls came to Rome, the plebeian Marcus Caedicius reported to the Senate that at midnight on the Via Nuova he had heard a more-than-human voice warning that the Gauls were coming.
episodes.quote: uno Marco Cedicio plebeio riferì al Senato avere udito di mezza notte, passando per la Via nuova, una voce, maggiore che umana

notes: Machiavelli explicitly attributes the Caedicius story to Titus Livius (Livy 5.32).

heading_en: The plebs is bold together, weak singly
thesis: The plebs united is strong, but each man by himself, thinking of his own danger, is weak: a multitude without a head is at once the most formidable and the feeblest of things.
thesis_quote: La Plebe insieme è gagliarda, di per sé è debole

propositions.statement: A multitude speaks boldly against its prince's decisions, but when punishment stares it in the face, each man, distrusting the others, runs to obey.
propositions.quote: la moltitudine è audace nel parlare, molte volte contro alle diliberazioni del loro principe; dipoi, come ei veggono la pena in viso, non si fidando l’uno dell’altro, corrono ad ubbidire

propositions.statement: Nothing is on one side more formidable than an unleashed multitude without a head, and on the other side nothing is weaker.
propositions.quote: non ci è cosa, dall’un canto, più formidabile che una moltitudine sciolta e sanza capo; e, dall’altra parte, non è cosa più debole

propositions.statement: An aroused multitude that wishes to escape these dangers must at once make from among itself a head to correct it, keep it united, and plan its defense.
propositions.quote: una moltitudine così concitata, volendo fuggire questi pericoli, ha subito a fare infra sé medesima uno capo che la corregga, tenghila unita e pensi alla sua difesa

episodes.description: After the Gallic sack many Romans moved to Veii against the Senate's ordinance; they first mocked the public edicts ordering their return under penalty, but when the deadline neared each one obeyed.
episodes.quote: comandò per i suoi editti publici che ciascuno, infra certo tempo, e sotto certe pene, tornasse a abitare a Roma

episodes.description: After the death of Virginia the Roman plebs departed from Rome and, to save itself, created twenty tribunes from among its own number.
episodes.quote: come fece la plebe romana, quando, dopo la morte di Virginia, si partì da Roma, e per salvarsi feciono infra loro venti Tribuni

notes: Quotes Livy verbatim: 'Ex ferocibus universis singuli metu suo obedientes fuere' (Livy 6.4).

heading_en: The multitude is wiser and more constant than a prince
thesis: Against the common opinion of all writers, a people that commands and is well ordered is as stable, prudent, and grateful as a prince or more so; the defects imputed to the multitude belong to all men unregulated by laws, and above all to princes.
thesis_quote: un popolo che comandi e sia bene ordinato, sarà stabile, prudente e grato non altrimenti che un principe, o meglio che un principe, eziandio stimato savio

propositions.statement: The defect writers charge to the multitude can be charged to all men individually and most of all to princes, for anyone unregulated by laws would make the same errors as an unleashed multitude.
propositions.quote: di quello difetto di che accusano gli scrittori la moltitudine, se ne possono accusare tutti gli uomini particularmente, e massime i principi; perché ciascuno, che non sia regolato dalle leggi, farebbe quelli medesimi errori che la moltitudine sciolta

propositions.statement: The variation in their conduct arises not from diverse nature but from more or less respect for the laws within which both live.
propositions.quote: la variazione del procedere loro nasce non dalla natura diversa, perché in tutti è a un modo, e, se vi è vantaggio di bene, è nel popolo; ma dallo avere più o meno rispetto alle leggi

propositions.statement: In its elections to magistracies a people chooses far better than a prince, and will never be persuaded to raise an infamous and corrupt man to dignities, as a prince easily is.
propositions.quote: Vedesi ancora, nelle sue elezioni ai magistrati, fare, di lunga, migliore elezione che un principe

propositions.statement: A licentious and tumultuous people can be spoken to by a good man and easily led back to the good way; for a bad prince there is no remedy but steel.
propositions.quote: a un popolo licenzioso e tumultuario, gli può da un uomo buono essere parlato, e facilmente può essere ridotto nella via buona: a un principe cattivo non è alcuno che possa parlare né vi è altro rimedio che il ferro

episodes.description: The Roman people condemned Manlius Capitolinus to death and shortly afterward, once no danger remained from him, supremely desired him back.
episodes.quote: come si vede aver fatto il popolo romano, di Manlio Capitolino, il quale avendo condannato a morte, sommamente dipoi desiderava quello

episodes.description: Livy describes the unleashed multitude of Syracuse after the death of Hieronymus, grandson of Hiero, which either serves humbly or dominates proudly.
episodes.quote: quando mostra gli accidenti che nacquono in Siracusa dopo la morte di Girolamo nipote di Ierone

episodes.description: Princes held wise have likewise put men to death and then supremely desired them back, as Alexander with Clitus and his other friends, and Herod with Mariamne.
episodes.quote: de’ principi, tenuti savi, i quali hanno fatto morire qualche persona, e poi sommamente desideratola: come Alessandro, Clito ed altri suoi amici; ed Erode, Marianne

episodes.description: Cities where peoples rule make excessive gains in a very short time, as Rome did after the expulsion of the kings and Athens after freeing itself from Pisistratus.
episodes.quote: come fece Roma dopo la cacciata de’ re, ed Atene da poi che la si liberò da Pisistrato

notes: Opens citing 'Tito Livio nostro' and quotes him twice verbatim; the Syracuse quotation ('Haec natura multitudinis est...') is from Livy 24.25, outside the Livy 1-10 corpus. The Rome/Athens episode spans Roman and Greek history; period set to roman-republic.

heading_en: Whose alliance is more trustworthy, a republic's or a prince's
thesis: Leagues made by force are kept by neither princes nor republics, and fear breaks both faiths alike; but where danger is urgent, and where utility tempts to betrayal, republics show somewhat more stability and keep their accords far better than princes.
thesis_quote: in questi casi, dove è il pericolo urgente, si troverrà qualche stabilità più nelle republiche, che ne’ principi

propositions.statement: Accords made by force will be observed toward you neither by a prince nor by a republic; when fear for the state comes, both will break faith and show ingratitude rather than lose it.
propositions.quote: gli accordi fatti per forza non ti saranno né da uno principe né da una republica osservati

propositions.statement: Because republics move slowly, they take longer to resolve, and therefore longer to break faith, than a prince.
propositions.quote: lo avere il moto loro tardo, farà che le perranno sempre più a risolversi che il principe, e per questo perranno più a rompere la fede di lui

propositions.statement: Confederations are broken for utility, and in this republics are far more observant of accords than princes.
propositions.quote: In questo le republiche sono, di lunga, più osservanti degli accordi, che i principi

episodes.description: Demetrius, called the besieger of cities, after conferring infinite benefits on the Athenians, was routed by his enemies and, fleeing to Athens as a friendly and obligated city, was not received by it.
episodes.quote: sendo rotto da’ suoi inimici, e rifuggendosi in Atene come in città amica ed a lui obligata, non fu ricevuto da quella

episodes.description: Pompey, routed by Caesar in Thessaly, fled to Egypt to Ptolemy, whom he had previously restored to his kingdom, and was killed by him.
episodes.quote: Pompeio, rotto che fu da Cesare in Tessaglia, si rifuggì in Egitto a Tolomeo, il quale era per lo adietro da lui stato rimesso nel regno

episodes.description: The princes of the kingdom of Naples who followed the French party awaited ruin out of loyalty, hoping for eventual restoration.
actors: princes of the kingdom of Naples
episodes.quote: sono stati quegli principi del reame di Napoli, che hanno seguite le parti franciose

episodes.description: Saguntum in Spain awaited its ruin rather than desert the Roman side.
episodes.quote: fu di questa sorte Sagunto in Ispagna, che aspettò la rovina per seguire le parti romane

episodes.description: Florence in 1512 awaited ruin for following the French party.
episodes.quote: di questa Firenze, per seguire nel 1512 le parti franciose

episodes.description: Themistocles proposed a secretly advantageous plan to the Athenians; Aristides, chosen to judge it, reported it most useful but most dishonest, and the people wholly refused it.
episodes.quote: Aristide riferì al popolo, il partito di Temistocle essere utilissimo ma disonestissimo: per la quale cosa il popolo al tutto lo ricusò

notes: The Saguntum episode (Livy 21) falls outside the Livy 1-10 corpus; no candidate given. Philip of Macedon cited as a faith-breaking prince.

heading_en: Rome gave the consulate without respect of age
thesis: Once the consulate was opened to the plebs, Rome conferred it and every other magistracy without respect of age or blood, always seeking virtue whether in young or old—a necessity for any city that wants to achieve what Rome achieved.
thesis_quote: la Republica romana, poiché il Consolato venne nella Plebe, concesse quello ai suoi cittadini sanza rispetto di età o di sangue

propositions.statement: One cannot give men hardship without reward, nor take from them the hope of attaining the reward, without danger.
propositions.quote: e’ non si può dare agli uomini disagio sanza premio, né si può tôrre loro la speranza di conseguire il premio sanza pericolo

propositions.statement: A city that does not employ its plebs in anything glorious may treat it as it pleases, but one that wants to do what Rome did cannot make this distinction.
propositions.quote: la città che non adopera la sua plebe a alcuna cosa gloriosa, la può trattare a suo modo

propositions.statement: When a young man has shown notable virtue, it would be most harmful for the city not to avail itself of him then, waiting for the vigor of mind of that age to grow old with him.
propositions.quote: sarebbe cosa dannosissima che la città non se ne potessi valere allora, e che l’avesse a aspettare che fosse invecchiato con lui quel vigore dell’animo

episodes.description: Valerius Corvinus was made consul at twenty-three, and told his soldiers that the consulate was the reward of virtue, not of blood.
episodes.quote: si vede per il testimone di Valerio Corvino, che fu fatto Consolo in ventitré anni

episodes.description: Rome availed itself of Valerius Corvinus, Scipio, Pompey, and many others who triumphed very young.
episodes.quote: come si valse Roma di Valerio Corvino, di Scipione e di Pompeio, e di molti altri, che trionfarono giovanissimi

notes: Latin tag «praemium virtutis, non sanguinis» echoes Valerius Corvus' speech in Livy 7.32; the consulship at 23 is narrated at Livy 7.26.

heading_en: Whether virtue or fortune was the greater cause of Rome's empire
thesis: Rome's empire was won not by fortune alone, as Plutarch and even Livy suggest, but by extraordinary virtue and prudence mixed with fortune, visible in the ordering of its wars.
thesis_quote: chi considererà bene l’ordine di queste guerre, ed il modo del procedere loro, vi vedrà dentro mescolate con la fortuna una virtù e prudenza grandissima

propositions.statement: When a prince or people attains such reputation that every neighbor fears to attack it on its own, each will attack only when forced, leaving the power free to choose its wars and lull the rest.
propositions.quote: come uno principe e uno popolo viene in tanta riputazione, che ciascuno principe e popolo vicino abbia di per sé paura ad assaltarlo e ne tema, sempre interverrà che ciascuno d’essi mai lo assalterà, se non necessitato

propositions.statement: Rome never had two very powerful wars at the same time; one always arose as the other was extinguished.
propositions.quote: mai non intervenne che eglino avessero due potentissime guerre in uno medesimo tempo: anzi parve sempre che, o, nel nascere dell’una, l’altra si spegnesse

propositions.statement: Had two of those powers joined forces while fresh, the ruin of the Roman republic would surely have followed.
propositions.quote: che se due di queste potenze intere si fossero, quando erano fresche, accozzate insieme, senza dubbio si può facilmente conietturare che ne sarebbe seguito la rovina della romana Republica

propositions.statement: The Romans always secured some friend in a new province to serve as ladder and gate for entering and holding it.
propositions.quote: sempre s’ingegnarono avere nelle provincie nuove qualche amico che fussi scala o porta a salirvi o entrarvi, o mezzo a tenerla

episodes.description: The sequence of Rome's wars: first the Aequi and Volsci, then the Samnites, the Latin revolt (with Samnite help for Rome), the Tuscans, Pyrrhus, and finally Carthage, never two great wars at once.
episodes.quote: mentre che combatterno con gli Equi e con i Volsci, mai, mentre che questi popoli furono potenti, non scesero contro di loro altre genti

episodes.description: After the First Punic War all the Gauls on both sides of the Alps conspired against Rome and were slaughtered between Populonia and Pisa.
episodes.quote: intra Populonia e Pisa, dove è oggi la torre a San Vincenti, furono con massima strage superati

episodes.description: The Carthaginians, powerful but distant, never thought of attacking Rome or aiding the Samnites and Tuscans, even seeking Roman friendship until it was too late.
episodes.quote: fece che non pensarono mai di assaltare quello, né di soccorrere i Sanniti ed i Toscani

episodes.description: Rome entered provinces through local friends: the Capuans into Samnium, Camertines in Tuscany, Mamertines in Sicily, Saguntines in Spain, Masinissa in Africa, Aetolians in Greece.
episodes.quote: per il mezzo de’ Capuani entrarono in Sannio, de’ Camertini in Toscana, de’ Mamertini in Sicilia, de’ Saguntini in Spagna

notes: Livy invoked ('E pare che a questa opinione si accosti Livio') as leaning toward the fortune thesis Machiavelli rejects.

heading_en: The peoples Rome fought and how obstinately they defended their liberty
thesis: Nothing made Roman conquest harder than the ancient peoples' love of liberty, for only free cities pursuing the common good grow in dominion and wealth.
thesis_quote: Nessuna cosa fe’ più faticoso a’ Romani superare i popoli d’intorno e parte delle provincie discosto, quanto lo amore che in quelli tempi molti popoli avevano alla libertà

propositions.statement: Not private but common good makes cities great, and the common good is observed only in republics.
propositions.quote: non il bene particulare, ma il bene comune è quello che fa grandi le città. E senza dubbio, questo bene comune non è osservato se non nelle republiche

propositions.statement: As soon as a tyranny arises over a free polity, the least evil is that the city stops growing; usually it goes backward.
propositions.quote: subito che nasce una tirannide sopra uno vivere libero, il manco male che ne resulti a quelle città è non andare più innanzi

propositions.statement: Christian education, prizing humility over worldly honor, has made men weaker than the ancients, whose religion made them fierce in action.
propositions.quote: avendoci la nostra religione mostro la verità e la vera via, ci fa stimare meno l’onore del mondo: onde i Gentili, stimandolo assai, ed avendo posto in quello il sommo bene, erano nelle azioni loro più feroci

propositions.statement: Of all hard servitudes, the hardest is subjection to a republic, which is more durable and aims to enervate all other bodies to swell its own.
propositions.quote: E di tutte le servitù dure, quella è durissima che ti sottomette a una republica

episodes.description: The Tuscans refused to aid Veii against Rome so long as the Veientes, who had made themselves a king, lived under him.
episodes.quote: deliberarono di non dare aiuto a’ Veienti, infino a tanto che vivessono sotto il re

episodes.description: On the death of Hieronymus of Syracuse his army, about to avenge him, was calmed entirely by the cry of liberty in the city.
episodes.quote: come ei sentì che in Siracusa si gridava libertà, allettato da quel nome, si quietò tutto

episodes.description: In Corcyra during the Peloponnesian war the popular party imprisoned the nobles and killed them all, crushing the last under the ruins of their prison.
episodes.quote: il popolo, a questo romore fatto uno concorso, scoperse la parte superiore di quel luogo, e quegli con quelle rovine suffocò

episodes.description: The Samnites, while free, resisted Rome for forty-six years until the consulship of Papirius Cursor the younger despite repeated defeats.
episodes.quote: potessono infino al tempo di Papirio Cursore consolo, figliuolo del primo Papirio, resistere a’ Romani

episodes.description: Reduced to servitude, the Samnites sent envoys begging Hannibal for help because they could barely defend themselves against one Roman legion at Nola.
episodes.quote: sendo i Sanniti oppressi da una legione di uomini che era in Nola, mandarono oratori ad Annibale, a pregarlo che gli soccorressi

heading_en: Rome became great by ruining neighboring cities and freely admitting foreigners to its honors
thesis: A city that would build empire must fill itself with inhabitants, by love (welcoming foreigners) and by force (destroying neighboring cities and transplanting their people).
thesis_quote: si debbono con ogni industria ingegnare di farla piena di abitatori; perché, sanza questa abbondanza di uomini, mai non riuscirà di fare grande una città

propositions.statement: There are two ways to populate a city: by love and by force.
propositions.quote: Questo si fa in due modi: per amore e per forza

propositions.statement: A small republic cannot seize cities or kingdoms stronger than itself; like a thin trunk bearing a thick branch, any small wind breaks it.
propositions.quote: una republica piccola non può occupare città né regni che sieno più validi né più grossi di lei

propositions.statement: Sparta and Athens, though heavily armed and excellently ordered, never reached Roman greatness because they kept their bodies small.
propositions.quote: essendo dua republiche armatissime, ed ordinate di ottime leggi, nondimeno non si condussono alla grandezza dello Imperio romano

episodes.description: By the time of the sixth king Rome held eighty thousand men capable of bearing arms, grown by destroying neighbors and receiving foreigners.
episodes.quote: nel tempo del sesto re, in Roma abitavano ottantamila uomini da portare arme

episodes.description: Livy's dictum that Rome grows on the ruins of Alba epitomizes the method.
episodes.quote: Il che dimostra Tito Livio in due parole, quando disse: «Crescit interea Roma Albae ruinis»

episodes.description: Lycurgus barred foreigners from Sparta, even instituting leather money to deter traders, so Sparta never exceeded twenty thousand men and, after Thebes rebelled, lost all its Greek conquests.
episodes.quote: ordinò che in quella sua republica si spendesse monete di cuoio, per tor via a ciascuno il disiderio di venirvi

institutions: admission of foreigners to civic honors
notes: Chapter opens and closes with the same Latin tag from Livy 1.30.

heading_en: Republics have had three modes of expansion
thesis: Of the three modes of expansion — a league of equal republics, making companions while keeping command, and making outright subjects — the Roman mode of companions under one head is the only true path to great empire.
thesis_quote: le republiche hanno tenuti tre modi circa lo ampliare

propositions.statement: Making immediate subjects is wholly useless: Sparta and Athens were ruined precisely by acquiring dominion they could not hold.
propositions.quote: De’ quali tre modi, questo ultimo è al tutto inutile; come si vide ch’ei fu nelle soprascritte due republiche: le quali non rovinarono per altro, se non per avere acquistato quel dominio che le non potevano tenere

propositions.statement: The league mode has a fixed limit, never exceeded in any example, of about twelve or fourteen communities, after which it seeks no further dominion.
propositions.quote: simile modo di procedere ha un termine fisso, il quale non ci è esemplo che mostri che si sia trapassato: e questo è di aggiugnere a dodici o quattordici comunità

propositions.statement: A republic that wishes to expand can hold no other mode than Rome's, experience having shown none more certain or true.
