propositions.quote: né può tenere altro modo una republica che voglia ampliare; perché la esperienza non ce ne ha mostro nessuno più certo o più vero

episodes.description: The ancient Tuscans, a league of twelve equal cities including Chiusi, Veii, Arezzo, Fiesole and Volterra, ruled Italy from the Tiber to the Alps before losing Lombardy to the Gauls.
episodes.quote: furono dodici città, tra le quali era Chiusi, Veio, Arezzo, Fiesole, Volterra, e simili: i quali per via di lega governavano lo Imperio loro

episodes.description: Rome's Italian companions, having helped subjugate the provinces with their own blood, found themselves suddenly ringed by Roman subjects, and when they conspired against Rome they lost and became subjects themselves.
episodes.quote: quegli compagni di Roma che erano in Italia, si trovarono in un tratto cinti da’ sudditi romani, ed oppressi da una grossissima città come era Roma

episodes.description: At the parley between Philip of Macedon and Titus Quinctius Flamininus, Philip reproached the Aetolian praetor for Aetolian greed and faithlessness in serving both sides for pay.
episodes.quote: venendo a parlamento Filippo re di Macedonia con Tito Quinzio Flaminio, e ragionando d’accordo alla presenza d’uno pretore degli Etoli

episodes.description: Today only the Swiss and the Swabian league imitate the ancient league mode of the Tuscans, Achaeans and Aetolians.
episodes.quote: E quanto alle leghe, si trovano solo i Svizzeri e la lega di Svezia che gli imita

institutions: seat of empire and title of command
notes: The Flamininus parley is in Livy book 32-33, outside Livy I-X, so no candidate given.

heading_en: Changes of sects and languages, with floods and plagues, extinguish the memory of things
thesis: The memory of the past is extinguished partly by human causes — changes of religions and languages — and partly by heaven, through flood, plague and famine that nearly wipe out mankind.
thesis_quote: queste memorie de’ tempi per diverse cagioni si spengano: delle quali, parte vengono dagli uomini, parte dal cielo

propositions.statement: When a new sect arises, its first effort, to gain reputation, is to extinguish the old one, and it succeeds easily when its founders speak a different language.
propositions.quote: quando e’ surge una setta nuova, cioè una religione nuova, il primo studio suo è, per darsi riputazione, estinguere la vecchia

propositions.statement: Since sects change two or three times in five or six thousand years, memory of things done before is lost, and surviving traces are dismissed as fable.
propositions.quote: queste sètte in cinque o in seimila anni variano due o tre volte, si perde la memoria delle cose fatte innanzi a quel tempo

propositions.statement: When provinces are overfull and human cunning at its height, nature necessarily purges the world through flood, plague or famine, as in simple bodies.
propositions.quote: conviene di necessità che il mondo si purghi per uno de’ tre modi; acciocché gli uomini, sendo divenuti pochi e battuti, vivino più comodamente

episodes.description: The Christian sect, under St. Gregory and other church heads, obstinately persecuted pagan memory, burning the works of poets and historians and destroying images.
episodes.quote: e’ perseguitarono tutte le memorie antiche, ardendo le opere de’ poeti e degli istorici, ruinando le imagini

episodes.description: Tuscany, once powerful and full of religion and virtue with its own customs and language, was so extinguished by Roman power that only the memory of its name remains.
episodes.quote: già la Toscana potente, piena di religione e di virtù, aveva i suoi costumi e la sua lingua patria: il che tutto è suto spento dalla potenza romana

notes: Largely theoretical chapter; mentions Diodorus Siculus and Procopius-adjacent themes elsewhere.

heading_en: How the Romans proceeded in making war
thesis: The Romans made their wars short and massive, ending them with quick decisive battles, land confiscations and frontier colonies, so that war enriched rather than impoverished the state.
thesis_quote: fu in prima di fare le guerre, come dicano i Franciosi, corte e grosse

propositions.statement: In acquiring and holding one must think not to spend but to do everything to the public profit.
propositions.quote: È necessario dunque, e nello acquistare e nel mantenere, pensare di non spendere; anzi fare ogni cosa con utilità del publico suo

propositions.statement: Colonies placed on conquered frontiers guarded Roman borders at no public expense while profiting the colonists.
propositions.quote: la quale posta in su le frontiere di coloro veniva ad essere guardia de’ confini romani, con utile di essi coloni

propositions.statement: The consuls' ambition to triumph within their one-year term kept wars short even after soldiers' pay allowed longer campaigns.
propositions.quote: gli tenne, circa il fare le guerre brevi oltra a il loro naturale uso, l’ambizione de’ Consoli

episodes.description: All Roman wars from the city's beginning to the siege of Veii — against Latins, Samnites and Tuscans — were dispatched in six, ten or twenty days by immediate pitched battle.
episodes.quote: tutte si vedranno ispedite, quale in sei, quale in dieci, quale in venti dì

episodes.description: At the siege of Veii the Romans instituted pay for their soldiers so as to be able to wage war at length and at a distance.
episodes.quote: il che fu dopo la ossidione de’ Veienti; dove, per potere fare guerra lungamente, gli ordinarono di pagare i soldati

heading_en: How much land the Romans gave per colonist
thesis: Roman land distributions to colonists were everywhere sparing, so as to send more men as guards and keep colonists as poor abroad as citizens were at home.
thesis_quote: Giudicasi che ad ogni modo ed in ogni luogo la distribuzione fussi parca

propositions.statement: Distribution was sparing first to send more men as garrison, and because those living poor at home would not let their colonists abound abroad.
propositions.quote: prima, per potere mandare più uomini, sendo quelli diputati per guardia di quel paese; dipoi perché, vivendo loro poveri a casa, non era ragionevole che volessono che i loro uomini abbondassino troppo fuora

propositions.statement: The Romans judged that not abundant but well-cultivated land sufficed.
propositions.quote: non lo assai terreno, ma il bene cultivato, bastasse

propositions.statement: Every colony must have public fields for pasturing livestock and woods for firewood, without which it cannot be ordered.
propositions.quote: È necessario bene, che tutta la colonia abbi campi publici dove ciascuno possa pascere il suo bestiame

episodes.description: After Veii was taken the Romans sent a colony there and distributed to each colonist three iugera and seven unciae of land.
episodes.quote: preso Veio, e’ vi mandarono una colonia, e distribuirono a ciascuno tre iugeri e sètte once di terra

notes: The text has a lacuna after 'che sono, al modo nostro....' where the modern equivalent of the measure is left blank.

heading_en: Why peoples leave their native lands and flood other countries
thesis: Besides wars of ambition there are wars of whole migrating peoples, driven by famine or war to seize and wholly possess new lands; these are the cruelest and most terrifying wars.
thesis_quote: quando uno popolo intero con tutte le sue famiglie si lieva d’uno luogo, necessitato o dalla fame o dalla guerra, e va a cercare nuova sede e nuova provincia

propositions.statement: Wars of ambition, however dangerous, do not expel a province's inhabitants, since the victor is content with obedience and usually leaves laws, homes and goods.
propositions.quote: Le quali guerre sono pericolose, ma non cacciano al tutto gli abitatori d’una provincia; perché e’ basta, al vincitore, solo la ubbidienza de’ popoli

propositions.statement: Peoples driven out by ultimate necessity are most formidable and can be withstood only by good arms.
propositions.quote: Sono, pertanto, questi popoli formidolosissimi, sendo cacciati da una ultima necessità; e se e’ non riscontrano buone armi, non mai saranno sostenuti

propositions.statement: The great migrating hordes have almost all come from Scythia, whose cold poor lands cannot feed their many men.
propositions.quote: Escono i popoli grossi, e sono usciti quasi tutti, de’ paesi di Scizia; luoghi freddi e poveri

episodes.description: Overpopulated Gaul sent out part of its people under Bellovesus and Sicovesus; Bellovesus crossed into Italy, took Lombardy from the Tuscans, and thence came the first Gallic war on Rome.
episodes.quote: elessono, per capitani di quegli che si avevano a partire, Belloveso e Sicoveso, duoi re de’ Franciosi: de’ quali Belloveso venne in Italia, e Sicoveso passò in Ispagna

episodes.description: The first of Rome's three migration wars: the capture of Rome by the Gauls who had earlier seized Lombardy.
episodes.quote: La prima fu quella quando Roma fu presa, la quale fu occupata da quei Franciosi che avevano tolto, come di sopra si disse, la Lombardia a’ Toscani

episodes.description: The second: after the First Punic War the Romans killed more than two hundred thousand Gauls between Piombino and Pisa.
episodes.quote: quella che fecero dopo la prima guerra cartaginese, quando intra Piombino e Pisa ammazzarono più che dugentomila Franciosi

episodes.description: The third: the Germans and Cimbri, having beaten several Roman armies, came into Italy and were defeated by Marius.
episodes.quote: quando i Tedeschi e’ Cimbri vennero in Italia: i quali, avendo vinti più eserciti romani, furono vinti da Mario

episodes.description: When Roman virtue failed, the empire was destroyed by similar peoples — Goths, Vandals and the like — who occupied the whole western empire.
episodes.quote: fu quello imperio destrutto da simili popoli: i quali furono Gotti, Vandali, e simili, che occuparono tutto lo Imperio occidentale

episodes.description: The Maurusii of Syria, unable to resist the invading Hebrews, abandoned their country for Africa, driving out its inhabitants, as Procopius's column inscriptions attest.
episodes.quote: levatisi con loro famiglie, se ne andarono in Africa, dove posero la loro sedia, cacciando via quelli abitatori che in quegli luoghi trovarono

episodes.description: Moses occupied part of Syria and renamed it Judea, as new occupiers rename provinces.
episodes.quote: Moisè ancora chiamò Giudea quella parte di Soria occupata da lui

episodes.description: Small displaced groups like Aeneas, Dido and the Massilians seized places by art rather than violence, maintaining themselves with the consent of neighbors.
episodes.quote: come si vede che fece Enea, Didone, i Massiliesi e simili; i quali tutti, per consentimento de’ vicini, dov’e’ posono, poterono mantenervisi

notes: Also cites Sallust (end of the Jugurthine War) and Procopius.

heading_en: What causes commonly make wars arise among the powerful
thesis: Wars among powerful states arise either by chance, as the Roman-Samnite war did, or are deliberately engineered by one who wants war, typically by attacking the friend of his intended enemy.
thesis_quote: è una cagione comune che nasce infra tutti i principati potenti. La quale cagione o la viene a caso o la è fatta nascere da colui che disidera muovere la guerra

propositions.statement: To war on a prince with whom treaties stand, one attacks his friend instead: either he reacts, giving the desired war, or his failure to defend a client exposes his weakness or faithlessness.
propositions.quote: con altra giustificazione e con altro colore assalterò io uno suo amico che lui proprio

propositions.statement: A city that cannot defend itself but wants defense at all costs should give itself freely to the power it designs as its defender.
propositions.quote: darsi liberamente a quello che tu disegni che ti difenda

propositions.statement: Rome, having empire and glory and not quiet as its end, could not refuse the Campanian enterprise.
propositions.quote: avendo Roma per fine lo imperio e la gloria, e non la quiete, non poteva ricusare questa impresa

episodes.description: The Samnite war arose by chance when the oppressed Campanians gave themselves to Rome, forcing the Romans to defend them as subjects against their Samnite allies.
episodes.quote: sendo i Campani oppressati, e ricorrendo a Roma fuora della opinione de’ Romani e de’ Sanniti, furono forzati, dandosi i Campani ai Romani, come cosa loro defendergli

episodes.description: The First Punic War likewise began by chance from Rome's defense of the Messinesi in Sicily.
episodes.quote: Questa medesima cagione dette principio alla prima guerra contro ai Cartaginesi, per la defensione che i Romani presono de’ Messinesi in Sicilia

episodes.description: Hannibal attacked Rome's Saguntine friends in Spain not to harm them but to provoke Roman arms and gain occasion to pass into Italy.
episodes.quote: Annibale capitano cartaginese assaltò i Saguntini amici de’ Romani in Ispagna, non per offendere quelli, ma per muovere l’armi romane

episodes.description: The Florentines gave themselves to King Robert of Naples, who, unwilling to defend them as friends, defended them as subjects against Castruccio of Lucca.
episodes.quote: i Fiorentini a il re Ruberto di Napoli: il quale non gli volendo difendere come amici, gli difese poi come sudditi contro alle forze di Castruccio da Lucca

heading_en: Money is not the sinews of war, contrary to common opinion
thesis: Good soldiers, not gold, are the sinews of war: gold cannot find good soldiers, but good soldiers can always find gold.
thesis_quote: non l’oro, come grida la comune opinione, essere il nervo della guerra, ma i buoni soldati: perché l’oro non è sufficiente a trovare i buoni soldati, ma i buoni soldati sono bene sufficienti a trovare l’oro

propositions.statement: A prince will always deceive himself if he measures his forces by money, terrain or men's goodwill while lacking arms of his own.
propositions.quote: ogni volta s’ingannerà, quando le misuri o dai danari, o dal sito, o dalla benivolenza degli uomini, mancando, dall’altra parte, d’armi proprie

propositions.statement: Money not only fails to defend you but makes you plundered the sooner.
propositions.quote: I danari ancora, non solo non ti difendono, ma ti fanno predare più presto

propositions.statement: Many necessities, of which shortage of money is only one, force a captain to battle against his intention.
propositions.quote: Sono, adunque, molte necessitadi che fanno a un capitano fuor della sua intenzione pigliare partito di azzuffarsi, intra le quali qualche volta può essere la carestia de’ danari

episodes.description: The Spartan king, lacking money against Antipater, was forced to battle and beaten, whereas a few days' delay would have brought news of Alexander's death and victory without fighting (Quintus Curtius).
episodes.quote: per difetto di danari, il re di Sparta fu necessitato azzuffarsi, e fu rotto

episodes.description: Shown Croesus's innumerable treasure, Solon judged him no more powerful for it, since war is made with iron, not gold.
episodes.quote: gli rispose Solone, che per quello e’ non lo giudicava più potente; perché la guerra si faceva con il ferro e non con l’oro

episodes.description: The king of Macedon displayed his gold and silver to Gallic envoys to frighten them; the Gauls broke the nearly settled peace out of desire to seize that gold.
episodes.quote: quel re, per mostrare la potenza sua e per sbigottirli, mostrò loro oro ed ariento assai

episodes.description: The Venetians recently lost their whole state although their treasury was still full of treasure.
episodes.quote: I Viniziani, pochi anni sono, avendo ancora lo erario loro pieno di tesoro, perderno tutto lo stato

episodes.description: Livy, debating whether Alexander would have beaten Rome, names three necessities of war — many good soldiers, prudent captains and good fortune — never mentioning money.
episodes.quote: mostra essere tre cose necessarie nella guerra; assai soldati e buoni, capitani prudenti, e buona fortuna

episodes.description: The Capuans, measuring their power by money rather than soldiers, aided the Sidicini and after two defeats had to make themselves tributaries of Rome.
episodes.quote: preso ch’egli ebbero partito di aiutargli, dopo due rotte furono constretti farsi tributari de’ Romani, se si vollono salvare

episodes.description: Modern proofs: Duke Charles was beaten by the Swiss, and the Pope and Florentines together could not easily beat Francesco Maria in the war of Urbino, despite money.
episodes.quote: il duca Carlo arebbe vinti i Svizzeri; e pochi giorni sono, il Papa ed i Fiorentini insieme non arebbono avuta difficultà in vincere Francesco Maria

episodes.description: Hasdrubal, caught in the Marches by Claudius Nero and the other consul, had to choose between flight and battle, and chose battle.
episodes.quote: come intervenne a Asdrubale, quando nella Marca fu assaltato da Claudio Nerone, insieme con l’altro console romano

notes: Also cites Quintus Curtius and Pericles's advice to the Athenians.

heading_en: It is not prudent to ally with a prince who has more reputation than strength
thesis: Leagues with princes who lack the proximity or forces to help bring more fame than aid to those who trust in them.
thesis_quote: le leghe che si fanno coi principi, che non abbino o commodità di aiutarti per la distanza del sito, o forze da farlo per suo disordine o altra sua cagione, arrecono più fama che aiuto

propositions.statement: Alliances with distant or disordered princes yield reputation, not protection, to those who rely on them.
propositions.quote: le leghe che si fanno coi principi, che non abbino o commodità di aiutarti per la distanza del sito, o forze da farlo per suo disordine o altra sua cagione, arrecono più fama che aiuto

propositions.statement: Men of little prudence, unable to defend themselves, nevertheless undertake to defend others.
propositions.quote: non sappiendo né potendo difendere sé medesimi, vogliono prendere impresa di difendere altrui

episodes.description: Livy's verdict on the Sidicini trusting Campanian aid: the Campanians brought a name rather than forces to their protection.
episodes.quote: «Campani magis nomen in auxilium Sidicinorum, quam vires ad praesidium attulerunt»

episodes.description: In 1479, attacked by the Pope and the king of Naples, the Florentines drew from their French friendship a name rather than protection.
episodes.quote: nel 1479, il Papa ed il re di Napoli gli assaltarono: ché, essendo amici del re di Francia, trassono di quella amicizia «magis nomen, quam praesidium»

episodes.description: The Tarentine ambassadors demanded peace between Rome and the Samnites; the Roman consul, laughing, had battle sounded in their presence.
episodes.quote: il Console, ridendosi di questa proposta, alla presenza di detti ambasciadori fece sonare a battaglia

notes: Also warns against enterprises trusting Emperor Maximilian.

heading_en: Whether, fearing attack, it is better to begin war or to await it
thesis: A prince whose people are armed and ordered for war should await a powerful war at home; one with unarmed subjects should carry war as far from home as he can.
thesis_quote: quel principe che ha i suoi popoli armati ed ordinati alla guerra, aspetti sempre in casa una guerra potente e pericolosa, e non la vadia a rincontrare

propositions.statement: He whose subjects are unarmed and country unused to war should keep the war far from home, since his strength lies in money, which home war cuts off.
propositions.quote: quello che ha i suoi sudditi disarmati, ed il paese inusitato alla guerra, se le discosti sempre da casa il più che può

propositions.statement: Soldiers in another's country are more compelled to fight, and that necessity makes virtue.
propositions.quote: i suoi soldati, per trovarsi nel paese d’altrui, sono più necessitati a combattere; e quella necessità fa virtù

propositions.statement: Awaiting at home you risk all your forces but not all your fortune; going abroad you risk all your fortune but not all your forces.
propositions.quote: tanto che tu vieni ad arristiare tutte le forze, e non tutta la fortuna; e, discostandoti, arrischi tutta la fortuna, e non tutte le forze

propositions.statement: Had Rome suffered its three Hannibalic defeats in France instead of Italy, it would without doubt have been finished.
propositions.quote: se i Romani avessono avute in tanto spazio di tempo quelle tre rotte in Francia ch’egli ebbero in Italia da Annibale, sanza dubbio erano spacciati

episodes.description: Croesus, against the others' opinion, advised Cyrus to cross into queen Tomyris's realm to attack the Massagetae in their own country.
episodes.quote: Creso, contro alla opinione degli altri, disse che si andasse a trovare lei

episodes.description: Hannibal advised Antiochus that the Romans could be beaten only in Italy, where their fount of men and wealth could be dried up.
episodes.quote: ei mostra come i Romani non si potevano vincere se non in Italia

episodes.description: Agathocles, unable to sustain the war at home, attacked the Carthaginians in Africa and reduced them to asking for peace.
episodes.quote: Agatocle che, non potendo sostenere la guerra di casa, assaltò i Cartaginesi che gliene facevano, e gli ridusse a domandare pace

episodes.description: Scipio attacked Africa to lift the war from Italy.
episodes.quote: Allega Scipione che, per levare la guerra di Italia, assaltò la Africa

episodes.description: The Athenians prospered while warring near home but lost their liberty when they took their armies to Sicily.
episodes.quote: come si discostarono, ed andarono con gli eserciti in Sicilia, perderono la libertà

episodes.description: The fable of Antaeus, king of Libya, invincible while he awaited Hercules within his own borders but lost when drawn away from the earth, his mother.
episodes.quote: Anteo, re di Libia, assaltato da Ercole Egizio, fu insuperabile mentre che lo aspettò dentro a’ confini del suo regno

episodes.description: Dying Ferdinand of Naples counseled his son Alfonso to await Charles VIII inside the kingdom; the advice was ignored, and army and state were lost without a battle.
episodes.quote: fu ch’egli aspettasse il nimico dentro a il regno; e per cosa del mondo non traesse forze fuora dello stato suo

episodes.description: The Florentines were helpless against Castruccio's war at home yet later boldly attacked the duke of Milan far away — brave in distant wars, cowardly in near ones.
episodes.quote: tanta virtù mostrarono nelle guerre longinque, e tanta viltà nelle propinque

episodes.description: The Cimbri broke a Roman army in Germany where Rome had no remedy, but once in Italy, facing Rome's united forces, they were destroyed.
episodes.quote: I Cimbri ruppono uno esercito romano nella Magna, né vi ebbono i Romani rimedio

heading_en: One rises from low to great fortune more by fraud than by force
thesis: Men of small fortune rarely or never reach great rank without force and fraud; force alone never suffices, but fraud alone can, and republics too must use it until they are powerful.
thesis_quote: rado, o non mai, intervenga che gli uomini di piccola fortuna venghino a gradi grandi, sanza la forza e sanza la fraude

propositions.statement: Force alone is never found sufficient, but fraud alone will be found sufficient.
propositions.quote: Né credo si truovi mai che la forza sola basti, ma si troverrà bene che la fraude sola basterà

propositions.statement: What princes must do at the beginnings of their growth, republics too must do until they have become powerful and force alone suffices.
propositions.quote: quel che sono necessitati fare i principi ne’ principii degli augumenti loro, sono ancora necessitate a fare le republiche, infino che le siano diventate potenti

propositions.statement: Fraud is the less blameworthy the more it is covered, as Rome's was.
propositions.quote: la quale è meno vituperabile quanto è più coperta, come fu questa de’ Romani

episodes.description: Xenophon's Cyrus rose through deceit: his first expedition against the king of Armenia was full of fraud, and he deceived his uncle Cyaxares in many ways.
episodes.quote: la prima ispedizione che fe’ fare a Ciro contro al re di Armenia è piena di fraude

episodes.description: Giangaleazzo Visconti took the state and empire of Lombardy from his uncle Bernabò by fraud.
episodes.quote: come fece Giovan Galeazzo per tôrre lo stato e lo imperio di Lombardia a messer Bernabò suo zio

episodes.description: Rome's greatest early fraud was making 'companions' of the Latins and neighbors, who under that name made themselves slaves with their own arms and blood.
episodes.quote: Né poté usare, nel principio, il maggiore inganno, che pigliare il modo, discorso di sopra da noi, di farsi compagni; perché sotto questo nome se gli fece servi

episodes.description: The Latins recognized the deception only after Rome's double defeat of the Samnites, as the Latin praetor Annius Setinus declared in their council.
episodes.quote: «Nam si etiam nunc sub umbra foederis aequi servitutem pati possumus etc.»

notes: Also cites Xenophon's Cyropaedia and the careers of Philip of Macedon and Agathocles.

heading_en: Men often deceive themselves believing humility conquers pride
thesis: Humility toward insolent enemies not only does not help but harms: Roman patience only increased Latin arrogance, so a prince should never yield from fear of force.
thesis_quote: Vedesi molte volte come l’umiltà non solamente non giova ma nuoce, massimamente usandola con gli uomini insolenti

propositions.statement: It is almost always better to let a thing be taken from you by force than by the fear of force.
propositions.quote: gli è meglio, quasi sempre, sendosi condotta la cosa in termine che tu non la possa lasciare nel modo detto, lasciarsela tôrre con le forze, che con la paura delle forze

propositions.statement: Yielding from fear does not remove the war: the adversary, esteeming you less, will want more, while your defenders grow colder.
propositions.quote: se tu la lasci con la paura, lo fai per levarti la guerra, ed il più delle volte non te la lievi

propositions.statement: With several enemies, it is always prudent to give something back to one of them, even after war has broken out, to regain him and split him from the confederates.
propositions.quote: rendere delle cose che tu possedessi a alcuno di loro per riguadagnarselo, ancora che fussi di già scoperta la guerra, e per ismembrarlo dagli altri confederati tuoi nimici, fia sempre partito prudente

episodes.description: When the Samnites complained of Latin attacks, Rome, not wishing to irritate the Latins, declined to forbid the war — which emboldened the Latins and made them open enemies sooner, as Annius's speech on Roman patience shows.
episodes.quote: i Romani non vollono proibire ai Latini tale guerra, disiderando non gli irritare: il che non solamente non gli irritò ma gli fece diventare più animosi

notes: Livy is invoked as 'lo istorico nostro' and quoted in Latin (Annius's speech, Livy 8.4) but not named.

heading_en: Weak states are always ambiguous in resolving, and slow deliberations are always harmful
thesis: In every consultation one must come to a definite resolution, for ambiguity and slow deliberation harm republics; once the mind is fixed on what to do, the words are easily found.
thesis_quote: in ogni consulta è bene venire allo individuo di quello che si ha a diliberare, e non stare sempre in ambiguo né in su lo incerto della cosa

propositions.statement: Once the mind is firm and the course resolved, it is easy to find the words to fit the deeds.
propositions.quote: fermo una volta l’animo, e diliberato quello sia da esequire, è facil cosa trovarvi le parole

propositions.statement: Slow and late deliberations are no less harmful than ambiguous ones, especially those in favor of a friend: they help no one and hurt oneself.
propositions.quote: Non sono meno nocive ancora le diliberazioni lente e tarde, che le ambigue; massime quelle che si hanno a diliberare in favore di alcuno amico

propositions.statement: Such deliberations proceed either from weakness of spirit and forces or from the malignity of the deliberators.
propositions.quote: Queste diliberazioni così fatte procedono o da debolezza d’animo e di forze, o da malignità di coloro che hanno a diliberare

episodes.description: In the Latin council the praetor Annius urged deciding what to do rather than what to say, since words are easily fitted once plans are unfolded.
episodes.quote: Ad summam rerum nostrarum pertinere arbitror, ut cogitetis magis, quid agendum nobis, quam quid loquendum sit

episodes.description: After Hieronymus's death Syracuse hung divided between Rome and Carthage until Apollonides's prudent oration showed that the ambiguity itself, not either choice, would ruin the republic.
episodes.quote: Apollonide, uno de’ primi in Siracusa, con una sua orazione piena di prudenza

episodes.description: The Lavinians delayed aiding the Latins so long that as they marched out the gate news came of the Latin defeat, prompting the praetor Milionius's remark that the short march would cost them dear with Rome.
episodes.quote: Questo poco della via ci costerà assai col Popolo romano

episodes.description: The Florentines delayed ratifying the neutrality accord with Louis XII during his descent against Ludovico Sforza; the late ratification was refused, costing Florence much money and nearly the state.
episodes.quote: Fu differita tale ratificazione da chi per poca prudenza favoriva le cose di Lodovico

notes: Machiavelli adds that such ambiguity has repeatedly damaged 'la republica nostra' (Florence).

heading_en: How far the soldiers of our times diverge from the ancient orders
thesis: Modern armies, having abandoned the Roman three-line order that let an army rally three times in battle, stake everything on the first shock and can be ruined by any small disorder.
thesis_quote: chi si ordina di potersi rifare nelle giornate tre volte, ha ad avere tre volte inimica la fortuna a volere perdere, ed ha ad avere per iscontro una virtù che sia atta tre volte a vincerlo

propositions.statement: Victory consists in obstinacy of spirit: while it lasts in the breasts of the fighters, armies never turn.
propositions.quote: nella quale ostinazione consiste, come altre volte si è detto, la vittoria; perché, mentre che la dura ne’ petti di quelli che combattono, mai non dànno volta gli eserciti

propositions.statement: An army that stands only on the first shock, as all Christian armies now do, can easily lose, since any disorder or middling virtue can snatch victory from it.
propositions.quote: chi non sta se non in sul primo urto, come stanno oggi tutti gli eserciti cristiani, può facilmente perdere; perché ogni disordine, ogni mezzana virtù gli può tôrre la vittoria

propositions.statement: Modern deployments in which lines cannot receive one another make the ranks crash together, so that a minimal accident ruins an army.
propositions.quote: urtando la prima la seconda, e la seconda la terza, ne nasce tanta confusione, che spesso un minimo accidente rovina uno esercito

episodes.description: Rome's most important battle ever, against the Latins in the consulship of Torquatus and Decius, with armies equal in order, virtue, obstinacy and number, Livy giving the edge only to the Roman commanders; Livy's account also sets out the hastati-principes-triarii order.
episodes.quote: fu questa che ei fece con i popoli latini, nel consolato di Torquato e di Decio

episodes.description: To hold their soldiers firm and resolved, one consul killed himself (Decius's devotio) and the other his own son (Torquatus).
episodes.quote: di due Consoli, per tenere fermi gli animi de’ soldati, ed ubbidienti a’ comandamenti loro, e diliberati al combattere l’uno ammazzò sé stesso, e l’altro il figliuolo

episodes.description: At the battle of Ravenna, where Gaston de Foix died, both the Spanish and French armies deployed all their troops in a single wide shallow front.
episodes.quote: Gli eserciti spagnuoli e franciosi nella zuffa di Ravenna, dove morì monsignor de Fois capitano delle genti di Francia

episodes.description: At San Regolo and elsewhere in the Pisan war the Florentines were routed when their own repulsed cavalry crashed into their infantry, as the veteran captain Ciriaco dal Borgo often affirmed to Machiavelli.
episodes.quote: non nacque tale rovina d’altronde che dalla cavalleria amica; la quale, sendo davanti e ributtata da’ nimici, percosse nella fanteria fiorentina

episodes.description: The Swiss, masters of modern war, take care above all when serving with the French to place themselves where friendly cavalry, if repulsed, cannot crash into them.
episodes.quote: I Svizzeri, che sono i maestri delle moderne guerre, quando ei militano con i Franciosi, sopra tutte le cose hanno cura di mettersi in lato

notes: Episode 2 spans Livy 8.7 (execution of Torquatus's son) and 8.9 (Decius's devotio); 8:9 given for the devotio mentioned first.

heading_en: How much artillery should be esteemed by armies in the present times
thesis: Artillery is useful to an army in which the ancient virtue is mingled, but against a virtuous army it is quite useless by itself; it helps the attacker far more than the defender, and the Romans would have conquered even faster with it.
thesis_quote: l’artiglieria essere utile in uno esercito quando vi sia mescolata l’antica virtù; ma, sanza quella, contro a uno esercito virtuoso è inutilissima

propositions.statement: Artillery does incomparably more harm to the defender than to the attacker.
propositions.quote: io credo che sanza comparazione faccino più danno a chi si difende, che a chi offende

propositions.statement: It is a maxim that where men can go in a mass and with impetus, artillery does not hold them.
propositions.quote: questa è una massima, che dove gli uomini in frotta e con impeto possono andare, le artiglierie non gli sostengono

propositions.statement: Since Rome's wars were almost all offensive, the Romans would have had more advantage and made their conquests faster had artillery existed then.
propositions.quote: quelli arebbono avuto più vantaggio, e più presto arebbono fatto i loro acquisti, se le fossono state in quelli tempi

propositions.statement: Infantry can evade artillery fire more easily than ancient infantry evaded elephants and scythed chariots, since artillery hinders only before the fight, not during it.
propositions.quote: con più facilità le fanterie, nello accostarsi al nimico, possono fuggire il colpo delle artiglierie, che non potevano anticamente fuggire l’impeto degli elefanti

episodes.description: At Brescia, Gaston de Foix dismounted and led his squadron through the whole Venetian artillery lining the street from the fortress and took the city without notable harm.
episodes.quote: quello con il suo squadrone, disceso a piede, passando per il mezzo di quelle, occupò la città

episodes.description: At Ravenna the Spaniards, entrenched between the Ronco and a too-low rampart, were forced by the French artillery to leave their defenses and come to battle.
episodes.quote: furono costretti dalle artiglierie uscire delle fortezze loro, e venire alla zuffa

episodes.description: At Novara in 1513 the Swiss, without artillery or cavalry, attacked the French army entrenched with artillery and broke it without hindrance from the guns.
episodes.quote: i quali a Novara nel 1513, sanza artiglierie e sanza cavagli, andarono a trovare lo esercito francioso, munito d’artiglierie, dentro alle fortezze sue, e lo roppono

episodes.description: In twenty-four years of Italian wars only count Lodovico della Mirandola at Ferrara and the duke of Nemours at Cerignola died by artillery; Foix at Ravenna died by steel.
episodes.quote: dal conte Lodovico della Mirandola, che morì a Ferrara quando i Viniziani, pochi anni sono, assaltarono quello stato, ed il Duca di Nemors, che morì alla Cirignuola, in fuori

episodes.description: The Turk's artillery victories over the Sophi and the Soldan came only from the unaccustomed noise frightening their cavalry.
episodes.quote: se il Turco, mediante l’artiglieria, contro al Sofi ed il Soldano ha avuto vittoria

notes: Ottoman victories (Chaldiran, Marj Dabiq era) tagged contemporary-italy for period as 1500s events; no closer enum value.

heading_en: Infantry should be esteemed more than cavalry
thesis: Following Roman authority and the example of the ancient militia, infantry, not cavalry, is the foundation and sinew of an army; Italian princes' neglect of infantry helped make Italy prey to foreigners.
thesis_quote: ma il fondamento e il nervo dello esercito, e quello che si debbe più stimare, debbano essere le fanterie

propositions.statement: Ordered infantry can easily break cavalry and can only with difficulty be broken by it.
propositions.quote: Possono le fanterie, ordinate, facilmente rompere i cavagli, e difficilmente essere rotte da quegli

propositions.statement: Among the sins of Italian princes that made Italy servile to foreigners, the greatest was neglecting infantry and devoting all care to cavalry, a disorder born of the condottieri's interests.
propositions.quote: Ed infra i peccati de’ principi italiani, che hanno fatto Italia serva de’ forestieri, non ci è il maggiore che avere tenuto poco conto di questo ordine

propositions.statement: To overcome ordered infantry one must oppose it with infantry better ordered still; otherwise certain loss follows.
propositions.quote: a volere superare i fanti ordinati, è necessario opporre loro fanti meglio ordinati di quegli: altrimenti, si va a una perdita manifesta

episodes.description: At Lake Regillus the Romans, their army wavering against the Latins, dismounted their cavalry to fight on foot, renewed the battle and won.
episodes.quote: quando si azzuffarono con i Latini appresso al lago Regillo; dove essendo già inclinato lo esercito romano

episodes.description: At Cannae Hannibal mocked the Roman consuls for making their cavalry dismount, saying he would rather have them delivered to him bound.
episodes.quote: veggendo in la giornata di Canne che i Consoli avevano fatto discendere a piè li loro cavalieri

episodes.description: At the camp before Sora, after both cavalry commanders were killed, the Roman horsemen dismounted and compelled the enemy cavalry to do the same, winning on foot.
episodes.quote: Erano i Romani a campo a Sora, ed essendo uscito fuori della terra una turma di cavagli per assaltare il campo

episodes.description: Crassus and Mark Antony marched for days through Parthian territory with much infantry and few horse against innumerable Parthian cavalry; Antony saved himself, Crassus was deceived rather than overpowered.
episodes.quote: Crasso e Marc’Antonio romani corsono per il dominio de’ Parti molte giornate con pochissimi cavagli ed assai fanteria

episodes.description: At Novara nine thousand Swiss infantry attacked ten thousand cavalry and as many foot soldiers and defeated them.
episodes.quote: E’ si è veduto novemila Svizzeri a Novara, da noi di sopra allegata, andare a affrontare diecimila cavagli ed altrettanti fanti, e vincergli

episodes.description: Twenty-six thousand Swiss attacked Francis I of France near Milan, who had twenty thousand horse, forty thousand foot and a hundred guns; though beaten after two days, half of them escaped.
episodes.quote: Videsi di poi ventiseimila Svizzeri andare a trovare sopra a Milano Francesco re di Francia, che aveva seco ventimila cavagli

episodes.description: Marcus Atilius Regulus presumed to withstand not only cavalry but elephants with his infantry, trusting in its virtue even though the design failed.
episodes.quote: Presunse Marco Regolo Attilio, non solo con la fanteria sua sostenere i cavagli, ma gli elefanti

episodes.description: In the time of Filippo Visconti, Carmagnola's cavalry failed against sixteen thousand Swiss; he then dismounted his men-at-arms and destroyed the Swiss on foot.
episodes.quote: Ne’ tempi di Filippo Visconti, duca di Milano, scesono in Lombardia circa sedicimila Svizzeri

notes: Hannibal's Latin dictum and the Sora episode lack confident Livy I-X anchors; Lake Regillus matched to Livy 2.20 where cavalry dismounts.

heading_en: Acquisitions by ill-ordered republics bring ruin, not greatness
thesis: Conquests made by republics not well ordered, and not proceeding according to Roman virtue, lead to their ruin: acquiring empire without acquiring strength destroys a state.
thesis_quote: chi acquista imperio e non forze insieme, conviene che rovini

propositions.statement: It is impossible for a republic to remain quiet enjoying liberty and narrow borders: if it does not molest others it will be molested, which breeds the will and necessity to acquire.
propositions.quote: è impossibile che ad una republica riesca lo stare quieta, e godersi la sua libertà e gli pochi confini: perché, se lei non molesterà altrui, sarà molestata ella

propositions.statement: He who impoverishes himself in wars cannot acquire strength even when victorious, since he spends more than he gains from his acquisitions.
propositions.quote: Non può acquistare forze chi impoverisce nelle guerre, ancora che sia vittorioso, che ei mette più che non trae degli acquisti

propositions.statement: Cities full of delights avenge themselves on their conqueror without battle, filling him with their corrupt customs and exposing him to defeat.
propositions.quote: simili città o provincie si vendicano contro al vincitore sanza zuffa e sanza sangue; perché, riempiendogli de’ suoi tristi costumi, gli espongono a essere vinti

propositions.statement: The German free republics can live quiet and free only because of conditions peculiar to that province, found nowhere else.
propositions.quote: E se le republiche della Magna possono vivere loro in quel modo, ed hanno potuto durare un tempo, nasce da certe condizioni che sono in quel paese

episodes.description: At Novara ten thousand foot attacked and defeated ten thousand horse and as many foot on open ground, refuting Italian military opinion.
episodes.quote: diecimila fanti potessono assaltare in un piano diecimila cavagli ed altrettanti fanti, e con quelli non solamente combattere ma vincergli

episodes.description: Lucullus with few infantry routed the hundred and fifty thousand cavalry of Tigranes, among which were horsemen like modern men-at-arms.
episodes.quote: Lucullo con pochi fanti ruppe cento cinquantamila cavalli di Tigrane

episodes.description: Certain communities subject to the duke of Austria, among them Fribourg and the Swiss, rebelled, prospered, and became feared by all their neighbors.
episodes.quote: certe comunità sottoposte al duca di Austria si ribellarono da lui; tra le quali fu Filiborg, e i Svizzeri

episodes.description: The Venetians and Florentines were weaker when they held Lombardy and Tuscany than when content with the sea and six miles of borders.
episodes.quote: come hanno fatto i Viniziani ed i Fiorentini, i quali sono stati molto più deboli, quando l’uno aveva la Lombardia e l’altro la Toscana

episodes.description: The acquisition of Capua, a city of delights, corrupted first Rome's soldiers and later Hannibal's army, as Livy attests.
episodes.quote: come intervenne a Roma, prima, nello acquisto di Capova, e dipoi, a Annibale

notes: Livy quoted verbatim ('Iam tunc minime salubris militari disciplinae Capua...'); Juvenal also cited.

heading_en: The danger of auxiliary and mercenary troops
thesis: Of all kinds of soldiers, auxiliaries—troops sent, captained and paid by another power—are the most harmful, for the prince or republic using them has no authority over them.
thesis_quote: di tutte l’altre qualità de’ soldati, gli ausiliari sono i più dannosi: perché in essi quel principe o quella repubblica che gli adopera in suo aiuto, non ha autorità alcuna

propositions.statement: Auxiliary soldiers, once they have won, most often prey upon the one who hired them as much as upon the enemy, whether from their sender's malice or their own ambition.
propositions.quote: Questi tali soldati, vinto ch’eglino hanno, il più delle volte predano così colui che gli ha condotti, come colui contro a chi e’ sono condotti

propositions.statement: A prince or republic should take any other course—even a hard pact with the enemy—before bringing auxiliary troops into its state for its defense.
propositions.quote: Debbe, dunque, un principe o una republica pigliare prima ogni altro partito, che ricorrere a condurre nello stato suo per sua difesa genti ausiliarie

propositions.statement: An ambitious prince or republic can have no greater opportunity to seize a city or province than to be asked to send its armies to defend it.
propositions.quote: non può avere la maggiore occasione di occupare una città o una provincia, che essere richiesto che mandi gli eserciti suoi alla difesa di quella

episodes.description: Two Roman legions left to protect Capua grew corrupt in idleness and plotted to seize the country they had defended, a conspiracy Rome suppressed.
episodes.quote: lasciarono due legioni nel paese di Capova, che gli difendesse. Le quali legioni marcendo nell’ozio, cominciarono a dilettarsi in quello

episodes.description: The people of Rhegium were deprived of life and city by the legion the Romans had placed there as a garrison.
episodes.quote: quello de’ Regini, a’ quali fu tolto la vita e la terra da una legione che i Romani vi avevano messa in guardia

notes: Machiavelli says he found the auxiliaries example in Tito Livio and refers back to his treatment in The Prince; Rhegium episode falls outside Livy I-X.

heading_en: The first praetor the Romans sent anywhere was to Capua, four hundred years after they began making war
thesis: The Romans let the towns they did not destroy live under their own laws, without visible signs of empire; this humanity and liberality—governing unseen—greatly eased Roman expansion.
thesis_quote: e’ lasciavano quelle terre, che non disfacevano, vivere con le leggi loro, eziandio quelle che, non come compagne, ma come suggette si arrendevano loro

propositions.statement: Cities used to living free remain more content under a dominion they do not see, which does not daily remind them of their servitude.
propositions.quote: quelle città, massime che sono use a vivere libere, o consuete governarsi per sua provinciali, con altra quiete stanno contente sotto uno dominio che non veggono

propositions.statement: Men throw themselves into your lap the more you appear averse to occupying them, and fear you less for their liberty the more humane and familiar you are.
propositions.quote: gli uomini tanto più ti si gettono in grembo, quanto più tu pari alieno dallo occupargli

propositions.statement: Arms and force are not to be renounced, but should be reserved as the last resort, where and when other means do not suffice.
propositions.quote: Non è per questo che io giudichi che non si abbia adoperare l’armi e le forze; ma si debbono riservare in ultimo luogo dove e quando gli altri modi non bastino

episodes.description: The first praetor Rome ever sent out went to Capua, not from Roman ambition but at the request of the discordant Capuans themselves.
episodes.quote: il primo Pretore che fussi mandato da loro in alcun luogo, fu a Capova: il quale vi mandarono, non per loro ambizione

episodes.description: Moved by Capua's example and the same necessity, the people of Antium also asked Rome for a prefect.
episodes.quote: Da questo esemplo gli Anziati mossi, e constretti dalla medesima necessità, domandarono, ancora loro, uno Prefetto

episodes.description: The king of France always sent a French governor to occupied Genoa, except in recent times when necessity let the city govern itself under a Genoese governor, to greater security and contentment.
episodes.quote: sendo Genova stata più volte occupata da’ Franciosi, sempre quel re, eccetto che ne’ presenti tempi, vi ha mandato uno governatore francioso

episodes.description: Pistoia came voluntarily under Florentine rule because Florence treated the Pistoiese as brothers, while Pisa, Lucca and Siena resisted Florence's enmity.
episodes.quote: Ciascuno sa quanto tempo è che la città di Pistoia venne volontariamente sotto lo imperio fiorentino

notes: Livy quoted: 'quod jam non solum arma, sed iura romana pollebant' (Livy 9.20 on the Antiates).

heading_en: How often men's opinions on great matters are false
thesis: Men's opinions in great deliberations are often contrary to all truth unless formed by excellent men, who in corrupt republics are kept out of counsel in quiet times.
thesis_quote: Quanto siano false molte volte le opinioni degli uomini, lo hanno visto e veggono coloro che si truovono testimoni delle loro diliberazioni

propositions.statement: The victor rarely loses many soldiers—men die in battle, not in flight, and the fighting is brief—and the reputation and terror of victory far outweigh his losses.
propositions.quote: rade volte accade che il vincitore perda assai suoi soldati: perché de’ vincitori ne muore nella zuffa, non nella fuga

propositions.statement: In corrupt republics, especially in quiet times, excellent men are treated as enemies out of envy and ambition, so counsel follows common error or self-interested favorites.
propositions.quote: gli eccellenti uomini nelle republiche corrotte, nei tempi quieti massime, e per invidia e per altre ambiziose cagioni, sono inimicati

episodes.description: Pope Leo X was advised to stay neutral and attack whoever won between Francis I and the Swiss at Milan; after the Swiss were beaten, the papal and Spanish troops prepared to flee rather than assault the victor.
episodes.quote: sendo dopo una lunga zuffa suti superati i Svizzeri, non che le genti del Papa e di Spagna presumessero assaltare i vincitori, ma si prepararono alla fuga

episodes.description: After the Romans defeated the Latins, the praetor Numicius proclaimed through Latium that the weakened Romans could now be attacked; the peoples who believed him raised a new army and were promptly routed.
episodes.quote: il quale, vinto che i Romani ebbero i Latini, gridava per tutto il paese di Lazio, che allora era tempo assaltare i Romani debilitati

notes: Battle near Milan is Marignano (1515); Numicius corresponds to Livy's Numisius.

heading_en: The Romans avoided the middle way in judging subjects
thesis: When judging powerful cities used to freedom, one must either extinguish them or caress them; the middle way is ruinous, as Roman judgments on the Latins and Privernates show.
thesis_quote: quando si ha a giudicare cittadi potenti e che sono use a vivere libere, conviene o spegnerle o carezzarle; altrimenti, ogni giudizio è vano

propositions.statement: Government is nothing other than holding subjects so that they cannot or should not wish to harm you—either securing yourself wholly against them or benefiting them so they do not desire change.
propositions.quote: uno governo non è altro che tenere in modo i sudditi che non ti possano o debbano offendere

propositions.statement: The middle way in judgments of state must be wholly avoided, for it is harmful.
propositions.quote: E debbesi fuggire al tutto la via del mezzo, la quale è dannosa

propositions.statement: Most unhappy of all is the prince or republic reduced to being unable to accept peace or sustain war, a condition reached through bad counsels and failure to measure one's forces.
propositions.quote: è infelicissimo quello d’uno principe o d’una republica che è ridotto in termine che non può ricevere la pace o sostenere la guerra

propositions.statement: A prince who does not punish an offender so that he can offend no more is held either ignorant or cowardly.
propositions.quote: quel principe che non gastiga chi erra, in modo che non possa più errare, è tenuto o ignorante o vile

episodes.description: On Camillus's proposal the Senate judged the defeated Latins town by town, either benefiting each with citizenship and privileges or destroying it, never taking the neutral course.
episodes.quote: recatosi innanzi, terra per terra, tutti quegli ch’erano di momento, o e’ gli benificarono o e’ gli spensono

episodes.description: The Latins were conquered and utterly crushed, first by Manlius Torquatus and then by Camillus, who garrisoned all Latium and took hostages.
episodes.quote: Erano, dunque, vinti i Latini ed al tutto afflitti, prima da Manlio Torquato, e dipoi da Cammillo

episodes.description: The rebel Privernates' envoy answered the Senate boldly that only a good and faithful peace would last; the Senate made the Privernates Roman citizens, honoring the free and manly answer.
episodes.quote: deliberarono che i Privernati fossero cittadini romani, e de’ privilegi della civilità gli onorarono

episodes.description: When Arezzo and the Val di Chiana rebelled in 1502, the Florentines took the damaging middle way—banishing and condemning some Aretines, stripping honors, but leaving the city intact.
episodes.quote: A questo dovevano accostarsi i Fiorentini, quando nel 1502 si ribellò Arezzo, e tutta la Val di Chiana

episodes.description: The Samnites at the Caudine Forks rejected the old man's advice to free the Romans honorably or kill them all, and by the middle way—disarming and humiliating them—earned their own ruin.
episodes.quote: come la fu ai Sanniti quando avevano rinchiusi i Romani alle Forche Gaudine

notes: Extensive verbatim Latin from Livy 8.13 (Camillus's speech) and 8.21 (Privernates).

heading_en: Fortresses are generally far more harmful than useful
thesis: Fortresses, built either against enemies or against subjects, are unnecessary in the first case and harmful in the second; goodwill and good armies, not fortresses, preserve states.
thesis_quote: Debbesi, adunque, considerare come le fortezze si fanno o per difendersi dagl’inimici o per difendersi da’ suggetti. Nel primo caso le non sono necessarie; nel secondo, dannose

propositions.statement: Fortresses make a ruler bolder and more violent toward his subjects, breeding the very hatred that causes rebellion, while providing less security than he imagines.
propositions.quote: le ti fanno essere più audace e più violento ne’ sudditi; dipoi, non vi è quella sicurtà, dentro, che tu ti persuadi

propositions.statement: Good armies without fortresses suffice for defense; fortresses without good armies cannot defend you.
propositions.quote: i buoni eserciti sanza le fortezze sono sofficienti a difendersi; le fortezze sanza i buoni eserciti non ti possono difendere

propositions.statement: For holding one's own country a fortress is harmful; for holding acquired towns fortresses are useless—the Romans tore down walls and did not build them.
propositions.quote: per tenere la patria propria, la fortezza è dannosa; per tenere le terre che si acquistono, le fortezze sono inutili

episodes.description: Francesco Sforza, become duke of Milan, built a fortress in Milan that emboldened his heirs to oppress their subjects, so they lost the state at the first enemy assault.
episodes.quote: E se il conte Francesco Sforza, diventato duca di Milano, fu riputato savio, e nondimeno fece in Milano una fortezza

episodes.description: Guidobaldo of Urbino, expelled by Cesare Borgia and later restored, razed all the fortresses of his province, judging them harmful since the people's love protected him better.
episodes.quote: Guidubaldo duca di Urbino, figliuolo di Federigo, che fu ne’ suoi tempi tanto stimato capitano, sendo cacciato da Cesare Borgia

episodes.description: Pope Julius II, having expelled the Bentivogli, built a fortress in Bologna and let his governor abuse the people; the people rebelled and he immediately lost the fortress.
episodes.quote: Papa Iulio, cacciati i Bentivogli di Bologna fece in quella città una fortezza; e dipoi faceva assassinare quel popolo da uno suo governatore

episodes.description: Niccolò Vitelli, returned from exile to Città di Castello, at once demolished the two fortresses Pope Sixtus IV had built, trusting the people's goodwill rather than fortresses.
episodes.quote: Niccolò da Castello, padre de’ Vitelli, tornato nella sua patria donde era esule, subito disfece due fortezze

episodes.description: After Genoa's 1507 revolt Louis XII retook the city and built the supposedly impregnable Codefà fortress; in 1512 Genoa rebelled anyway, Ottaviano Fregoso starved the fortress out in sixteen months and wisely razed it.
episodes.quote: nel 1507, Genova si ribellò da Luigi XII re di Francia, il quale venne personalmente e con tutte le forze sue a riacquistarla

episodes.description: The Florentine fortresses at Pisa were handed over at the coming of King Charles, through faithlessness or fear, costing Florence the city.
episodes.quote: la virtù delle fortezze si vide nella venuta del re Carlo; al quale si dettono o per poca fede di chi le guardava o per timore di maggiore male

episodes.description: Tarentum was recovered only when Fabius Maximus was sent a year later with a whole army—which could have retaken it even without the citadel.
episodes.quote: alla ricuperazione di Taranto, in capo di uno anno, fu mandato Fabio Massimo con tutto lo esercito

episodes.description: Rebel Brescia was recovered through its citadel only because Monsieur de Foix marched the French army from Bologna and reached it in three days.
episodes.quote: sendo monsignor di Fois, capitano del re, con lo esercito a Bologna, intesa la perdita di Brescia, sanza differire ne andò a quella volta

episodes.description: A Spartan, asked by an Athenian whether the walls of Athens seemed beautiful to him, replied: yes, if they were inhabited by women.
episodes.quote: sendo domandato uno Spartano da uno Ateniese, se le mura di Atene gli parevano belle, gli rispose: - Sì, s’elle fussono abitate da donne -

episodes.description: Francesco Maria della Rovere, in recent times, left ten hostile cities behind him without concern in order to attack Urbino.
episodes.quote: come si vede fece Francesco Maria, il quale, ne’ prossimi tempi, per assaltare Urbino si lasciò indietro dieci città inimiche

institutions: citizen goodwill as foundation of rule
notes: Latin tags 'spoliatis arma supersunt' and 'furor arma ministrat' are proverbial/Virgilian, not Livy; Tarentum (Livy 27) outside Livy I-X.

heading_en: Attacking a disunited city to exploit its division is a mistaken policy
thesis: Assaulting a divided city in hopes of conquering it through its disunion is a self-defeating course, for attack unites the defenders; the wise instead keep war distant and manage the factions by the arts of peace.
thesis_quote: Credettono i Veienti, assaltando i Romani disuniti, vincergli; e quello assalto fu cagione della unione di quegli, e della rovina loro

propositions.statement: The cause of disunion in republics is usually idleness and peace; the cause of union is fear and war.
propositions.quote: la cagione della disunione delle republiche il più delle volte è l’ozio e la pace; la cagione della unione è la paura e la guerra

propositions.statement: The right method against a divided city is to win its confidence, manage its factions as arbiter until they come to arms, and then give measured support to the weaker side.
propositions.quote: Il modo è cercare di diventare confidente di quella città che è disunita; ed infino che non vengono all’armi, come arbitro maneggiarsi intra le parti

episodes.description: The Veientes and Etruscans, counting on the discord between Roman plebs and nobility, attacked and taunted Rome; the insolence united the Romans, who routed them.
episodes.quote: mandò il Senato, loro contro, Gaio Manilio e Marco Fabio; i quali avendo condotto il loro esercito propinquo allo esercito de’ Veienti

episodes.description: Divided Pistoia, with Florence favoring now one faction now the other, wore itself out and threw itself spontaneously into Florence's arms.
episodes.quote: sendo quella divisa, e favorendo i Fiorentini ora l’una parte ora l’altra, sanza carico dell’una e dell’altra la condussono in termine

episodes.description: Siena never changed its state through Florentine favors except when those favors were weak and few; strong support only united the city in defense of its regime.
episodes.quote: La città di Siena non ha mai mutato stato, col favore de’ Fiorentini, se non quando i favori sono stati deboli e pochi

episodes.description: Filippo Visconti repeatedly made war on Florence relying on its disunions and always lost, complaining that Florentine follies had cost him two million gold.
episodes.quote: Filippo Visconti, duca di Milano, più volte mosse guerra a’ Fiorentini, fondatosi sopra le disunioni loro, e sempre ne rimase perdente

notes: Machiavelli's 'Gaio Manilio' corresponds to Livy's consul Cn. Manlius (Livy 2.43-47); battle with taunts and reunion at 2.45.

heading_en: Contempt and insult breed hatred without any benefit
thesis: Threatening or insulting an enemy with words takes no strength from him but makes him more cautious and more hateful, so prudent men and commanders must abstain from and suppress such abuse.
thesis_quote: astenersi o dal minacciare o dallo ingiuriare alcuno con le parole: perché l’una cosa e l’altra non tolgono forze al nimico

propositions.statement: Threats make the enemy more cautious, insults make him hate you more and plot your harm more industriously; neither hinders his power to hurt you.
propositions.quote: l’una lo fa più cauto, l’altra gli fa avere maggiore odio contro di te, e pensare con maggiore industria di offenderti

propositions.statement: Good army commanders and governors of republics must take every remedy so that insults and taunts are used neither within the city or army nor against the enemy.
propositions.quote: Hanno dunque i buoni principi di eserciti, ed i buoni governatori di republica, a fare ogni opportuno rimedio, che queste ingiurie e rimproveri non si usino

episodes.description: The Veientes added verbal abuse to the injury of war, taunting the Romans from the palisade; the insults enraged the previously reluctant Roman soldiers, who forced the consuls to battle and defeated them.
episodes.quote: a’ quali, come è detto, non bastando il fare guerra a’ Romani, ancora con le parole gli vituperarono

episodes.description: Gabades, the Persian commander, weary of besieging Amida, was departing when the townsmen's insults from the walls so enraged him that he resumed the siege, took the city and sacked it.
episodes.quote: Gabade, capitano de’ Persi, essendo stato a campo a Amida più tempo, ed avendo deliberato, stracco dal tedio della ossidione, partirsi

episodes.description: After Valerius Corvinus quieted the sedition born of the Capua legions' conspiracy, the settlement imposed the gravest penalties on anyone who reproached the soldiers with that sedition.
episodes.quote: essendone di questa congiura nata una sedizione, la quale fu poi da Valerio Corvino quietata

episodes.description: Tiberius Gracchus, commanding slaves armed in the war against Hannibal, made it a capital offense for anyone to reproach any of them with their servitude.
episodes.quote: Tiberio Gracco, fatto, nella guerra di Annibale, capitano sopra certo numero di servi che i Romani, per carestia d’uomini, avevano armati

notes: Amida episode (Kavadh I, AD 502-503) is from Procopius, not Livy; closing Latin 'Nam facetiae asperae...' is Tacitus. Gracchus episode (Livy 23-24) outside Livy I-X.

heading_en: Prudent princes and republics should be content to win
thesis: For prudent princes and republics winning should suffice; false hope of greater victory makes men pass the mark and most often lose the certain good for an uncertain better.
thesis_quote: questa speranza, quando la entra ne’ petti degli uomini, fa loro passare il segno; e perdere, il più delle volte, quella occasione dell’avere uno bene certo, sperando di avere un meglio incerto

propositions.statement: Princes assaulted by far more powerful forces can make no greater error than refusing every accord, especially when offered, for any offer contains some part of their victory.
propositions.quote: Non possono, pertanto, i principi, che sono assaltati, fare il maggiore errore, quando lo assalto è fatto da uomini di gran lunga più potenti di loro, che recusare ogni accordo

propositions.statement: No prudent man ever risks his last stake at fortune's discretion unless compelled by necessity.
propositions.quote: mettere quella in alcuna parte a discrezione della fortuna, andandone l’ultima posta sua: la quale qualunque prudente mai arrischierà se non necessitato

propositions.statement: Men make the error of setting no limits to their hopes, and building on them without measuring themselves, they come to ruin.
propositions.quote: Ma gli uomini fanno questo errore, che non sanno porre termini alle speranze loro; ed in su quelle fondandosi, sanza misurarsi altrimenti, rovinano

episodes.description: After Cannae, Hanno counseled Carthage to use the victory wisely by making peace with Rome on honorable terms; the advice was rejected and later recognized as wise when the occasion was lost.
episodes.quote: Consigliava Annone, uno vecchio e prudente cittadino cartaginese, che si usasse questa vittoria saviamente in fare pace con i Romani

episodes.description: Tyre first refused Alexander entry, then—grown proud when he offered the very terms they had asked—killed his negotiators; Alexander stormed, destroyed and enslaved the city.
episodes.quote: sdegnato Alessandro, che una città gli volesse chiudere quelle porte che tutto il mondo gli aveva aperte, gli ributtò

episodes.description: In 1512 a Spanish army entered Florentine territory to restore the Medici; the Florentines proudly rejected the accord the starving army offered, bringing the sack of Prato and the fall of their government.
episodes.quote: Venne, nel 1512, uno esercito spagnuolo in sul dominio fiorentino per rimettere i Medici in Firenze, e taglieggiare la città

episodes.description: Hannibal, recalled to save Carthage, did not blush to ask for peace before risking his country's last stake in battle, and only fought when peace was denied.
episodes.quote: non si vergognò di domandare la pace, giudicando, se alcuno rimedio aveva la sua patria, era in quella e non nella guerra

notes: All episodes outside Livy I-X (Cannae/Zama: Livy 22-30; Tyre: Alexander historians).

heading_en: How dangerous it is not to avenge an injury, public or private
thesis: A republic or prince that leaves an injury against the public or a private person unavenged is in danger, for the gravely offended will seek revenge at any cost, even the state's ruin.
thesis_quote: se uno uomo è offeso grandemente o dal publico o dal privato e non sia vendicato secondo la soddisfazione sua; se e’ vive in una republica, cerca, ancora che con la rovina di quella, vendicarsi

propositions.statement: A ruler must never esteem a man so little as to believe that, injury being heaped upon injury, the injured man will not think of avenging himself at every danger and personal cost.
propositions.quote: mai non debbe tanto poco stimare un uomo, che ei creda, aggiugnendo ingiuria sopra ingiuria, che colui che è ingiuriato non pensi di vendicarsi con ogni suo pericolo e particulare danno

propositions.statement: Rome's ruin at the hands of the Gauls arose solely from its failure to observe justice against its own offending envoys.
propositions.quote: La quale rovina nacque ai Romani solo per la inosservanza della giustizia

episodes.description: The three Fabii, sent as envoys to the Gauls attacking Chiusi, fought against them contrary to the law of nations; instead of being surrendered or punished they were made tribunes, and the enraged Gauls took Rome except the Capitol.
episodes.quote: ei mandarono i tre Fabii oratori a’ Franciosi, che erano venuti a assaltare la Toscana, ed in particulare Chiusi

episodes.description: Pausanias, outraged by Attalus and left unavenged and his enemy honored by Philip of Macedon, turned his wrath on Philip and murdered him at his daughter's wedding.
episodes.quote: Pausania, vedendo il suo nimico onorato e non gastigato, volse tutto lo sdegno suo, non contro a quello che gli aveva fatto ingiuria, ma contro a Filippo

notes: 'contra ius gentium' quoted without naming Livy; Gallic episode spans Livy 5.35-38.

heading_en: Fortune blinds men's minds when it does not want its designs opposed
thesis: When fortune wills great outcomes, heaven blinds men so they cannot provide against events: it chooses men fit for its ends and strips of remedy those who could oppose it, as Rome's fall to the Gauls shows.
thesis_quote: si vedrà molte volte nascere cose e venire accidenti, a’ quali i cieli al tutto non hanno voluto che si provvegga

propositions.statement: When fortune wishes to bring about great ruin, it puts forward men who further that ruin, and kills or disables anyone who could withstand it.
propositions.quote: quando la voglia condurre grandi rovine, ella vi prepone uomini che aiutino quella rovina. E se alcuno fusse che vi potesse ostare, o la lo ammazza

propositions.statement: Men can second fortune but not oppose it, weave its threads but not break them; yet they should never abandon themselves, since fortune's ends are unknown.
propositions.quote: gli uomini possono secondare la fortuna e non opporsegli; possono tessere gli orditi suoi, e non rompergli. Debbono, bene, non si abbandonare mai

propositions.statement: Men who live amid great adversity or prosperity deserve less blame or praise, having been driven to ruin or greatness by the opportunity heaven gave or withheld.
propositions.quote: gli uomini che vivono ordinariamente nelle grandi avversità o prosperità, meritano manco laude o manco biasimo

episodes.description: Heaven made the Fabii envoys err and provoke the Gauls to war, had Camillus exiled to Ardea, prevented the naming of a dictator, and let Rome prepare feebly against the Gallic assault.
episodes.quote: fece prima errare quegli Fabii che andarono oratori a’ Franciosi, e, mediante l’opera loro, gli concitò a fare guerra a Roma

episodes.description: The Romans, slow to arms, met the Gauls on the river Allia ten miles from Rome with a carelessly placed camp and thin ranks, and fled almost without bloodshed.
episodes.quote: furono tanto pigri al pigliare l’arme, che a fatica furono a tempo a scontrare i Franciosi sopra il fiume di Allia, discosto a Roma dieci miglia

episodes.description: Fortune, wishing to beat Rome but not destroy it, preserved the Capitol and prepared the recovery, keeping an intact Roman army at Veii and Camillus untainted at Ardea.
episodes.quote: avendo condotto uno esercito romano intero a Veio, e Cammillo a Ardea, da potere fare grossa testa

notes: Livy named and quoted: 'Adeo obcaecat animos fortuna, cum vim suam ingruentem refringi non vult' (Livy 5.37).

heading_en: Truly powerful states buy friendships not with money but with virtue and reputation of arms
thesis: Truly powerful republics and princes acquire friendship through virtue and the reputation of their forces, never with money; Rome never bought lands or peace, while weak states that pay tribute and disarm their peoples invite ruin.
thesis_quote: mai acquistarono terre con danari, mai feciono pace con danari, ma sempre con la virtù dell’armi

propositions.statement: When neighbors, even inferiors, draw money from a state for its friendship, it is a great sign of that state's weakness; when they pay it tribute, a sign of strength.
propositions.quote: quando detti vicini, ancora che inferiori a lui, traggono da quello danari, allora è segno grande della debolezza di quello

propositions.statement: The heart and vital parts of a body, not its extremities, must be kept armed, for one lives without the extremities but dies if the heart is struck.
propositions.quote: il cuore e le parti vitali d’uno corpo si hanno a tenere armate, e non le estremità d’esso; perché sanza quelle si vive, e, offeso questo, si muore

propositions.statement: Things acquired with gold cannot be defended with iron.
propositions.quote: le cose che si acquistano con l’oro, non si sanno difendere con il ferro

propositions.statement: Where men have little virtue, fortune greatly shows its power, and states vary with its variations.
propositions.quote: dove gli uomini hanno poca virtù, la fortuna mostra assai la potenza sua

episodes.description: The Romans besieged on the Capitol were about to ransom themselves with gold from the Gauls when Camillus arrived with his army as the gold was being weighed, so that Rome was not redeemed by gold.
episodes.quote: sopra tale convenzione pesandosi di già l’oro, sopravvenne Cammillo con lo esercito suo

episodes.description: The Massilians, Aedui, Rhodians, Hiero of Syracuse, kings Eumenes and Masinissa, all neighbors of Roman empire, contributed expenses and tribute for Rome's friendship, asking only protection.
episodes.quote: i Massiliensi, gli Edui, i Rodiani, Ierone siracusano, Eumene e Massinissa regi, i quali tutti erano vicini ai confini dello imperio romano

episodes.description: Florence at the height of its reputation paid pensions to every petty lord of Romagna and to the Perugians, Castellani and other neighbors, instead of being paid for its protection.
episodes.quote: non era signorotto in Romagna che non avessi da quello provvisione; e di più la dava a’ Perugini, a’ Castellani

episodes.description: The king of France, tributary of the Swiss and of England through having disarmed his people, saw the whole province tremble when the English attacked the kingdom in 1513.
episodes.quote: quando gli Inghilesi, nel 1513, assaltarono quel regno, tremò tutta quella provincia

episodes.description: The Venetians gave the same proof a few years ago, and had their city not been girded by water its end would have been seen.
episodes.quote: De’ Viniziani si vide, pochi anni sono, la medesima pruova

episodes.description: Once under bad emperors, the Romans began buying off the Parthians, Germans and other neighboring peoples, which was the beginning of the ruin of so great an empire.
episodes.quote: cominciarono ancora essi a ricomperarsi, ora dai Parti, ora dai Germani, ora da altri popoli convicini: il che fu principio della rovina di tanto Imperio

episodes.description: After Hannibal's coming into Italy and three defeats, Rome, its heart well armed, could still sustain the enemy and win the war through the people of Rome, the Latin name, allied towns and colonies.
episodes.quote: si vide nella venuta d’Annibale in Italia, che, dopo tre rotte e dopo tante morti di capitani e di soldati, ei poterono, non solo sostenere il nimico

episodes.description: Hanno asked Hannibal's envoys after Cannae whether any Roman had sued for peace or any town of the Latin name or colonies had rebelled; when they denied both, he judged the war as whole as before.
episodes.quote: furono domandati da Annone, se del popolo romano alcuno era venuto a domandare pace, e se del nome latino e delle colonie alcuna terra si era ribellata

notes: Livy quoted as 'lo istorico' ('ut Romani auro redempti non viverent', cf. Livy 5.49) without being named.

heading_en: How dangerous it is to believe exiles
thesis: It is dangerous for those who hold states to trust men driven from their country, for both the faith and the promises of exiles are vain.
thesis_quote: Debbesi considerare, pertanto, quanto sia vana e la fede e le promesse di quelli che si truovano privi della loro patria

propositions.statement: Whenever exiles can return home by other means than yours, they will abandon you and attach themselves to others, despite any promises made.
propositions.quote: qualunque volta e’ possano per altri mezzi che per gli tuoi rientrare nella patria loro, che lasceranno te ed accosterannosi a altri

propositions.statement: So extreme is exiles' desire to return home that they naturally believe many false things and add many more by art, filling you with vain hope.
propositions.quote: egli è tanta la voglia estrema che è in loro di ritornare in casa, che ei credono naturalmente molte cose che sono false e molte a arte ne aggiungano

propositions.statement: A prince should be slow to undertake enterprises on an exile's report, for most often he is left with shame or gravest loss.
propositions.quote: Debbe, adunque, uno principe andare adagio a pigliare imprese sopra la relazione d’uno confinato, perché il più delle volte se ne resta o con vergogna o con danno gravissimo

episodes.description: Alexander of Epirus, called into Italy by Lucanian exiles who promised him the province, was killed by those same exiles when their fellow citizens promised them repatriation for the deed.
episodes.quote: Alessandro di Epiro, cognato e zio di quello, venne con gente in Italia, chiamato dagli sbanditi Lucani

episodes.description: The exiled Themistocles promised Darius so much for an attack on Greece that the king undertook it; unable to keep his promises, Themistocles poisoned himself from shame or fear of punishment.
episodes.quote: Temistocle ateniese; il quale, essendo fatto ribello, se ne fuggì in Asia a Dario; dove gli promisse tanto, quando ei volessi assaltare la Grecia

notes: Machiavelli says the example is 'addotto da Tito Livio nelle sue istorie' though outside Livy's main design; Alexander of Epirus's death is Livy 8.24.

heading_en: The ways in which the Romans seized towns
thesis: The Romans, waging war with every advantage, shunned costly sieges and took towns either by assault or by surrender, relying above all on wearing down their neighbors with defeats and raids.
thesis_quote: si guardarono da il pigliare le terre per ossidione; perché giudicavano questo modo di tanta spesa e di tanto scommodo, che superassi di gran lunga la utilità

propositions.statement: The modes by which the Romans acquired cities were either expugnation (by open force, or force mixed with fraud) or dedition (voluntary or forced surrender).
propositions.quote: I modi, adunque, con i quali gli acquistavano le città, erano o per espugnazione o per dedizione

propositions.statement: Captures by stealth and conspiracy rarely succeed because the smallest impediment ruins the design, and impediments arise easily.
propositions.quote: ogni minimo impedimento rompe il disegno, e gl’impedimenti vengano facilmente

propositions.statement: For more than four hundred and fifty years the Romans attended to wearing out their neighbors with defeats and raids, gaining reputation over them through accords.
propositions.quote: ed attesono per più che quattrocento cinquanta anni a straccare i vicini con le rotte e con le scorrerie, e pigliare, mediante gli accordi, riputazione sopra di loro

propositions.statement: With one defeat of an enemy army they acquired a kingdom in a day, while taking an obstinate city by siege consumed many years.
propositions.quote: con una rotta di esercito inimico acquistavano un regno in un giorno; e, nel pigliare per ossidione una città ostinata, consumavano molti anni

episodes.description: Scipio took New Carthage in Spain in a single all-round assault ('aggredi urbem corona').
episodes.quote: come quando Scipione prese Cartagine Nuova in Ispagna

episodes.description: The Romans took the city of the Veientes by digging a tunnel and entering the city through it.
episodes.quote: o ei facevano una cava, e per quella entravano nella città (nel quale modo presono la città de’ Veienti)
