episodes.description: Publilius Philo, besieging Palaepolis at the end of his consulate, became the first whose command was prorogued, being made the first proconsul.
episodes.quote: Il primo a chi fu prorogato lo imperio, fu a Publio Philone; il quale essendo a campo alla città di Palepoli

episodes.description: Through prolonged commands Sulla and Marius found soldiers to follow them against the public good, and Caesar was able to seize his fatherland.
episodes.quote: Per questo Silla e Mario poterono trovare soldati che contro al bene publico gli seguitassono: per questo, Cesare potette occupare la patria

heading_en: On the poverty of Cincinnatus and of many Roman citizens
thesis: The most useful ordinance of a free polity is to keep citizens poor; in Rome poverty barred no one from any rank or honor, and produced better fruits than riches.
thesis_quote: la più utile cosa che si ordini in uno vivere libero è che si mantenghino i cittadini poveri

propositions.statement: Because poverty did not block the way to any rank or honor, and virtue was sought out in whatever house it dwelt, riches were made less desirable.
propositions.quote: per la povertà non ti era impedita la via a qualunque grado ed a qualunque onore, e come e’ si andava a trovare la virtù in qualunque casa l’abitasse

propositions.statement: Poverty produces better fruits than riches: the one has honored cities, provinces, and sects, the other has ruined them.
propositions.quote: quanto migliori frutti produca la povertà che la ricchezza, e come l’una ha onorato le città, le provincie, le sétte, e l’altra le ha rovinate

episodes.description: Cincinnatus, plowing his four-iugera farm, was made dictator, freed the besieged consul Minucius from the Aequi, denied the rescued army a share of the spoils, and demoted Minucius to legate.
episodes.quote: crearono Lucio Quinzio Cincinnato, il quale allora si trovava nella sua piccola villa, la quale lavorava di sua mano

episodes.description: Marcus Regulus, with the armies in Africa, asked the Senate's leave to return and tend his farm, which his laborers were spoiling.
episodes.quote: sendo in Affrica con gli eserciti, domandò licenza al Senato per potere tornare a custodire la sua villa

episodes.description: Paulus Aemilius enriched Rome with his triumph yet kept himself poor; the silver cup he gave his son-in-law for valor was the first silver in his house.
episodes.quote: Paulo, nell’onorare chi si era portato bene nella guerra, donò a uno suo genero una tazza d’ariento

notes: Livy cited by name with 'Operae pretium est audire...' (Livy 3.26).

heading_en: How a state is ruined because of women
thesis: Women have been the cause of many ruins and divisions of states; rulers must weigh the disorders that arise from injuries over women and remedy them before the remedy comes with harm and shame.
thesis_quote: le donne sono state cagioni di molte rovine, ed hanno fatti gran danni a quegli che governano una città

propositions.statement: Absolute princes and governors of republics must not take lightly injuries involving women, but must consider and remedy the resulting disorders in time.
propositions.quote: i principi assoluti ed i governatori delle republiche non hanno a tenere poco conto di questa parte

propositions.statement: Having to call in external aid to reunite a divided city is a great beginning of imminent servitude.
propositions.quote: ebbono a mandare per soccorsi esterni: il che è uno grande principio d’una propinqua servitù

episodes.description: In Ardea a sedition between patricians and plebeians over the marriage of a rich woman came to arms; the beaten plebs called in the Volsci and the nobles called Rome, which besieged and starved the Volsci, entered Ardea, and killed the heads of the sedition.
episodes.quote: Nacque nella città d’Ardea intra i patrizi e gli plebei una sedizione per cagione d’uno parentado

episodes.description: The outrage against Lucretia took the state from the Tarquins.
episodes.quote: lo eccesso fatto contro a Lucrezia tolse lo stato ai Tarquinii

episodes.description: The outrage against Virginia deprived the decemvirs of their authority.
episodes.quote: quell’altro, fatto contro a Virginia, privò i Dieci dell’autorità loro

notes: Also cites Aristotle on injuries over women as a first cause of tyrants' ruin.

heading_en: How to unite a divided city, and why holding towns by keeping them divided is false
thesis: A divided city is cured only by killing the leaders of the tumults, or at least removing them; forced peace does not last, and the policy of holding subject towns divided is useless and harmful.
thesis_quote: non è altro, né altrimenti si debbe medicare, che ammazzare i capi de’ tumulti

propositions.statement: Of the three modes of settling a divided city - killing the leaders, removing them from the city, or forcing them to make peace - the last is the most harmful, least sure, and most useless.
propositions.quote: o ammazzargli, come feciono costoro; o rimuovergli della città; o fare loro fare pace insieme, sotto oblighi di non si offendere. Di questi tre modi, questo ultimo è più dannoso

propositions.statement: For a republic, there is no surer way to corrupt its citizens and divide itself than to govern a divided city, each faction seeking favors through corruption.
propositions.quote: non ci è il più bel modo a fare cattivi i tuoi cittadini ed a fare dividere la tua città, che avere in governo una città divisa

propositions.statement: Whether prince or republic governs, it is impossible to keep both factions of a divided town friendly, and the discontented party loses you the town in the first war.
propositions.quote: egli è impossibile che tu ti mantenga tutte a due quelle parti amiche, o principe o republica che le governi

propositions.statement: The weakness of present-day men, caused by their weak education and scant knowledge of things, makes them judge ancient judgments partly inhuman and partly impossible.
propositions.quote: la debolezza de’ presenti uomini, causata dalla debole educazione loro e dalla poca notizia delle cose, fa che si giudicano i giudicii antichi, parte inumani, parte impossibili

episodes.description: The Roman consuls reconciled the Ardeates by killing the leaders of the tumults.
episodes.quote: Per lo esemplo de’ Consoli romani che riconciliorono insieme gli Ardeati

episodes.description: Pistoia, divided between the Panciatichi and Cancellieri, came to blood and ruin; the Florentines' repeated use of forced peace bred greater scandals until they removed the faction heads by prison and confinement, which made the accord hold.
episodes.quote: Era divisa quella città, come è ancora, quindici anni sono, in Panciatichi e Cancellieri

episodes.description: In 1502, after Arezzo and the Tiber and Chiana valleys were lost to the Vitelli and Duke Valentino, the French envoy monsignor de Lant rebuked the Florentine partisans of the Marzocco, saying the king of France wants his towns united and without factions.
episodes.quote: Nel 1502, quando si perdé Arezzo, e tutto Val di Tevere e Val di Chiana, occupatoci dai Vitelli e dal duca Valentino

notes: Also quotes Biondo: while the Florentines sought to reunite Pistoia they divided themselves.

heading_en: The works of citizens must be watched, for a pious work often hides a beginning of tyranny
thesis: Works that seem pious can conceal the beginning of tyranny; a republic must open public ways to reputation and close private ones, punishing in time those who grow great by private favors.
thesis_quote: molte volte le opere che paiono pie e da non le potere ragionevolmente dannare, diventono crudeli, e per una republica sono pericolosissime, quando le non siano a buona ora corrette

propositions.statement: Reputation acquired by public ways - good counsel and good works for the common benefit - is never dangerous, but reputation acquired by private ways is most dangerous and wholly harmful.
propositions.quote: quando queste riputazioni, prese per queste vie, siano stiette e semplici, non saranno mai pericolose

propositions.statement: Private ways of gaining reputation consist in benefiting private individuals - lending money, marrying off their daughters, defending them from the magistrates - which makes men partisans and emboldens corruption of the public and the laws.
propositions.quote: Le vie private sono, faccendo beneficio a questo ed a quello altro privato, col prestargli danari, maritargli le figliuole, difenderlo dai magistrati

propositions.statement: A well-ordered republic must open the ways to those seeking favor publicly and close them to those seeking it privately, as Rome did with triumphs, accusations, and the dictator.
propositions.quote: Debbe, pertanto, una republica bene ordinata aprire le vie come è detto, a chi cerca favori per vie publiche, e chiuderle a chi li cerca per vie private

episodes.description: During a famine, the rich Spurius Maelius privately provisioned grain to feed the plebs and won such a following that the Senate, fearing his liberality, created a dictator against him and put him to death.
episodes.quote: prese animo uno Spurio Melio, essendo assai ricco, secondo quegli tempi, di fare provisione privatamente di frumento

heading_en: The sins of peoples are born from their princes
thesis: Princes should not complain of the sins of the peoples they govern, for such sins necessarily arise either from the prince's negligence or from his being stained with like errors.
thesis_quote: tali peccati conviene che naschino o per la sua negligenza, o per essere lui macchiato di simili errori

propositions.statement: The crimes of the Romagna arose from the wickedness of its princes, not from the wicked nature of its men as those princes claimed.
propositions.quote: Il che nasceva dalla tristitia di quelli principi; non dalla natura trista degli uomini, come loro dicevano

propositions.statement: Those princes made laws and prohibitions, were themselves the first to cause their non-observance, and punished only out of greed for the fines, impoverishing the peoples without correcting them.
propositions.quote: e’ facevano leggi, e proibivono alcuna azione; dipoi erano i primi che davano cagione della inosservanza di esse

propositions.statement: The multitude is always like its ruler, as Livy's judgment on Timasitheus affirms.
propositions.quote: Timasitheus multitudinem religione implevit, quae semper regenti est similis

episodes.description: The Romagna, before Pope Alexander VI extinguished its lords, exemplified the most wicked life, with killings and great rapines on every slight occasion, caused by its poor princes who wanted to live rich.
episodes.quote: La Romagna, innanzi che in quella fussono spenti da papa Alessandro VI quegli signori che la comandavano, era un esempio d’ogni sceleratissima vita

episodes.description: Roman legates carrying the gift from the Veientine spoils to Apollo were seized by corsairs of Lipari, but their prince Timasitheus, learning of the sacred gift, filled the multitude with religious awe and released the legates with all their goods.
episodes.quote: portando i Legati romani il dono della preda de’ Veienti ad Apolline, furono presi da’ corsali di Lipari in Sicilia

notes: Closes with Lorenzo de' Medici's couplet confirming that what the lord does, many then do.

heading_en: A citizen who would do good by his authority must first extinguish envy; and how to order a city's defense
thesis: A citizen wishing to do good for his fatherland by his own authority must first extinguish envy, which otherwise denies him the necessary authority; and a city's defense must be ordered, never tumultuary.
thesis_quote: quanto utile e’ possa fare alla sua patria, quando, mediante la sua bontà e virtù, egli ha spenta la invidia

propositions.statement: Envy is extinguished either by a grave and difficult accident in which all, seeing themselves perishing, run voluntarily to obey the man whose virtue can free them, or by the death of one's competitors.
propositions.quote: O per qualche accidente forte e difficile, dove ciascuno, veggendosi perire, posposta ogni ambizione, corre volontariamente ad ubbidire a colui che crede che con la sua virtù lo possa liberare

propositions.statement: Against enviers raised in a corrupt city there is no remedy but their death; if fortune does not kill them off, the virtuous man must find a way to remove them before doing anything.
propositions.quote: A vincere questa invidia non ci è altro rimedio che la morte di coloro che l’hanno

propositions.statement: No defense is more dangerous or more useless than one made tumultuously and without order; a multitude must never take arms except under a fixed order and mode.
propositions.quote: non è la più pericolosa né la più inutile difesa, che quella che si fa tumultuariamente e sanza ordine

episodes.description: Facing war with all Tuscany, the Latins, Hernici, and Volsci, Camillus' fellow consular tribunes voluntarily ceded him supreme command, and he enrolled three armies and assigned his colleagues to supply, the Senate, and the city's guard.
episodes.quote: trovandosi Cammillo tribuno di potestà consolare, pensò che si potesse fare sanza creare il Dittatore, quando gli altri Tribuni suoi collegi volessono cedergli la somma dello imperio

episodes.description: Moses, to make his laws and orders go forward, was forced to kill countless men who opposed his designs moved by nothing but envy.
episodes.quote: vedrà Moisè essere stato forzato, a volere che le sue leggi e che i suoi ordini andassero innanzi, ad ammazzare infiniti uomini

episodes.description: Friar Girolamo Savonarola knew this necessity but could not overcome envy, lacking the authority to do so and being misunderstood by followers who had it; his sermons are full of invectives against 'the wise of the world'.
episodes.quote: Questa necessità conosceva benissimo frate Girolamo Savonerola

episodes.description: Piero Soderini, gonfalonier of Florence, believed that time, goodness, and fortune would extinguish envy without violence, not knowing that time cannot be waited for, goodness does not suffice, fortune varies, and malignity finds no placating gift; he was ruined.
episodes.quote: Quell’altro credeva, col tempo, con la bontà, con la fortuna sua, col benificare alcuno, spegnere questa invidia

notes: Livy cited by name with 'Nec quicquam de maiestate sua detractum...' (Livy 6.6).

heading_en: Strong republics and excellent men keep the same spirit and dignity in every fortune
thesis: Great men and strong republics remain the same in every fortune, neither insolent in prosperity nor abject in adversity; this constancy comes from education and good arms, whose lack made the Venetians vary with fortune.
thesis_quote: gli uomini grandi sono sempre in ogni fortuna quelli medesimi; e se la varia, ora con esaltarli, ora con opprimerli, quegli non variano, ma tengono sempre lo animo fermo

propositions.statement: Weak men grow vain and intoxicated in good fortune, attributing their success to a virtue they never knew, and so become insufferable and odious, then vile and abject when fortune turns.
propositions.quote: invaniscono ed inebriano nella buona fortuna, attribuendo tutto il bene che gli hanno a quella virtù che non conobbono mai

propositions.statement: Becoming insolent in good fortune and abject in bad arises from one's mode of proceeding and the education in which one was reared.
propositions.quote: questo diventare insolente nella buona fortuna ed abietto nella cattiva, nasce dal modo del procedere tuo, e dalla educazione nella quale ti se’ nutrito

propositions.statement: The foundation of all states is a good military; where this is lacking there can be neither good laws nor any other good thing.
propositions.quote: il fondamento di tutti gli stati è la buona milizia; e come, dove non è questa, non possono essere né leggi buone né alcuna altra cosa buona

propositions.statement: A military cannot be good unless it is exercised, and it cannot be exercised unless composed of one's own subjects, since one cannot always be at war.
propositions.quote: la milizia non puoté essere buona, se la non è esercitata; e come la non si può esercitare, se la non è composta di tuoi sudditi

episodes.description: After the defeat at Cannae, the Romans never grew abject: they sent out armies, refused to ransom their prisoners against their orders, sought no peace from Hannibal or Carthage, and armed their old men and slaves.
episodes.quote: per quella rotta, ancora che gravissima per essere stata la terza, non invilirono mai; e mandarono fuori eserciti; non vollono riscattare i loro prigioni

episodes.description: After defeating Antiochus, Scipio offered him no other terms than those proposed before the victory, saying the Romans neither lose spirit if beaten nor grow insolent if they win.
episodes.quote: mandando Antioco oratori a Scipione, a chiedere accordo, avanti che fussono venuti alla giornata

episodes.description: The Venetians, insolent in prosperity, after a half-defeat at Vailà by the king of France lost their whole state by rebellion and abjectly surrendered parts to the pope and Spain, sending tribute embassies to the emperor and submissive letters to the pope.
episodes.quote: come la buona sorte gli abbandonò e ch’egli ebbono una mezza rotta a Vailà, dal re di Francia, perderono non solamente tutto lo stato loro per ribellione

episodes.description: Camillus, marching against the Tuscans, found his soldiers dismayed at the enemy's numbers, walked the camp talking the opinion out of their heads, and said each would do what he had learned and was accustomed to do.
episodes.quote: Era Cammillo andato, come di sopra dicemo, con lo esercito contro ai Toscani; ed avendo i suoi soldati veduto la grandezza dello esercito de’ nimici

notes: Livy referenced as 'il nostro istorico' with Latin quotes 'Nec mihi dictatura animos fecit, nec exilium ademit' and 'Quod quisque didicit, aut consuevit, faciet'.

heading_en: The modes some have used to disrupt a peace
thesis: To make a people or prince wholly abandon thought of an accord, there is no truer or more stable remedy than to have them commit some grave crime against the party with whom peace is to be prevented.
thesis_quote: non ci è altro rimedio più vero né più stabile, che farli usare qualche grave sceleratezza contro a colui con il quale tu non vuoi che l’accordo si faccia

propositions.statement: Fear of the punishment seemingly deserved for the crime committed will always keep them far from any accord.
propositions.quote: perché sempre lo terrà discosto quella paura di quella pena che a lui parrà per lo errore commesso avere meritata

episodes.description: When the rebellious colonies Circei and Velitrae considered sending envoys to Rome after the Latins' defeat, the authors of the rebellion, fearing punishment, incited the multitude to arm and raid the Roman borders to cut off all talk of peace.
episodes.quote: Essendosi ribellate dal Popolo romano Circei e Velitre, due sue colonie, sotto speranza di essere difese dai Latini

episodes.description: After the First Punic War, the rebel mercenaries under Matho and Spendius tortured and killed the Carthaginian envoy and all Carthaginian prisoners, decreeing the same for any Carthaginians taken, to bind their soldiers against ever hoping for peace with Carthage.
episodes.quote: fatti, di loro, due capi, Mato e Spendio, occuparono molte terre ai Cartaginesi, e molte ne saccheggiarono

notes: Machiavelli names the Carthaginian envoy Asdrubale; Polybius' account (1.79-80) names Gesco.

heading_en: To win a battle it is necessary to make the army confident in itself and in its captain
thesis: To win a battle the army must be made confident in itself and in its captain, which the Romans secured through religion and the auspices; but such confidence avails nothing unless accompanied by virtue.
thesis_quote: A volere che uno esercito vinca la giornata, è necessario farlo confidente, in modo che creda dovere in ogni modo vincere

propositions.statement: Confidence and order can arise only among soldiers who are born and have lived together.
propositions.quote: Né può nascere questa confidenza o questo ordine, se non in quelli soldati che sono nati e vissuti insieme

propositions.statement: The captain maintains the majesty of his rank by punishing errors, not wearying the soldiers in vain, keeping promises to them, and showing the way to victory as easy.
propositions.quote: e sempre la manterrà, quando gli punisca degli errori, e non gli affatichi invano; osservi loro le promesse; mostri facile la via del vincere

propositions.statement: The Romans made their armies take up this confidence by way of religion, using auguries and auspices in creating consuls, levying, marching, and giving battle.
propositions.quote: Usavano i Romani di fare pigliare agli eserciti loro questa confidenza per via di religione

propositions.statement: True virtue, good order, and the assurance of many victories cannot be extinguished by things of little moment, nor does any vain thing frighten them.
propositions.quote: una vera virtù, un ordine buono, una sicurtà presa da tante vittorie, non si può con cose di poco momento spegnere

episodes.description: The Romans punished any consul or captain who fought against the auspices, as they punished Claudius Pulcher.
episodes.quote: E quando alcuno Consolo, o altro loro capitano, avesse combattuto, contro agli auspicii, lo arebbero punito; come ei punirono Claudio Pulcro

episodes.description: Livy puts in the mouth of Appius Claudius, complaining of the tribunes' insolence, the speech that the neglect of auspices and religion, though small things, was what made the republic great.
episodes.quote: si pruova più certo per le parole che Livio usa nella bocca di Appio Claudio

episodes.description: The Praenestines encamped at the river Allia, where the Gauls had beaten the Romans, to hearten their own soldiers and dismay the Romans by the fortune of the place; the dictator told his master of horse to trust in arms and spirit and charge the center.
episodes.quote: I Prenestini, avendo contro ai Romani fuori el loro esercito, se n’andarono ad alloggiare in sul fiume d’Allia

episodes.description: When the two Manlii, consuls against the Volsci, rashly sent part of the camp to plunder and both parts found themselves besieged, it was the steady virtue of the soldiers themselves, not the consuls' prudence, that saved them.
episodes.quote: essendo due Manlii consoli contro a’ Volsci, per avere mandato temerariamente parte del campo a predare

episodes.description: Fabius, newly entered into Tuscany with his army, told his soldiers before battle that he could tell them further grounds of certain victory were it not dangerous to reveal them, a device to make the army confident in a new country against new enemies.
episodes.quote: uno termine usato da Fabio, sendo entrato di nuovo con lo esercito in Toscana, per farlo confidente

notes: Four Latin Livy quotes cited verbatim; chapter-map matches them to Livy 6.41, 6.29, 6.30.

heading_en: What fame or opinion makes the people begin to favor a citizen; whether the people distributes offices more prudently than a prince
thesis: The people, judging by fame, associates, and notable deeds, does not found its first grants of office badly, and when counseled errs less than a prince; a citizen should win favor by some notable deed.
thesis_quote: il popolo, quando ei comincia a dare uno grado a uno suo cittadino, fondandosi sopra quelle tre cagioni soprascritte, non si fonda male

propositions.statement: Initial public reputation derives from ancestry, from one's associates, or from an extraordinary and notable action, and the last gives the greatest reputation.
propositions.quote: E di tutte a tre queste cose che danno nel principio buona riputazione ad uno, nessuna la dà maggiore che questa ultima

propositions.statement: Notable actions are necessary not only to begin a reputation but must be renewed to maintain and increase it.
propositions.quote: Né solamente sono necessarie simili cose per cominciare a darsi la riputazione ma sono ancora necessarie per mantenerla ed accrescerla

propositions.statement: When peoples can be counseled as princes are, they err less than princes in electing magistrates.
propositions.quote: quando ei possono essere consigliati come i principi, errano meno de’ principi

episodes.description: Titus Manlius (later Torquatus) saved his father Lucius Manlius from an accusation by the tribune Marcus Pomponius, winning such favor that he was made tribune of the legions.
episodes.quote: Tito Manlio, che fu poi detto Torquato, salvò Lucio Manlio suo padre da una accusa

episodes.description: Manlius fought the Gaul in single combat and took from the corpse the gold collar that gave him the name Torquatus.
episodes.quote: combatté con quel Francioso, e, morto, gli trasse quella collana d’oro che gli dette il nome di Torquato

episodes.description: In mature age Manlius executed his own son for fighting without permission even though he had beaten the enemy.
episodes.quote: ammazzò il figliuolo per avere combattuto sanza licenza, ancora ch’egli avesse superato il nimico

episodes.description: The elder Scipio won early fame by defending his father at the Ticinus and, after Cannae, forcing young Romans at sword-point to swear not to abandon Italy.
episodes.quote: A Scipione maggiore non arrecarono tanta gloria tutti i suoi trionfi, quanto gli dette lo avere, ancora giovinetto, in sul Tesino, difeso il padre

episodes.description: Fabius Maximus spoke to the people against electing Titus Otacilius consul in the Second Punic War, showing his insufficiency and turning the vote elsewhere.
episodes.quote: l’orazione di Fabio Massimo, la quale ei fece al popolo nella seconda guerra punica

notes: Scipio and Otacilius episodes fall in the Second Punic War, outside Livy I-X, hence null refs.

heading_en: The dangers of making oneself head in counseling a new enterprise, the more so the more extraordinary it is
thesis: Since men judge counsels by their outcome, whoever makes himself head of an important deliberation bears all the blame for failure; the only remedy is to advise moderately and without passion.
thesis_quote: giudicando gli uomini le cose dal fine, tutto il male che ne risulta s’imputa allo autore del consiglio

propositions.statement: Counselors of republics and princes face a dilemma: if they do not counsel what seems useful they fail their office, if they do they risk life and position.
propositions.quote: se non consigliano le cose che paiono loro utili, o per la città o per il principe, sanza rispetto, e’ mancano dell’ufficio loro

propositions.statement: The only escape is to take positions moderately, adopt no enterprise as one's own, and state one's opinion without passion.
propositions.quote: pigliare le cose moderatamente, e non ne prendere alcuna per sua impresa, e dire la opinione sua sanza passione

propositions.statement: Keeping silent is no refuge, for it is useless to the state and the silent soon become suspect and still face danger.
propositions.quote: consigliandogli che tacessono, e che non dicessono l’opinione loro, sarebbe cosa inutile alla republica o al loro principe, e non fuggirebbono il pericolo

episodes.description: Sultan Selim (the Grand Turk), advised by a pasha to march against the Sophy of Persia, lost much of his army to famine and plague and killed the author of the counsel.
episodes.quote: irato contro allo autore del consiglio, lo ammazzò

episodes.description: Roman citizens who championed the plebeian consulship were endangered when the first plebeian consul to take the field was routed.
episodes.quote: Fecionsi capi alcuni cittadini romani, che si facesse in Roma il Consule plebeio

episodes.description: Perseus of Macedon, fleeing after his defeat by Paulus Aemilius, killed with his own hand a friend who only then recounted his errors.
episodes.quote: Traditore, sì che tu hai indugiato a dirmelo ora che io non ho più rimedio!

notes: Selim episode is contemporary (1510s) but Ottoman-Persian, not Italian; bucketed under contemporary-italy as the only 1400s-1500s period available.

heading_en: Why the French have been and are still judged in fights more than men at the beginning and less than women afterwards
thesis: Natural fury unsupported by order fails; only where ordered virtu governs fury with method and timing does an army keep its spirit to the end.
thesis_quote: dove la virtù ordinata usa il furore suo con i modi e co’ tempi, né difficultà veruna lo invilisce, né li fa mancare l’animo

propositions.statement: There are three kinds of armies: one with fury and order (the Roman), one with fury without order (the French), and one with neither.
propositions.quote: e’ sono di tre ragioni eserciti: l’uno dove è furore ed ordine; perché dall’ordine nasce il furore e la virtù

propositions.statement: Armies of fury without order fail when the first onset does not win, since their fury is not sustained by ordered virtu.
propositions.quote: non riuscendo loro con il primo impeto vincere, e non essendo sostenuto da una virtù ordinata quello loro furore

propositions.statement: The Italian armies of our times, having neither natural fury nor acquired order, are entirely useless.
propositions.quote: come sono gli eserciti italiani de’ nostri tempi, i quali sono al tutto inutili

episodes.description: The Gaul who challenged any Roman to combat near the river Anio, and the subsequent duel with Titus Manlius.
episodes.quote: La ferocità di quello Francioso che provocava qualunque Romano, appresso al fiume Aniene, a combattere seco

episodes.description: Papirius Cursor, wishing to punish Fabius, master of horse, described in Livy's words what an undisciplined soldiery would be.
episodes.quote: le parole di Papirio Cursore, quando ei voleva punire Fabio, Maestro de’ cavalli

heading_en: Whether skirmishes before the pitched battle are necessary, and how to know a new enemy if one wishes to avoid them
thesis: Next to every good lies an adjoining evil: light skirmishes to acquaint soldiers with a reputed new enemy are nearly necessary, yet risk the opposite effect, so they must be ventured only with great advantage.
thesis_quote: sempre propinquo al bene sia qualche male, il quale con quel bene sì facilmente nasca che pare impossibile potere mancare dell’uno, volendo l’altro

propositions.statement: A good captain must entirely avoid any action of small moment that can produce bad effects on his army.
propositions.quote: uno buono capitano debbe fuggire, al tutto, di operare alcuna cosa, che, essendo di poco momento, possa fare cattivi effetti nel suo esercito

propositions.statement: Against a new and reputed enemy, captains are compelled to let their soldiers test him in light skirmishes before the pitched battle, to remove the terror of his fame.
propositions.quote: sono necessitati, prima che venghino alla giornata, fare provare, con leggieri zuffe, ai loro soldati, tali nimici

propositions.statement: Small fights should be permitted only with very great advantage and hope of certain victory, and one should not defend posts or towns one cannot truly defend.
propositions.quote: si debbe guardare dalle zuffe piccole, e non le permettere se non con grandissimo vantaggio, e con speranza di certa vittoria

episodes.description: The duel of Manlius and the Gaul decided, per Livy, the outcome of the whole war, the Gallic army fleeing its camp into the Tiburtine land and Campania.
episodes.quote: Tanti ea dimicatio ad universi belli eventum momenti fuit, ut Gallorum exercitus, relictis trepide Castris, in Tiburtem agrum

episodes.description: Valerius Corvinus, sent against the Samnites, new enemies, had his Romans fight some light skirmishes so that a new war and new enemy should not terrify them.
episodes.quote: Valerio fece fare ai Romani con i Sanniti alcune leggieri zuffe

episodes.description: Philip of Macedon, father of Perseus, when attacked by the Romans abandoned and wasted lands of his he judged he could not defend.
episodes.quote: Filippo di Macedonia, padre di Perse, uomo militare e di gran condizione ne’ tempi suoi, essendo assaltato dai Romani

episodes.description: After the rout of Cannae the Romans denied aid to many dependents and subjects, telling them to defend themselves as best they could.
episodes.quote: dopo la rotta di Canne le cose loro erano afflitte, negarono a molti loro raccomandati e sudditi gli aiuti

episodes.description: Marius repeatedly encamped where the Cimbri had to pass so his soldiers could accustom their eyes to that disordered multitude and grow eager for battle.
episodes.quote: più che una volta collocò lo esercito suo in luogo donde i Cimbri con lo esercito loro dovessono passare

notes: Philip V, Cannae, and Marius episodes lie outside Livy I-X.

heading_en: How a captain should be made in whom his army can confide
thesis: A captain earns his army's confidence by deeds and personal example rather than words, for it is not titles that make men illustrious but men who make titles illustrious.
thesis_quote: non i titoli illustrono gli uomini, ma gli uomini i titoli

propositions.statement: A captain must offer his soldiers deeds, not words, giving them example as well as discipline from his own person.
propositions.quote: Facta mea, non dicta, vos, milites, sequi volo; nec disciplinam modo, sed exemplum etiam a me petere

propositions.statement: If an unaccustomed enemy frightens a veteran army, every enemy frightens a new army all the more, so greater industry is needed in commanding it.
propositions.quote: se lo inusitato inimico allo esercito vecchio dà terrore, tanto maggiormente lo debbe dare ogni inimico a uno esercito nuovo

propositions.statement: A prince who abounds in men but lacks soldiers should blame his own laziness and imprudence, not the cowardice of the men.
propositions.quote: quel principe, che abbonda di uomini e manca di soldati, debbe solamente, non della viltà degli uomini, ma della sua pigrizia e poca prudenza, dolersi

episodes.description: Valerius Corvinus, facing the Samnites as new enemies, reassured his soldiers with light skirmishes and a speech on his own deeds and example.
episodes.quote: Era, come di sopra dicemo, Valerio Corvino con lo esercito contro ai Sanniti, nuovi nimici del Popolo romano

episodes.description: Gracchus the Roman and Epaminondas the Theban, by months of mock battles and training in obedience, defeated veteran armies with new ones.
episodes.quote: come fece quel Gracco romano, ed Epaminonda tebano, de’ quali altra volta abbiamo parlato, che con eserciti nuovi vinsono eserciti veterani

notes: Second episode pairs a Roman (Sempronius Gracchus, Second Punic War) with the Theban Epaminondas; bucketed ancient-other.

heading_en: That a captain must be a knower of sites
thesis: Knowledge of sites and countries, general and particular, is necessary to a captain and is acquired above all through the practice of hunting.
thesis_quote: Intra le altre cose che sono necessarie a uno capitano di eserciti, è la cognizione de’ siti e de’ paesi

propositions.statement: This particular knowledge of country is acquired more through hunting than by any other exercise.
propositions.quote: Questa pratica, ovvero questa particulare cognizione, si acquista più mediante le cacce che per veruno altro esercizio

propositions.statement: Since every country has some conformity with others, mastering one region lets one easily comprehend new countries.
propositions.quote: ogni paese ed ogni membro di quelli hanno insieme qualche conformità, in modo che dalla cognizione d’uno facilmente si passa alla cognizione dell’altro

episodes.description: Xenophon's Cyrus, attacking the king of Armenia, reminded his men that the operation was nothing but one of the hunts they had often made with him.
episodes.quote: Senofonte, nella vita di Ciro, mostra che, andando Ciro ad assaltare il re d’Armenia

episodes.description: Publius Decius, military tribune under consul Cornelius against the Samnites, spotted the hill that saved the trapped Roman army and reconnoitered the escape routes in a soldier's cloak.
episodes.quote: essendo Tribuno de’ soldati nello esercito che Cornelio consolo conduceva contro ai Sanniti

heading_en: That to use fraud in managing war is a glorious thing
thesis: Though fraud is detestable in every other action, in managing war it is laudable and glorious, provided it is not the fraud that breaks given faith and pacts.
thesis_quote: Ancora che lo usare la fraude in ogni azione sia detestabile, nondimanco nel maneggiare la guerra è cosa laudabile e gloriosa

propositions.statement: Fraud that breaks given faith and made pacts may win you state and kingdom but never glory.
propositions.quote: io non intendo quella fraude essere gloriosa, che ti fa rompere la fede data ed i patti fatti

propositions.statement: The middle way, which neither gains friends nor removes enemies, was always pernicious in affairs of state.
propositions.quote: La quale via fu sempre perniziosa nelle cose di stato come di sopra in altro luogo si discorse

episodes.description: Hannibal feigned flight at Lake Trasimene to enclose the consul and the Roman army, and lit the horns of his herd to escape Fabius Maximus.
episodes.quote: quella di Annibale quando in sul lago di Perugia simulò la fuga per rinchiudere il Consolo e lo esercito romano

episodes.description: Pontius, captain of the Samnites, used soldiers disguised as shepherds to lure the Roman army into the Caudine Forks, but rejected his father's counsel against the middle way.
episodes.quote: questa che usò Ponzio capitano dei Sanniti, per rinchiudere lo esercito romano dentro alle Forche Caudine

notes: Hannibal episodes (Trasimene, escape from Fabius) are outside Livy I-X.

heading_en: That the fatherland should be defended with ignominy or with glory, and is well defended either way
thesis: When the entire safety of the fatherland is being deliberated, no consideration of just or unjust, merciful or cruel, praiseworthy or ignominious should intervene; whatever saves its life and liberty must be followed.
thesis_quote: dove si dilibera al tutto della salute della patria, non vi debbe cadere alcuna considerazione né di giusto né d’ingiusto, né di piatoso né di crudele

propositions.statement: The fatherland is well defended in whatever way it is defended, whether with ignominy or with glory.
propositions.quote: la patria è bene difesa in qualunque modo la si difende, o con ignominia o con gloria

episodes.description: Lucius Lentulus, Roman legate, advised accepting the ignominious Caudine terms, since saving the army saved Rome, which could in time cancel the ignominy.
episodes.quote: Lucio Lentolo, legato romano, disse che non gli pareva che fosse da fuggire qualunque partito per salvare la patria

episodes.description: The French in words and deeds hold that their king can suffer no shame in any deliberation, since winning or losing, all are the king's affairs.
episodes.quote: nessuna voce odono più impazientemente che quella che dicesse: - Il tale partito è ignominioso per il re

heading_en: That promises exacted by force ought not to be observed
thesis: Forced promises touching the public will always be broken when the force is removed, and without shame to the breaker.
thesis_quote: sempre le promesse forzate che riguardano il publico, quando e’ manchi la forza, si romperanno, e fia sanza vergogna di chi le rompe

propositions.statement: Glory can be acquired in any action: ordinarily in victory, and in loss by showing the loss was not your fault or by some virtuous act that cancels it.
propositions.quote: in qualunque azione si può acquistare gloria, perché nella vittoria si acquista ordinariamente; nella perdita si acquista o col mostrare tale perdita non essere venuta per tua colpa

propositions.statement: Among princes even unforced promises go unobserved when the causes that made them promise are gone.
propositions.quote: non si osservano ancora tutte le altre promesse, quando e’ mancano le cagioni che le feciono promettere

episodes.description: Spurius Postumius argued in the Senate that the Caudine peace did not bind the Roman people and had himself delivered prisoner to the Samnites, who refused him, returning more glorious in defeat than Pontius in victory.
episodes.quote: il primo che in Senato disse che la pace fatta a Caudio non si doveva osservare, fu il consolo Spurio Postumio

notes: Closes with a cross-reference to Machiavelli's own treatise De Principe on whether princes should keep promises.

heading_en: That men born in a province observe through all times almost the same nature
thesis: Whoever wants to see what is to be should consider what has been, for all things of the world in every time have their counterpart in ancient times, being worked by men with the same passions.
thesis_quote: chi vuole vedere quello che ha a essere, consideri quello che è stato; perché tutte le cose del mondo, in ogni tempo, hanno il proprio riscontro con gli antichi tempi

propositions.statement: Because all things are done by men who have always had the same passions, they must of necessity produce the same effects.
propositions.quote: essendo quelle operate dagli uomini, che hanno ed ebbono sempre le medesime passioni, conviene di necessità che le sortischino il medesimo effetto

propositions.statement: Works are more virtuous in one province than another according to the form of education by which those peoples took their mode of life.
propositions.quote: secondo la forma della educazione nella quale quegli popoli hanno preso il modo del vivere loro

propositions.statement: Had Florence read and known the ancient customs of the barbarians, it would not have been deceived by them this and many other times.
propositions.quote: se Firenze non fosse stata o costretta dalla necessità o vinta dalla passione, ed avesse letti e conosciuti gli antichi costumi de’ barbari, non sarebbe stata né questa né molte altre volte ingannata da loro

episodes.description: King Charles VIII repeatedly took Florentine money promising to return the fortresses of Pisa and never returned them.
episodes.quote: quante volte si dette danari a re Carlo VIII, ed elli prometteva rendere le fortezze di Pisa, e non mai le rendé

episodes.description: The emperor, paid two hundred thousand ducats by Florence to attack the Visconti of Milan, turned back at Verona without doing anything.
episodes.quote: giunto che fu a Verona, se ne tornò indietro sanza operare alcuna cosa

episodes.description: The ancient Tuscans, oppressed by Rome, paid the Gauls of cisalpine Italy to join arms with them, but the Gauls took the money and refused to fight.
episodes.quote: i Franciosi, presi i danari, non vollono dipoi pigliare l’armi per loro

heading_en: That one often obtains with impetus and audacity what one would never obtain by ordinary means
thesis: A prince who desires something from another should give him no space to deliberate, making him see the necessity of instant decision, since refusal or delay would bring sudden and dangerous indignation.
thesis_quote: E’ si ottiene con l’impeto e con l’audacia molte volte quello che con modi ordinarii non si otterrebbe mai

propositions.statement: When occasion permits, one should deny the other party time to deliberate and force a quick decision by making refusal or delay seem to breed sudden and dangerous indignation.
propositions.quote: debbe, se la occasione lo patisce, non gli dare spazio a diliberarsi, e fare in modo che vegga la necessità della presta diliberazione

episodes.description: The Samnites, unable to face the Romans in the field, marched their whole army into Tuscany and by its presence and their words induced the Tuscans to take up arms, saying peace was heavier for the enslaved than war for the free.
episodes.quote: diliberarono lasciare guardate le terre in Sannio e di passare con tutto lo esercito loro in Toscana

episodes.description: Pope Julius II, marching suddenly from Rome toward Bologna against the Bentivogli, left the French king and the Venetians no time to deliberate, obtaining aid from one and neutrality from the other.
episodes.quote: partitosi da Roma con quelle tante genti ch’ei poté raccozzare, ne andò verso Bologna

episodes.description: Monsieur de Foix, moving his troops at once toward Brescia through Mantuan territory, demanded and obtained the keys of the pass from the marquis of Mantua, who was given no time to deliberate.
episodes.quote: a un tratto mosse le sue genti per quella via, ed al marchese significò gli mandasse le chiavi di quel passo

heading_en: Which is the better course in battle, to withstand the enemies' charge and then counterattack, or to assault them with fury from the first
thesis: Of the two consuls' methods at the battle with the Samnites and Tuscans, Fabius's way of sustaining the enemy's first ardor and reserving his impetus for the end proved safer and more worthy of imitation than Decius's furious assault.
thesis_quote: si vede che il modo del procedere di Fabio è più sicuro e più imitabile

propositions.statement: A slow assault is more useful, reserving one's impetus for the end when the enemy has lost his first ardor for combat.
propositions.quote: giudicando lo assalto lento essere più utile, riserbando l’impeto suo nello ultimo, quando il nimico avesse perduto el primo ardore del combattere

episodes.description: Consul Decius attacked with all impetus, exhausted his troops, and in imitation of his father sacrificed himself for the legions, while Fabius, sustaining the attack and committing his reserved forces late, won a most happy victory.
episodes.quote: ad imitazione del padre sacrificò sé stesso per le romane legioni

notes: Battle of Sentinum; Decius's devotio is Livy 10.28.

heading_en: Whence it arises that a family in a city keeps the same customs for a time
thesis: The persistent differences of character between families in the same city cannot come from blood alone, which marriages vary, but must come from the differing education of one family and another.
thesis_quote: non possono nascere solamente dal sangue, perché conviene che varii mediante la diversità de’ matrimonii; ma è necessario venga dalla diversa educazione

propositions.statement: What a youth hears praised or blamed from tender years necessarily makes an impression that regulates his conduct through all his life.
propositions.quote: gl’importa assai che un giovanetto da’ teneri anni cominci a sentire dire bene o male d’una cosa

propositions.statement: In Rome the Manlii were hard and obstinate, the Publicolae benign lovers of the people, the Appii ambitious enemies of the plebs, each family keeping its own qualities.
propositions.quote: i Manlii essere stati duri ed ostinati, i Publicoli uomini benigni ed amatori del popolo, gli Appii ambiziosi e nimici della Plebe

episodes.description: An Appius made censor refused to lay down the magistracy after eighteen months as the law required, claiming five years under the original law, against the will of the people and most of the Senate, drawing the oration of the tribune Publius Sempronius against him.
episodes.quote: essendo uno di loro fatto Censore ed avendo il suo collega alla fine de’ diciotto mesi, come ne disponeva la legge, diposto il magistrato

heading_en: That a good citizen for love of his fatherland ought to forget private injuries
thesis: For the public benefit a good citizen must set aside private hatreds, as Fabius did in nominating his enemy Papirius Cursor dictator out of love of country.
thesis_quote: Il che Fabio fece, mosso dalla carità della patria; ancora che col tacere e con molti altri modi facesse segno che tale nominazione gli premesse

propositions.statement: All who seek to be held good citizens should take example from Fabius, who put aside private hatred for the public benefit.
propositions.quote: Dal quale debbono pigliare esemplo tutti quelli che cercano di essere tenuti buoni cittadini

episodes.description: With consul Marcius wounded fighting the Samnites, the Senate sent envoys to beg Fabius, consul in Tuscany, to set aside private hatred and name his enemy Papirius Cursor dictator, which he did.
episodes.quote: Era Marzio consolo con lo esercito contro ai Sanniti, ed essendo stato in una zuffa ferito

heading_en: When one sees an enemy commit a great error, one should believe there is deceit beneath it
thesis: A captain should never trust an error the enemy is evidently seen to make, for there will always be fraud beneath it, men not plausibly being so incautious.
thesis_quote: uno capitano di eserciti non debbe prestare fede ad uno errore che evidentemente si vegga fare al nimico: perché sempre vi sarà sotto fraude

propositions.statement: An evident enemy blunder always conceals fraud, since it is not reasonable that men should be so incautious.
propositions.quote: sempre vi sarà sotto fraude, non sendo ragionevole che gli uomini siano tanto incauti

propositions.statement: The desire to win often so blinds men's minds that they see nothing but what seems to favor them.
propositions.quote: spesso il disiderio del vincere acceca gli animi degli uomini, che non veggono altro che quello pare facci per loro

episodes.description: The Tuscans set an ambush near the Roman camp and sent soldiers dressed as shepherds with herds in sight of the army, but the legate Fulvius, suspecting such presumption, uncovered the fraud.
episodes.quote: mandarono alcuni soldati con veste di pastori con assai armento, e li feciono venire alla vista dello esercito romano

episodes.description: The Gauls, finding Rome's gates open and unguarded after Allia, stood a whole day and night without entering, fearing fraud.
episodes.quote: trovando le porte aperte e sanza guardia, stettero tutto quel giorno e la notte sanza entrarvi, temendo di fraude

episodes.description: In 1508 the Pisan Alfonso Del Mutolo promised to betray a gate of Pisa to the Florentines but negotiated openly, and his double treachery cost the blinded Florentines several leaders at the Lucca gate.
episodes.quote: Alfonso Del Mutolo, cittadino pisano, si trovava prigione de’ Fiorentini

notes: Shepherd-disguise episode against legate Fulvius not pinned to a specific Livy chapter with confidence; left null.

heading_en: That a republic, to keep itself free, needs new provisions every day; and for what merits Quintus Fabius was called Maximus
thesis: Every day in a great city accidents arise that need the physician, and the graver they are the wiser the physician must be; disorders touching the state ruin the city unless a prudent man corrects them.
thesis_quote: È di necessità, come altre volte si è detto, che ciascuno dì in una città grande naschino accidenti che abbiano bisogno del medico

propositions.statement: Decimating by lot, when all deserve punishment, makes the punished blame fortune and the unpunished fear the next time, so they guard against erring.
propositions.quote: ammazzandone la decima parte a sorte, quando tutti lo meritano, chi è punito si duole della sorte, chi non è punito ha paura che un’altra volta non tocchi a lui

propositions.statement: Punishing part of an erring multitude and leaving part unpunished wrongs the punished and emboldens the unpunished to err again.
propositions.quote: punirne parte, e parte lasciarne impuniti, si farebbe torto a quegli che si punissono, e gli impuniti arebbono animo di errare un’altra volta

propositions.statement: Unlike other disorders, those touching the state leave no time: if not corrected by a prudent man they ruin the city.
propositions.quote: non si ha già tempo in quelli che riguardano lo stato, i quali, se non sono da uno prudente corretti, rovinano la città

episodes.description: The conspiracy of the Roman matrons, so many of whom had poisoned or prepared poison for their husbands, was discovered and punished.
episodes.quote: e’ parve che tutte le donne romane avessono congiurato contro ai loro mariti di ammazzargli

episodes.description: The Bacchanalian conspiracy, discovered during the Macedonian war, had already entangled many thousands of men and women.
episodes.quote: quella congiura de’ Baccanali, che si scoprì nel tempo della guerra macedonica

episodes.description: The soldiers who fought unhappily at Cannae were confined to Sicily under extraordinary conditions, forbidden to lodge in towns and made to eat standing.
episodes.quote: come intervenne a quelli soldati che infelicemente avevano combattuto a Canne; i quali confinò in Sicilia

episodes.description: Quintus Fabius as censor confined the new citizens, whose votes were altering the government, into four tribes, a remedy so welcome he merited the name Maximus.
episodes.quote: messe tutte queste genti nuove, da chi dipendeva questo disordine, sotto quattro Tribù

notes: Bacchanalia (Livy 39) and Cannae legions episodes fall outside Livy I-X.
